anchors.summary: Africa's grain and tax revenue pass to a hostile kingdom with a fleet, and the western empire loses the richest provinces it had left along with the means to pay armies.

anchors.title: Saxon and Anglian war bands settle in Britain
anchors.summary: Federate troops hired against northern raiders send for their families instead, and over the next century lowland Britain changes its language, its law, and its fields.

anchors.title: Moche lords rule Peru's north coast
anchors.summary: Canals off the Andes water desert valleys for adobe pyramids, gilded copper regalia, and modeled pottery that records war, ritual, and sacrifice in exact detail.

anchors.title: Attila is checked on the Catalaunian Plains
anchors.summary: A Roman and Visigothic coalition fights the Hunnic confederation to a standstill in Gaul; Attila dies two years later and his empire is divided and lost by his sons.

anchors.title: The Council of Chalcedon splits the eastern churches
anchors.summary: A formula of two natures in one person is imposed as orthodoxy, and the Egyptian, Syrian, and Armenian churches that reject it separate for good.

anchors.title: Skandagupta turns back the Hunas
anchors.summary: The Gupta emperor beats off Alchon Hun invaders and repairs the Sudarshana reservoir, but the wars strain the treasury and his gold coinage loses fineness.

anchors.title: The western Roman empire ends
anchors.summary: Odoacer retires the last western emperor; the office lapses with less noise than its idea will make for the next millennium.

anchors.title: The king of Wa petitions the Song court
anchors.summary: A memorial from Japan asks a Chinese emperor to confirm titles over lands his ancestors subdued; the Yamato court now treats with its neighbors as a state.

anchors.title: The Northern Wei institute the equal-field system
anchors.summary: The state assigns cultivators fixed allotments in return for grain, cloth, and labor, a land and tax model the Sui and Tang inherit and Korea and Japan copy.

anchors.title: Theodoric takes Italy
anchors.summary: An Ostrogothic king kills Odoacer at Ravenna and rules from there with the Roman senate, taxes, and civil service left intact beneath a Gothic army.

anchors.title: Clovis is baptized at Reims
anchors.summary: The Frankish king takes Nicene Christianity rather than the Arianism of his Gothic rivals, and wins the Gallo-Roman bishops as allies in the conquest of Gaul.

anchors.title: Aryabhata completes the Aryabhatiya
anchors.summary: A verse handbook of astronomy supplies a sine table, a close value for pi, and the argument that the nightly turning of the stars is the earth rotating on its axis.

anchors.title: The Babylonian Talmud reaches its final form
anchors.summary: Generations of debate in the academies of Sura and Pumbedita are edited into one commentary that becomes the working law and the curriculum of Jewish communities everywhere.

anchors.title: The Franks defeat the Visigoths at Vouille
anchors.summary: Clovis kills Alaric II and takes Aquitaine; Visigothic power falls back on Spain, and nearly all of Gaul answers to one Frankish house.

anchors.title: Aksum invades Himyar
anchors.summary: An Ethiopian expedition crosses the Red Sea, overthrows the Himyarite king Dhu Nuwas after his killing of Christians at Najran, and rules Yemen through a viceroy.

anchors.title: Benedict founds Monte Cassino
anchors.summary: A rule balancing prayer, study, and manual work gives western monasteries a workable constitution, and gives their scriptoria a standing reason to copy books.

anchors.title: Khosrow I reforms the Sasanian state
anchors.summary: A fixed land tax assessed on survey replaces variable levies, and a salaried cavalry drawn from the lesser nobility loosens the great houses' hold on the army.

anchors.title: The Corpus Juris Civilis is completed
anchors.summary: Justinian's commissioners condense a thousand years of Roman jurisprudence into a code, a digest, and a textbook; medieval Europe rediscovers it and builds its law schools on it.

anchors.title: Justinian's armies invade Ostrogothic Italy
anchors.summary: The campaign to recover the west runs twenty years, and its sieges, famines, and requisitions leave Italy's cities, aqueducts, and senate in worse shape than Gothic rule did.

anchors.title: A dust veil dims the sun for a year
anchors.summary: Volcanic ash thins the sunlight from Ireland to China; chroniclers describe a sun without rays, and the cold summers that follow bring failed harvests and hunger.

anchors.title: Hagia Sophia is consecrated
anchors.summary: Justinian's dome outbuilds every church in Christendom and every engineer's caution.

anchors.title: Buddhism reaches the Yamato court
anchors.summary: A Baekje king sends images and sutras to Japan, and the quarrel over whether to accept them decides which clans will run the state for the next century.

anchors.title: Khosrow sacks Antioch
anchors.summary: Persian troops burn the Roman east's greatest city and deport its people to a new town built for them near Ctesiphon; Justinian buys the peace back with annual gold.

anchors.title: The Justinianic plague arrives
anchors.summary: Yersinia pestis reaches the Mediterranean and returns in waves for two centuries, resetting labor and land.

anchors.title: Chenla supplants Funan on the lower Mekong
anchors.summary: Inland Khmer rulers absorb the delta kingdom that had brokered the sea trade, and power in the region shifts upriver toward the plain that will later hold Angkor.

anchors.title: The Gupta empire dissolves
anchors.summary: Hun invasions, revolts by feudatories, and a debased gold coinage leave north India a mosaic of regional kingdoms, and no single power holds the Ganges plain for centuries.

anchors.title: Tikal is defeated and enters its hiatus
anchors.summary: Caracol and its Calakmul allies break the dominant city of the central lowlands, and Tikal raises no dated monuments for the next 130 years.

anchors.title: Columba founds the monastery on Iona
anchors.summary: An Irish exile settles a house on a Hebridean island that will send missionaries into Pictland and Northumbria and copy manuscripts for three centuries.

anchors.title: The Lombards invade Italy
anchors.summary: Alboin's people cross into a peninsula exhausted by the Gothic war and take the inland north; Italy stays split between Lombard duchies and Byzantine coasts for two centuries.

anchors.title: The Sui reunify China
anchors.summary: Sui armies cross the Yangtze and take the Chen capital, ending nearly three centuries of division and restoring one administration over north and south.

anchors.title: Gregory the Great becomes pope
anchors.summary: A former city prefect turned monk feeds Rome from church estates and negotiates with the Lombards himself, turning the bishopric into a governing power in central Italy.

anchors.title: Augustine lands in Kent
anchors.summary: A mission sent from Rome converts King Aethelberht and founds the see of Canterbury, tying the English church to the papacy rather than to the Irish houses.

anchors.title: The Grand Canal links China's rivers
anchors.summary: Grain from the Yangtze can now feed armies on the Yellow River; unification acquires plumbing.

anchors.title: Harsha builds a north Indian empire
anchors.summary: From Kanauj a young king assembles the last wide north Indian realm for centuries, held together by his own person and breaking apart almost at once when he dies without an heir.

anchors.title: Muhammad begins to preach at Mecca
anchors.summary: Muslim tradition dates the first revelation to this year, the seed of a scripture, a law, and a community that will outgrow Arabia within a single lifetime.

anchors.title: The Tang dynasty is founded
anchors.summary: Li Yuan takes the throne as the Sui collapse, inheriting their canals and codes and beginning three centuries in which Chinese law, script, and city plans are copied across East Asia.

anchors.title: The hijra to Medina
anchors.summary: Muhammad's community leaves Mecca; within a century its successors govern from Spain to Sind.

anchors.title: A king is buried in a ship at Sutton Hoo
anchors.summary: The East Anglian grave holds Byzantine silver, Frankish gold coin, and a helmet in a Swedish style, evidence that post-Roman Britain still traded across the North Sea.

anchors.title: Brahmagupta gives rules for zero
anchors.summary: The Brahmasphutasiddhanta treats zero and negative quantities as numbers with arithmetic of their own, closing the place-value system that later reaches Europe as the digits.

anchors.title: Mecca submits to Muhammad
anchors.summary: The city that expelled him opens its gates, the idols around the Kaaba are destroyed, and the sanctuary is refounded as the center of a single cult.

anchors.title: Muhammad dies at Medina
anchors.summary: He leaves no agreed successor, and the question of who may lead the community opens both the caliphate and a dispute that divides Islam permanently.

anchors.title: Arab armies win at Yarmouk
anchors.summary: Byzantine Syria falls in a week of battle; the Roman and Persian duopoly of the Near East ends.

anchors.title: Arab armies take Egypt and found Fustat
anchors.summary: Amr ibn al-As rules from a new garrison town beside the Nile rather than from Alexandria, and Egypt's grain and taxes pass from Constantinople to the caliphate.

anchors.title: Xuanzang returns from India
anchors.summary: Sixteen years of travel bring hundreds of Sanskrit manuscripts to Chang'an, and the translation bureau built to handle them fixes Buddhist vocabulary in Chinese.

anchors.title: The Quran is fixed in one codex
anchors.summary: Uthman's committee settles a single consonantal text and orders rival copies burned, giving the new religion a stable scripture within twenty years of its founder's death.

anchors.title: The Sasanian empire ends
anchors.summary: Yazdegerd III is killed near Merv while in flight, ending four centuries of Persian imperial rule whose bureaucracy and court manners the caliphate then absorbs.

anchors.title: The Umayyads rule from Damascus
anchors.summary: Ali is murdered at Kufa and Muawiya moves the caliphate to Syria, converting a contested elective leadership into a dynasty run from a former Roman province.

anchors.title: The Synod of Whitby chooses Rome
anchors.summary: Northumbria adopts the Roman reckoning of Easter and the Roman tonsure, binding English Christianity to the continent rather than to the Irish houses that converted it.

anchors.title: Silla unifies the Korean peninsula
anchors.summary: Goguryeo falls to a Tang and Silla alliance, and within eight years Silla has driven out its Tang ally and rules the peninsula as one kingdom.

anchors.title: Kairouan is founded in Ifriqiya
anchors.summary: A garrison town set inland from a hostile coast anchors Arab rule in North Africa and becomes the base from which armies and scholars move west.

anchors.title: Yijing finds a thousand monks at Srivijaya
anchors.summary: The Chinese pilgrim breaks his voyage at Palembang and reports a Sanskrit school worth years of study, evidence of a Sumatran state living off the straits it controls.

anchors.title: Greek fire burns an Arab fleet
anchors.summary: A siphon-projected incendiary that water will not quench destroys ships besieging Constantinople, and the formula is kept a state secret closely enough to be lost.

anchors.title: Husayn is killed at Karbala
anchors.summary: The Prophet's grandson and his small company are surrounded and killed by an Umayyad force, and the killing becomes the founding grief of Shia Islam.

anchors.title: Byzantium recognizes a Bulgar state
anchors.summary: Constantinople agrees to pay tribute to Asparukh, conceding a permanent power on the lower Danube that will absorb its Slavic subjects and outlast every attempt to remove it.

anchors.title: Pakal is entombed at Palenque
anchors.summary: The king who ruled Palenque for sixty-eight years is laid in a vaulted crypt beneath a stepped pyramid whose inscriptions argue his dynasty's descent at length.

anchors.title: Wu Zetian takes the imperial title
anchors.summary: The only woman to rule China in her own name declares a new dynasty, promotes examination graduates over the old aristocratic clans, and holds power for fifteen years.

anchors.title: The Dome of the Rock is completed
anchors.summary: An octagonal shrine on Jerusalem's temple platform, inscribed with verses denying the Trinity, states the new faith's claim in the architectural language of its rivals.

anchors.title: Arabic coin and register replace Greek
anchors.summary: Abd al-Malik strikes dinars bearing only words and moves the tax registers out of Greek and Persian into Arabic, welding scattered conquests into one fiscal state.

anchors.title: Classic Maya cities flourish
anchors.summary: Dynasts at Tikal and Calakmul war and ally, while scribes keep the hemisphere's only full writing system.

anchors.title: Camel caravans cross the Sahara regularly
anchors.summary: Desert crossings become routine commerce, and West African gold moving north against Saharan salt moving south begins to fund states at both ends of the sand.

anchors.title: Chang'an is the world's largest city
anchors.summary: Tang China's capital hosts perhaps a million people and every religion on the Silk Road.

anchors.title: Tiwanaku dominates the Titicaca basin
anchors.summary: Raised-field farming on the cold altiplano supports a stone capital whose gateways and distant colonies set the visual language of the southern Andes.

anchors.title: Japan's capital settles at Nara
anchors.summary: The court builds a grid city on the Chang'an model and governs through the ritsuryo codes, ending the custom of moving the capital at every succession.

anchors.title: The Visigothic kingdom falls
anchors.summary: An Arab and Berber force crossing at Gibraltar destroys the Visigothic army, and within seven years most of Iberia is under Muslim rule.

anchors.title: Arab armies take Sindh
anchors.summary: Muhammad ibn Qasim's campaign puts the lower Indus under the caliphate, opening the first durable channel between Indian learning and Arabic scholarship.

anchors.title: The Arab siege of Constantinople fails
anchors.summary: A year of blockade ends in hunger, disease, and a burned fleet; the empire survives, and the frontier between caliphate and Byzantium settles at the Taurus mountains.

anchors.title: Iconoclasm begins in Byzantium
anchors.summary: Leo III orders holy images taken down, and a century of argument over what may be depicted splits the church, the army, and the empire's relations with Rome.

anchors.title: Bede completes his English history
anchors.summary: A Northumbrian monk writes the first connected account of the English and dates its events from the Incarnation, a counting convention that spreads across Latin Europe.

anchors.title: Battle of Tours
anchors.summary: A Frankish shield wall checks a raiding army from al-Andalus; the Carolingians bank the prestige.

anchors.title: The Abbasid revolution overthrows the Umayyads
anchors.summary: An army raised in Khurasan destroys the Umayyad caliphate at the Zab, and power passes from Syrian Arab clans to a cosmopolitan court facing east toward Iran.

anchors.title: The Pala dynasty is founded in Bengal
anchors.summary: Bengali chiefs raise Gopala to kingship to end a long anarchy, beginning four centuries of Pala rule and the last great royal patronage of Indian Buddhism.

anchors.title: Wari administers a highland network
anchors.summary: Walled compounds built to one standard plan appear hundreds of kilometers apart in the Andes, evidence of a Peruvian state governing distant provinces directly.

anchors.title: Pepin deposes the last Merovingian
anchors.summary: The mayor of the palace takes the Frankish crown with papal assent and is anointed like a biblical king, tying Carolingian legitimacy to the church that performs it.

anchors.title: Tang and Abbasid armies meet at Talas
anchors.summary: A defeat in the Talas valley ends Tang expansion westward and leaves Central Asia to Muslim rule; captured artisans are said to have carried papermaking with them.

anchors.title: The An Lushan rebellion begins
anchors.summary: A frontier general marches on both Tang capitals, and eight years of war leave the dynasty without its western garrisons, its tax registers, or any trust in provincial armies.

anchors.title: An Umayyad survivor takes Cordoba
anchors.summary: Abd al-Rahman escapes the Abbasid purge, reaches Iberia, and founds an emirate that answers to no caliph, splitting the Muslim world into rival centers of authority.

anchors.title: Sijilmasa anchors the gold road
anchors.summary: A caravan town at the desert's northern edge becomes the terminus where West African gold is exchanged for salt, cloth, and Mediterranean coin.

anchors.title: Baghdad is founded
anchors.summary: The Abbasids build a round city at the crossroads of the world's trade and begin paying for translations of everything.

anchors.title: A million printed charms are finished in Japan
anchors.summary: An imperial vow is discharged with a million block-printed dharani slips housed in small wooden pagodas, the earliest printing to survive anywhere in quantity.

anchors.title: Charlemagne begins the Saxon wars
anchors.summary: Thirty years of campaigning annex Saxony to the Frankish realm, and conversion is enforced by capital law, mass deportation, and the execution of prisoners.

anchors.title: Indian astronomy reaches Baghdad
anchors.summary: A Sanskrit treatise brought to al-Mansur's court is rendered into Arabic as the Sindhind, carrying decimal place-value numerals into the mathematics of the caliphate.

anchors.title: Caroline minuscule standardizes the page
anchors.summary: Frankish scriptoria settle on a rounded hand with spaces between words and capitals reserved for hierarchy, and copying, correction, and silent reading all get faster.

anchors.title: Raiders sack Lindisfarne
anchors.summary: Ships from Scandinavia plunder an undefended island monastery off Northumbria, the first recorded Viking raid on Britain and the opening of two centuries of seaborne attack.

anchors.title: The Japanese court moves to Heian-kyo
anchors.summary: A new capital laid out away from Nara's monasteries opens four centuries in which aristocratic culture, not the ritsuryo state, does most of the governing.

anchors.title: Baghdad gets a paper mill
anchors.summary: Paper made from rag pulp begins replacing papyrus and parchment in the caliphate's offices, and the cost of a written page falls far enough to support a book trade.

anchors.title: Charlemagne is crowned emperor
anchors.summary: A pope revives the western imperial title on Christmas day; church and crown are entangled for a millennium.

anchors.title: Southern Maya cities begin to fail
anchors.summary: Southern lowland courts stop raising dated monuments and their cities empty over the following century, under some combination of drought, warfare, and failing royal legitimacy.

anchors.title: Jayavarman II founds the Khmer empire
anchors.summary: A ceremony on Mount Kulen declares one Khmer sovereign free of Javanese overlordship, beginning the state that will build Angkor and its irrigation works.

anchors.title: Krum destroys a Byzantine army at Pliska
anchors.summary: The Bulgar khan traps the emperor Nikephoros in a mountain pass and kills him, the first Byzantine emperor to die in battle in more than four centuries.

anchors.title: Al-Khwarizmi writes the algebra
anchors.summary: A short book on restoration and balancing sets out general procedures for solving equations, giving later mathematics both the subject and the word algebra.

anchors.title: Borobudur is completed in Java
anchors.summary: A mountain of carved stone terraces makes Southeast Asia's wealth and Buddhism visible for miles.

anchors.title: Aghlabid forces land in Sicily
anchors.summary: An army from Ifriqiya comes ashore at Mazara, beginning a conquest that takes most of a century and keeps Sicily under Muslim rule until the Norman wars of the eleventh.

anchors.title: Arabic geographers describe Ghana
anchors.summary: Writers in the caliphate record a kingdom south of the desert whose ruler is rich in gold, the first written notice of the West African states the caravans reached.

anchors.title: The House of Wisdom flourishes
anchors.summary: Baghdad's scholars translate Greek, Persian, and Indian science into Arabic, and improve it.

anchors.title: The caliph imposes a doctrinal test
anchors.summary: Al-Mamun requires judges and scholars to affirm that the Quran was created, and the campaign is abandoned within twenty years, leaving religious authority with the scholars.

anchors.title: The caliphs move to Samarra
anchors.summary: A new capital is built upriver to quarter a guard of Turkish slave soldiers away from Baghdad's population, and within a generation that guard makes and unmakes caliphs.

anchors.title: The Uyghur khaganate collapses
anchors.summary: Kyrgyz horsemen burn the Uyghur capital on the Orkhon, and the survivors migrate south and west into the Tarim oases, where they settle and take up farming.

anchors.title: The Tibetan empire fragments
anchors.summary: The killing of Langdarma ends central rule from Lhasa, and the plateau breaks into local lordships after two centuries of pressing on Tang China and the Silk Road oases.

anchors.title: Byzantium restores the icons
anchors.summary: A synod under the empress Theodora ends the image dispute for good, and the painted icon becomes fixed and defended doctrine in the eastern church.

anchors.title: The Treaty of Verdun divides the Franks
anchors.summary: Charlemagne's grandsons split the empire into western, middle, and eastern kingdoms, drawing the rough outline that France and Germany keep thereafter.

anchors.title: Wuzong dissolves China's monasteries
anchors.summary: Thousands of Buddhist houses are closed, their bronze melted into coin and their lands taxed, and hundreds of thousands of monks and nuns are returned to the lay registers.

anchors.title: Vijayalaya takes Thanjavur
anchors.summary: A minor chief seizes the city from the Muttaraiyar and revives the Chola line, from which grows the dynasty that will dominate southern India and raid across the Bay of Bengal.

anchors.title: Fujiwara no Yoshifusa governs for a child emperor
anchors.summary: Yoshifusa rules in the name of his eight-year-old grandson, and for two centuries Japanese emperors reign while Fujiwara in-laws govern.

anchors.title: Al-Qarawiyyin is endowed at Fez
anchors.summary: Fatima al-Fihri founds a mosque in Fez whose teaching circles harden into one of the longest continuously running centers of learning anywhere.

anchors.title: Turkish guards kill the caliph at Samarra
anchors.summary: Al-Mutawakkil is murdered by his own soldiers, and for nine years the guard makes and unmakes caliphs while the provinces stop remitting taxes.

anchors.title: Rurik takes power among the northern Rus
anchors.summary: The Primary Chronicle dates the Norse warlord's rule at Novgorod to this year, the start of a river polity that sends furs, wax, and captives south and silver north.

anchors.title: The Great Heathen Army lands in England
anchors.summary: Scandinavian raiding turns to conquest and settlement; the North Sea becomes one rough economy.

anchors.title: The Zanj rebellion begins in southern Iraq
anchors.summary: Enslaved East African laborers draining the salt marshes near Basra revolt, and their war holds the region for fourteen years before the caliphate crushes it.

anchors.title: Alfred becomes king of Wessex
anchors.summary: Alfred inherits the last English kingdom still fighting the Danes, buys time with tribute, and spends his reign rebuilding its army and walling its towns.

anchors.title: Alfred defeats Guthrum at Edington
anchors.summary: Wessex wins the battle that halts the Danish conquest of England; Guthrum accepts baptism and a negotiated border, and the Danelaw is fixed by treaty.

anchors.title: Vikings besiege Paris
anchors.summary: A Danish fleet blockades the Seine for a year, and the count who holds the bridges gains a reputation the emperor loses by paying the raiders to leave.

anchors.title: Yasovarman founds Yasodharapura at Angkor
anchors.summary: The Khmer king moves his capital to the plain north of the Tonle Sap and builds the reservoirs whose rice surplus will feed Angkor for five centuries.

anchors.title: Japan ends its embassies to China
anchors.summary: Sugawara no Michizane cancels the mission to a collapsing Tang court, and Japanese letters turn inward toward the kana script and a court style of their own.

anchors.title: The Magyars occupy the Carpathian basin
anchors.summary: Magyar clans cross the passes and settle the middle Danube, driving a permanent non-Slavic wedge between the Slavs of the north and those of the south.

anchors.title: Chaco canyon's great houses expand
anchors.summary: Builders at Pueblo Bonito raise multi-story masonry blocks aligned to the sun and moon, anchoring roads and outliers that reach settlements days away.

anchors.title: The Tang dynasty falls
anchors.summary: A warlord deposes the last Tang emperor, and China breaks into five northern dynasties and ten southern states for half a century.

anchors.title: Cluny is founded free of lay control
anchors.summary: William of Aquitaine gives the new abbey to Rome rather than to his heirs, and the reform network that grows from it will press the whole church to shake off lay lords.

anchors.title: Rollo is granted the land that becomes Normandy
anchors.summary: Charles the Simple buys off a Viking war band with the lower Seine, converting raiders into vassals whose descendants will take England, Sicily, and Antioch.

anchors.title: Abaoji proclaims a Khitan empire
anchors.summary: The Khitan chief takes an imperial title on the steppe frontier and rules herders and farmers through two separate administrations, a template later conquest dynasties copy.

anchors.title: Wang Geon founds Goryeo
anchors.summary: A merchant-general takes the throne in the north and within two decades absorbs Silla and Later Baekje, giving Korea the dynasty and the name outsiders still use.

anchors.title: Abd al-Rahman III declares the caliphate of Cordoba
anchors.summary: The Umayyad ruler of al-Andalus claims the caliphal title against Baghdad and Cairo, and Cordoba spends a century as western Europe's largest and richest city.

anchors.title: Iceland's Althing first meets at Thingvellir
anchors.summary: Settlers with no king agree to gather each summer to recite and amend the law, creating an assembly whose name Iceland's parliament still carries.

anchors.title: Ngo Quyen breaks the Southern Han at Bach Dang
anchors.summary: Iron-tipped stakes planted in the tidal river wreck the invading fleet, ending a thousand years of Chinese rule over the Red River delta.

anchors.title: The Buyids take Baghdad
anchors.summary: Daylamite soldiers occupy the capital and keep the Abbasid caliph as a figurehead, splitting religious authority from the power to tax and command.

anchors.title: Tula becomes central Mexico's leading city
anchors.summary: The Toltec center draws tribute and craftsmen into the vacuum Teotihuacan left, and later Mexica rulers will claim descent from its kings to legitimize their own.

anchors.title: Otto I destroys the Magyar army at Lechfeld
anchors.summary: The defeat ends fifty years of Magyar raiding into Germany and Italy, and the survivors turn from plunder to settled kingship on the Danube.

anchors.title: The Song dynasty is founded
anchors.summary: China reunifies under a dynasty that will govern with examinations, paper money, and the world's largest iron industry.

anchors.title: Otto I is crowned emperor in Rome
anchors.summary: The German king revives the western imperial title, binding his successors to Italian campaigns and to a papacy that can crown them or refuse.

anchors.title: Harald Bluetooth converts the Danes
anchors.summary: The Danish king accepts baptism and proclaims it on a carved stone at Jelling, pulling Scandinavia into Latin Christendom's bishops, tithes, and parchment.

anchors.title: The Fatimids take Egypt and found Cairo
anchors.summary: An Ismaili army out of Tunisia seizes the Nile valley and lays out a palace city beside Fustat, shifting the Islamic world's commercial weight away from Baghdad.

anchors.title: The Song emperor examines candidates himself
anchors.summary: Taizu adds a palace examination he presides over in person, so successful candidates owe their rank to the throne rather than to the official who marked them.

anchors.title: Rajaraja I takes the Chola throne
anchors.summary: The new king turns a Tamil river kingdom into a naval power, taking tribute from Sri Lanka and the Maldives and cutting his revenue surveys into temple walls.

anchors.title: Hugh Capet is elected king of the Franks
anchors.summary: The magnates pass over the Carolingians for a count whose lands sit around Paris, and his male line holds the French crown for the next three centuries.

anchors.title: Vladimir baptizes Kiev
anchors.summary: The prince takes Byzantine Christianity and a Byzantine bride, committing the eastern Slavs to Constantinople's liturgy, alphabet, and law rather than Rome's.

anchors.title: England pays the first great Danegeld
anchors.summary: After defeat at Maldon the English buy off a Viking fleet with ten thousand pounds of silver, and the land tax raised to pay it becomes the crown's most reliable revenue.

anchors.title: Voyagers settle the Hawaiian islands
anchors.summary: Canoes out of central East Polynesia carry taro, pigs, and dogs to the archipelago at the voyaging world's northern edge, where isolation soon breeds its own chiefdoms.

anchors.title: Stephen is crowned king of Hungary
anchors.summary: The Magyar prince takes a crown sent from Rome, founds bishoprics and counties, and turns a confederation of horse clans into a Latin Christian kingdom.

anchors.title: Stone towns rise along the Swahili coast
anchors.summary: Shanga, Manda, and their neighbors trade mangrove poles, ivory, and gold for Chinese porcelain and Persian glass, and coral-stone mosques replace timber ones.

anchors.title: Norse from Greenland camp in Newfoundland
anchors.summary: A short-lived settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows marks the first known European landfall in the Americas, abandoned within a few years and remembered only in sagas.

anchors.title: The Wari and Tiwanaku states unravel
anchors.summary: The Andes lose both of their large highland polities within a century, and their terraces and roads pass to smaller rival groups until the Inca reassemble them.

anchors.title: Song and Liao settle at Chanyuan
anchors.summary: The Song agree to send the Khitan silver and silk every year in exchange for a fixed border, and the two courts keep the peace for over a century.

anchors.title: The Tale of Genji circulates at the Heian court
anchors.summary: Murasaki Shikibu's long prose narrative of court life is read among the empress's women, written in the kana script that men of the time dismissed as women's writing.

anchors.title: The Brihadisvara temple is finished at Thanjavur
anchors.summary: Rajaraja crowns his capital with a granite tower over sixty meters high and endows it with villages, dancers, and accountants, all listed on its walls.

anchors.title: Ferdowsi completes the Shahnameh
anchors.summary: Some fifty thousand couplets of Persian kings and heroes, composed in a Persian that keeps Arabic loanwords out, give the language a canon that survives later conquests.

anchors.title: The Ly move the Vietnamese capital to Thang Long
anchors.summary: The new dynasty settles at the site of modern Hanoi, builds river dikes and a Confucian college, and holds the delta against Song and Khmer attacks for two centuries.

anchors.title: Cnut takes the English throne
anchors.summary: A Danish king rules England, then Denmark and Norway, running a North Sea empire on English silver and English clerks until it dissolves at his death.

anchors.title: Basil II completes the conquest of Bulgaria
anchors.summary: Byzantium annexes the Balkan kingdom after decades of war and restores its frontier to the Danube, the empire's furthest reach before a century of retreat.

anchors.title: Ibn al-Haytham completes the Book of Optics
anchors.summary: Working in Cairo, he shows that light travels to the eye rather than out of it and settles each claim by experiment, a method Latin readers will study for centuries.

anchors.title: Sichuan's paper notes become state money
anchors.summary: The Song take over the deposit certificates merchants had been passing in Chengdu and issue them officially, the first government paper currency anywhere.

anchors.title: Avicenna completes the Canon of Medicine
anchors.summary: Ibn Sina orders Greek, Persian, and Indian medicine into one system of causes and remedies, and the book is still set text in European medical faculties six centuries later.

anchors.title: Rajendra Chola raids Srivijaya
anchors.summary: A Tamil fleet crosses the Bay of Bengal and sacks the Malay ports that taxed the strait, loosening Srivijaya's hold on the sea road to China.

anchors.title: Mahmud of Ghazni sacks Somnath
anchors.summary: The Ghaznavid ruler's raid on the Gujarat temple kills its defenders and carries off its wealth, and accounts of it are still argued over a thousand years later.

anchors.title: Al-Biruni finishes his study of India
anchors.summary: A Khwarezmian scholar learns Sanskrit and sets out Indian astronomy, castes, and beliefs in their own terms, comparing them with Greek thought rather than condemning them.

anchors.title: The caliphate of Cordoba dissolves into taifas
anchors.summary: Al-Andalus splits into some two dozen small kingdoms that buy peace from Christian rulers with tribute and compete instead in poets, astronomers, and palaces.

anchors.title: Gunpowder formulas are published in China
anchors.summary: The Wujing Zongyao prints recipes for the mixture that will eventually rewrite every siege.

anchors.title: Anawrahta unifies Burma from Pagan
anchors.summary: The king pulls the Irrawaddy valley under one court, takes up Theravada Buddhism from the south, and begins the temple building that covers the plain.

anchors.title: Bi Sheng cuts movable type from clay
anchors.summary: A Song artisan sets individual baked-clay characters in an iron frame, a method too unwieldy for a script of thousands of characters to displace whole-page woodblocks.

anchors.title: Hohokam canals irrigate the Sonoran desert
anchors.summary: Farmers on the Salt and Gila rivers extend hundreds of kilometers of hand-dug canal, watering maize, beans, and cotton where rainfall alone supports none of them.

anchors.title: The sweet potato reaches eastern Polynesia
anchors.summary: A South American crop appears in Pacific island gardens under a name close to its Andean one, the clearest evidence of contact between Polynesia and the Americas.

anchors.title: Northern Europe takes up the plough and three fields
anchors.summary: Mouldboard ploughs, horse collars, and three-course rotation break the heavy northern soils, and the surplus feeds new towns, new markets, and a growing population.

anchors.title: The Great Schism
anchors.summary: Rome and Constantinople excommunicate each other; Christendom's halves stop pretending.

anchors.title: Tughril Beg enters Baghdad
anchors.summary: The Seljuk chief takes the city, is named sultan by the caliph, and installs a Turkish military class over the eastern Islamic world for the next two centuries.

anchors.title: Cardinals are given the election of the pope
anchors.summary: A Roman synod takes the choice of pope from the city's nobles and the emperor and hands it to the cardinal bishops, making the office one no lay ruler can fill.

anchors.title: The Norman conquest of England
anchors.summary: One October battle replaces England's ruling class, land law, and half its vocabulary.

anchors.title: The Nizamiyya opens in Baghdad
anchors.summary: Nizam al-Mulk endows a salaried college for Sunni law, and the madrasa becomes a state instrument for training judges and standardizing doctrine.

anchors.title: Al-Bakri describes the kingdom of Ghana
anchors.summary: A geographer in Cordoba compiles merchants' reports of a West African king whose duties on salt and gold caravans pay for an army of tens of thousands.

anchors.title: Wang Anshi launches the New Policies
anchors.summary: State loans to farmers, a resurveyed land tax, and hired labor in place of forced service split the Song bureaucracy into factions that fight over the program for decades.

anchors.title: The Almoravids found Marrakesh
anchors.summary: A Saharan Berber movement plants a capital at the desert's northern edge and comes to hold the gold routes from the Senegal river to the Mediterranean coast.

anchors.title: The Seljuks defeat Byzantium at Manzikert
anchors.summary: The emperor is captured and his army broken, and within a decade Turkish warlords and herders hold most of Anatolia, the empire's main source of soldiers and grain.

anchors.title: Henry IV waits at Canossa
anchors.summary: The excommunicated emperor stands outside the castle in winter to beg absolution from Gregory VII, and the image of a king submitting to a pope outlives the truce it bought.

anchors.title: Alfonso VI takes Toledo
anchors.summary: Castile captures the old Visigothic capital with its libraries and its Arabic-speaking Christians intact, and the Christian frontier reaches the Tagus for good.

anchors.title: England is surveyed for Domesday
anchors.summary: The Norman king's commissioners record who holds every manor, how many ploughs and mills it has, and what it is worth, a fiscal inventory no other kingdom could match.

anchors.title: The Almoravids beat Castile at Sagrajas
anchors.summary: Yusuf ibn Tashfin crosses from Morocco at the taifa kings' invitation, stops Alfonso VI's advance, and within a few years annexes the kingdoms that called him.

anchors.title: Bologna's law school becomes a university
anchors.summary: Students hire their teachers and incorporate; the European university is born as a guild.

anchors.title: Shen Kuo compiles the Dream Pool Essays
anchors.summary: A retired Song official records the magnetic needle's deviation from true south, fossil bamboo far north of any living grove, and a calendar reform his colleagues refused.

anchors.title: Hasan-i Sabbah seizes Alamut
anchors.summary: The Nizari Ismaili leader takes a mountain fortress in northern Persia and builds a chain of strongholds that outlasts the Seljuk state it was founded to defy.

anchors.title: The Normans complete the conquest of Sicily
anchors.summary: Thirty years of campaigning end Muslim rule on the island, and the new count rules through Greek and Arabic scribes while tolerating the island's mosques.

anchors.title: Urban II calls the crusade at Clermont
anchors.summary: The pope tells an assembly in the Auvergne to march east and recover Jerusalem, promising remission of sin for the journey, and tens of thousands take the vow.

anchors.title: The First Crusade takes Jerusalem
anchors.summary: Frankish armies storm the city and found crusader states the region will spend two centuries digesting.

anchors.title: Venice founds the Arsenal
anchors.summary: The republic concentrates shipbuilding in one state yard, and its fleets begin outbuilding every rival on the sea lanes.

anchors.title: Bernard founds Clairvaux
anchors.summary: The Cistercian order multiplies across Europe, clearing forests and running model farms that push settlement into the wastes.

anchors.title: Aguda proclaims the Jurchen Jin dynasty
anchors.summary: Jurchen tribes unite against Liao overlordship; within a decade their cavalry threatens the Song itself.

anchors.title: Chinese sailors navigate by compass
anchors.summary: Zhu Yu's Pingzhou Table Talks records mariners steering by the south-pointing needle; ocean sailing loosens its dependence on clear skies.

anchors.title: The Knights Templar are founded
anchors.summary: A vow to guard pilgrims becomes a military order whose houses double as Europe's first international bankers.

anchors.title: The White Ship sinks
anchors.summary: England's heir drowns off Barfleur in a night wreck; the disputed succession tips England into the civil war called the Anarchy.

anchors.title: The Concordat of Worms
anchors.summary: Pope and emperor split the making of bishops between them, settling fifty years of investiture conflict with a lasting church-state boundary.

anchors.title: The Jurchen sack Kaifeng
anchors.summary: Jin cavalry carry off the Song emperor and his court; the dynasty regroups south of the Yangtze at Hangzhou.

anchors.title: Roger II is crowned king of Sicily
anchors.summary: Norman Sicily fuses Latin, Greek, and Arab administration into the Mediterranean's best-run and richest kingdom.

anchors.title: Portugal is recognized as a kingdom
anchors.summary: The Treaty of Zamora seats Afonso Henriques as king; a narrow Atlantic kingdom acquires the crown that will later map the oceans.

anchors.title: Zengi takes Edessa
anchors.summary: The first crusader state founded is the first to fall, and the shock summons the Second Crusade from Europe.

anchors.title: Saint-Denis consecrates the first Gothic choir
anchors.summary: Abbot Suger's ribbed vaults and glass walls set off a building style every ambitious town will spend fortunes to copy.

anchors.title: The Almohads take Marrakesh
anchors.summary: Ibn Tumart's reform movement destroys the Almoravid state and rules from Morocco to al-Andalus under one doctrine.

anchors.title: Crusaders take Lisbon for Portugal
anchors.summary: Passing Second Crusade fleets besiege the city for the new Portuguese crown, one of that expedition's few lasting gains.

anchors.title: Angkor Wat is built
anchors.summary: The Khmer empire's hydraulic capital raises the largest religious monument on earth.

anchors.title: Cahokia at its height
anchors.summary: The mound city on the Mississippi holds more people than contemporary London, ruling a trade world of shell, copper, and maize.

anchors.title: Toledo's translators turn Arabic science into Latin
anchors.summary: Gerard of Cremona and his colleagues render Aristotle, Euclid, and Avicenna for Latin readers, stocking the new universities' shelves.

anchors.title: Al-Idrisi completes his world map for Sicily
anchors.summary: The Book of Roger compiles sailors' and merchants' reports into the most accurate geography either shore of the Mediterranean possesses.

anchors.title: The Song make paper money national
anchors.summary: The huizi becomes state-backed currency across the south; printing presses now issue money as well as books.

anchors.title: Gunpowder bombs defend the Yangtze at Caishi
anchors.summary: Song paddle-wheel ships and thunderclap bombs turn back a Jin invasion; the new chemistry proves itself in fleet action.

anchors.title: Becket is murdered in Canterbury cathedral
anchors.summary: Four knights kill the archbishop at vespers; the martyr's shrine humbles the crown before centuries of pilgrims.

anchors.title: Saladin ends the Fatimid caliphate
anchors.summary: Egypt returns to Sunni allegiance under a Kurdish soldier whose new house will unite Cairo and Damascus against the crusader states.

anchors.title: The Lombard League defeats Barbarossa at Legnano
anchors.summary: Militia infantry of the communes break an imperial army; the emperor concedes self-government to the Italian cities at Constance.

anchors.title: Kilwa steers the Sofala gold trade
anchors.summary: The Swahili port mints its own coins and channels southern African gold into Indian Ocean commerce.

anchors.title: Jayavarman VII rebuilds the Khmer empire
anchors.summary: After a Cham sack, the king raises Angkor Thom, a road network, and public hospitals; the empire reaches its widest extent.

anchors.title: The Minamoto destroy the Taira at Dan-no-ura
anchors.summary: A sea battle ends the Genpei war and the court's grip on force; power passes to warrior government.

anchors.title: Post windmills appear in northwest Europe
anchors.summary: Where streams are flat or frozen, wind now grinds the grain; milling detaches from rivers and lords' ponds.

anchors.title: Saladin wins at Hattin and retakes Jerusalem
anchors.summary: The crusader field army is destroyed in a day; the city surrenders on terms and Latin rule shrinks to the coast.

anchors.title: Yoritomo becomes shogun at Kamakura
anchors.summary: Japan acquires a warrior government beside the court; soldiers, not courtiers, will rule for most of seven centuries.

anchors.title: Ghurid cavalry win at Tarain
anchors.summary: Muhammad of Ghor defeats Prithviraj Chauhan; the Ganges plain opens to Turkic rule and the Delhi sultanate to come.

anchors.title: The Third Crusade ends at Jaffa
anchors.summary: Richard and Saladin settle for a truce: the coast stays Frankish, Jerusalem stays Muslim, and pilgrims may visit unarmed.

anchors.title: Nalanda is sacked
anchors.summary: Bakhtiyar Khalji's raiders burn the great monastery and its libraries; institutional Buddhism in India loses its center and fades.

anchors.title: Lalibela's rock-hewn churches are carved
anchors.summary: Ethiopian masons cut eleven churches down into living rock, a new Jerusalem for a Christian kingdom beyond crusader reach.

anchors.title: Paris masters win a royal charter
anchors.summary: Philip Augustus places scholars under church courts; the guild of masters hardens into the model northern university.

anchors.title: Fibonacci publishes the Liber Abaci
anchors.summary: Hindu-Arabic numerals reach Latin merchants in a usable handbook; counting houses begin abandoning the abacus for the pen.

anchors.title: The Fourth Crusade sacks Constantinople
anchors.summary: Diverted by debts to Venice, crusaders storm and loot the greatest Christian city; Byzantium is partitioned and never fully recovers.

anchors.title: The Delhi sultanate is founded
anchors.summary: Aibak, a former military slave, takes power at Lahore in his own name; Turkic sultans will rule north India for three centuries.

anchors.title: Temüjin becomes Genghis Khan
anchors.summary: The steppe confederates under one khan; within two generations his house rules from Korea to Hungary.

anchors.title: The Albigensian Crusade begins
anchors.summary: A crusade turns inward against Christian heretics; Beziers is massacred and Languedoc's independence bleeds away to the French crown.

anchors.title: Christian kings win at Las Navas de Tolosa
anchors.summary: A combined Iberian army breaks Almohad power in Spain; within four decades only Granada remains under Muslim rule.

anchors.title: The Fourth Lateran Council legislates for Christendom
anchors.summary: Innocent III's council fixes doctrine and annual confession, and orders Jews and Muslims to wear distinguishing dress.

anchors.title: Magna Carta is sealed
anchors.summary: English barons force a king to concede that even he sits under law, a clause lawyers will quote forever.

anchors.title: The Mongols destroy Khwarazm
anchors.summary: A murdered caravan brings Genghis Khan west; Samarkand, Bukhara, and Urgench fall, and Iran's cities count their dead for decades.

anchors.title: The Mongols extinguish the Jin
anchors.summary: Allied briefly with the Song, Mongol armies end Jurchen rule at Caizhou; all of north China now answers to the khan.

anchors.title: Sundiata founds the Mali empire
anchors.summary: Victory at Kirina yokes the Niger's gold fields and river trade to a Mande state that will span the western Sudan.

anchors.title: Sukhothai breaks from Angkor
anchors.summary: Tai chiefs found their own kingdom on the upper Chao Phraya; a Thai political tradition begins as Khmer power thins.

anchors.title: The Mongols sack Kiev
anchors.summary: Rus's mother city falls to Batu; the principalities pass under Horde tribute and their center of gravity drifts northeast.

anchors.title: Luebeck and Hamburg ally
anchors.summary: Two ports pool protection of the Baltic-North Sea portage; the pact grows into the Hanseatic League's grip on northern trade.

anchors.title: Ibn al-Nafis describes pulmonary circulation
anchors.summary: A Damascus-trained physician corrects Galen: blood crosses the lungs, not the heart's wall; the insight waits centuries for readers.

anchors.title: The Mongols withdraw from Europe
anchors.summary: With Hungary broken and Poland raided, Batu turns back east on news of the great khan's death; Latin Europe is spared by a funeral.

anchors.title: Castile takes Seville
anchors.summary: Ferdinand III's conquest of the Guadalquivir valley leaves Granada as Iberia's last emirate, a tributary holding on for two centuries.

anchors.title: The Mamluks take power in Egypt
anchors.summary: Slave soldiers depose their Ayyubid masters mid-crusade; a self-replacing military caste will hold Egypt and Syria for 267 years.

anchors.title: The Tu'i Tonga chiefdom spans the central Pacific
anchors.summary: Tongan fleets draw tribute and chiefly marriages from Fiji to Samoa, the widest political web in Oceania.

anchors.title: Florence mints the gold florin
anchors.summary: A stable gold coin from a merchant republic becomes Europe's unit of big money, quoted from London to the Levant.

anchors.title: The Mongols sack Baghdad
anchors.summary: The Abbasid caliphate ends in a week of slaughter; the Tigris runs with ink and blood alike, the chroniclers insist.

anchors.title: The Mamluks stop the Mongols at Ain Jalut
anchors.summary: Egypt's army defeats a Mongol force in Galilee; the westward conquest finds its limit and Cairo inherits the caliphate's prestige.

anchors.title: Yekuno Amlak restores the Solomonic line
anchors.summary: A new Ethiopian dynasty claims descent from Solomon and Sheba, binding crown, church, and legend for seven centuries.

anchors.title: Kublai proclaims the Yuan dynasty
anchors.summary: The Mongol khan takes a Chinese dynastic name and rules from Dadu; the steppe empire acquires a Confucian face.

anchors.title: Rumi dies at Konya
anchors.summary: The Masnavi's six books of Persian couplets become Sufism's most-read poetry, and his followers a lasting order.

anchors.title: Aquinas leaves the Summa unfinished
anchors.summary: Dying en route to a council, Thomas leaves a synthesis of Aristotle and scripture that becomes Catholic philosophy's spine.

anchors.title: Marco Polo reaches Kublai's court
anchors.summary: A Venetian family's trade mission becomes Europe's best-selling description of a richer world.

anchors.title: The Song dynasty ends at Yamen
anchors.summary: The child emperor drowns as the last loyalist fleet is destroyed; for the first time all China is ruled by conquest from the steppe.

anchors.title: Storms wreck the Mongol invasion of Japan
anchors.summary: Kublai's second armada founders in a typhoon off Kyushu; Japan stays unconquered and names the wind divine.

anchors.title: The Sicilian Vespers
anchors.summary: An Easter riot in Palermo becomes a general massacre of the French and a twenty-year war; Sicily passes to Aragon.

anchors.title: The Four Corners are abandoned
anchors.summary: After decades of drought, Ancestral Pueblo families leave Mesa Verde and Chaco's world for the Rio Grande and Hopi mesas.

anchors.title: Eyeglasses are invented in Italy
anchors.summary: Ground lenses in a frame double the working life of scribes, tailors, and scholars whose eyes blur with age.

anchors.title: Dai Viet breaks the Mongols at Bach Dang
anchors.summary: Tran Hung Dao's staked riverbed traps the Yuan fleet at low tide; the third invasion fails and Vietnam keeps its autonomy.

anchors.title: England expels its Jews
anchors.summary: Edward I banishes the whole community after decades of taxation and libels; the expulsion stands for over 350 years.

anchors.title: Acre falls to the Mamluks
anchors.summary: The last crusader capital is stormed after a six-week siege; two centuries of Latin states on the Levantine coast end.

anchors.title: Three forest cantons swear the Federal Charter
anchors.summary: Uri, Schwyz, and Unterwalden bind themselves to mutual defense; the oath becomes the seed of the Swiss confederation.

anchors.title: Majapahit is founded in Java
anchors.summary: Raden Wijaya turns a Mongol punitive expedition to his own use, then expels it; his new city grows into an archipelago power.

anchors.title: Edward I summons the Model Parliament
anchors.summary: Knights and burgesses sit alongside lords and bishops to grant taxes; consent of the shires becomes an English habit.

anchors.title: Osman's beylik emerges in Bithynia
anchors.summary: A frontier warband on Byzantium's shrinking edge begins the conquests tradition dates to this year; an empire grows from the marches.

anchors.title: Cahokia empties
anchors.summary: Flood, drought, and fraying authority thin the Mississippian metropolis; within two generations the great plazas fall silent.

anchors.title: Great Zimbabwe at its height
anchors.summary: Dry-stone walls enclose a cattle-and-gold capital trading with the Swahili coast and beyond.

anchors.title: Ife casts its brass heads
anchors.summary: Yoruba artists at Ile-Ife produce lifelike cast portraits of rulers, among the most technically assured metalwork anywhere in the world.

anchors.title: Mechanical clocks appear in Europe
anchors.summary: Weight-driven escapements spread through towers, and within decades bells strike equal public hours across town.

anchors.title: Giotto paints the Arena Chapel
anchors.summary: Weight, grief, and depth enter European painting at Padua; artists start rendering people instead of emblems.

anchors.title: The papacy moves to Avignon
anchors.summary: Clement V settles under the French crown's shadow; seven decades of absence corrode Rome and papal prestige alike.

anchors.title: Malik Kafur raids the Indian south
anchors.summary: Delhi's general returns from Madurai with temple gold by the ton; sultanate power now reaches, and unsettles, the peninsula.

anchors.title: The Great Famine strikes northern Europe
anchors.summary: Three years of drowned harvests kill perhaps a tenth of the population; the medieval boom ends in the rain.

anchors.title: Dante completes the Divine Comedy
anchors.summary: An exile's hundred cantos fix Tuscan as a literary language and give Europe its map of hell, purgatory, and heaven.

anchors.title: Mansa Musa's hajj floods Cairo with gold
anchors.summary: Mali's emperor spends so freely en route to Mecca that Egyptian gold prices sag for years.

anchors.title: Ibn Battuta leaves Tangier
anchors.summary: A twenty-nine-year journey through Dar al-Islam from Mali to China ends as the era's widest first-person geography.

anchors.title: Tenochtitlan is founded
anchors.summary: The Mexica settle a swampy island in Lake Texcoco; tradition marks the eagle on the cactus where their capital rises.

anchors.title: Cannon appear in Europe
anchors.summary: Florence orders metal guns and a manuscript pictures one firing a bolt; within a century walls are being redesigned around powder.

anchors.title: Moscow becomes the Horde's tax collector
anchors.summary: Ivan Kalita gathers the grand princely title and the metropolitan's seat; tribute flows through Moscow and sticks there.

anchors.title: Delhi's token currency fails
anchors.summary: Muhammad bin Tughluq decrees brass coins worth silver; forgery floods the realm and the treasury buys back the failure.

anchors.title: Vijayanagara is founded
anchors.summary: Harihara and Bukka raise a Hindu empire on the Tungabhadra that will anchor the south against Delhi for over two centuries.

anchors.title: The Hundred Years War begins
anchors.summary: Edward III claims the French crown; five generations of dynastic war will forge both kingdoms' taxes, armies, and nationhoods.

anchors.title: Ashikaga Takauji becomes shogun
anchors.summary: A new warrior government rules from Kyoto beside a split imperial court; provincial lords grow harder to command.

anchors.title: Petrarch is crowned poet laureate in Rome
anchors.summary: The Capitoline ceremony announces a program: recover the ancients, reform the present; humanism acquires its first celebrity.

anchors.title: The Bahmani sultanate rises in the Deccan
anchors.summary: Rebel Delhi officers found a plateau kingdom; its long duel with Vijayanagara will organize southern politics for 150 years.

anchors.title: The Black Death reaches Europe
anchors.summary: Perhaps half of Europe dies within five years; wages, faith, and the feudal bargain never fully recover.

anchors.title: The Black Death devastates the Islamic world
anchors.summary: Cairo, the largest city west of China, buries thousands a day; Egypt's fields and Syria's towns take a century's wound.

anchors.title: Plague massacres of Jews sweep the Rhineland
anchors.summary: Accused of poisoning wells, whole communities are burned at Strasbourg and beyond; survivors resettle eastward in Poland.

anchors.title: Maori settlement fills Aotearoa
anchors.summary: The Pacific's last great landmass fills with settlers from tropical Polynesia; within generations the giant moa are hunted out.

anchors.title: Ayutthaya is founded
anchors.summary: Ramathibodi plants a Thai capital on an island in the Chao Phraya; river trade and rice make it Southeast Asia's rising power.

anchors.title: Ilyas Shah unites Bengal
anchors.summary: The delta's three cities join under one independent sultanate; its muslins and rice draw traders from across the Indian Ocean.

anchors.title: The Ottomans take Gallipoli
anchors.summary: An earthquake topples the walls and Ottoman soldiers occupy the breach; the empire has its first foothold in Europe.

anchors.title: The Golden Bull fixes the Empire's elections
anchors.summary: Seven princes gain the sole right to choose the emperor; the Holy Roman Empire codifies its own decentralization.

anchors.title: Majapahit at its peak is sung in verse
anchors.summary: The Nagarakretagama catalogues tributaries across the archipelago; Java's court sits atop the spice routes' politics.

anchors.title: The Ming expel the Mongols
anchors.summary: A peasant rebel becomes emperor and rebuilds China's institutions around agrarian orthodoxy.

anchors.title: Timur takes power in Samarkand
anchors.summary: A Barlas soldier begins forty years of campaigns that wreck cities from Delhi to Damascus and gild his capital with their craftsmen.

anchors.title: The Ming ban private sea trade
anchors.summary: The haijin closes China's coast to private commerce; smuggling, piracy, and tribute fleets fill the vacuum it makes.

anchors.title: Korea prints with movable metal type
anchors.summary: The Jikji is printed decades before Mainz, the technique exists; the market and script differ.

anchors.title: The Western Schism splits the papacy
anchors.summary: Rival popes at Rome and Avignon excommunicate each other for four decades; every kingdom must pick its pontiff.

anchors.title: Moscow defeats the Horde at Kulikovo
anchors.summary: Dmitry Donskoy's coalition beats Mamai on the Don; tribute soon resumes, but the spell of Mongol invincibility is broken.

anchors.title: The English Peasants' Revolt
anchors.summary: Poll taxes after the plague bring rebels into London demanding an end to serfdom; the rising is crushed, but bondage keeps eroding.

anchors.title: Portugal secures its crown at Aljubarrota
anchors.summary: The new Aviz dynasty routs a Castilian invasion; an independent Portugal turns its ambitions toward the Atlantic.

anchors.title: Battle of Kosovo
anchors.summary: Both rulers die on the field; Serbia passes into vassalage and the Ottomans keep their Balkan road, while the day enters legend.

anchors.title: Yi Seong-gye founds Joseon
anchors.summary: A general turns his army back from the Ming border and takes the throne; his Neo-Confucian dynasty will rule Korea five centuries.

anchors.title: Timur sacks Delhi
anchors.summary: The sultanate's capital is plundered and its artisans marched to Samarkand; Delhi's power shrinks to a shadow for a generation.

anchors.title: Chimor rules the Peruvian coast from Chan Chan
anchors.summary: The largest adobe city in the Americas runs canal-fed valleys and craft workshops, until the Inca absorb it all within decades.

anchors.title: Melaka is founded on the strait
anchors.summary: A fugitive prince plants a port where the monsoons meet; with Ming patronage it becomes the emporium of Asian trade.

anchors.title: Timbuktu's manuscript culture flourishes
anchors.summary: Saharan trade underwrites libraries and jurists; books are the city's most durable export.

anchors.title: Timur captures Bayezid at Ankara
anchors.summary: The Ottoman sultan dies a prisoner and his sons fight a decade of civil war; Constantinople wins fifty more years.

anchors.title: Zheng He's first treasure voyage
anchors.summary: Ming fleets larger than anything afloat carry the emperor's flag to India, Arabia, and Africa, then, within thirty years, are scrapped.

anchors.title: The Yongle Encyclopedia is completed
anchors.summary: Two thousand scholars copy China's learning into eleven thousand volumes, a collection too vast ever to print.

anchors.title: Poland-Lithuania crushes the Teutonic Knights
anchors.summary: The order's field power breaks at Grunwald; the Baltic crusade ebbs and the Jagiellonian union stands as the region's great power.

anchors.title: Agincourt
anchors.summary: English longbows and French mud embarrass chivalry; the war grinds on anyway.

anchors.title: Portugal seizes Ceuta
anchors.summary: A crusading raid on a Moroccan port becomes the first step of an overseas empire; Henry the Navigator starts asking what lies south.

anchors.title: The Council of Constance ends the Schism
anchors.summary: One pope again after four decades of rivals; the council that reunites the church also burns Jan Hus and seeds a war.

anchors.title: The Hussite wars begin
anchors.summary: Bohemian reformers armed with war wagons and field guns defeat five crusades; a national church wins terms Rome must negotiate.

anchors.title: Portugal settles Madeira
anchors.summary: An empty Atlantic island becomes a laboratory for sugar, then for the plantation slavery that sugar will demand.

anchors.title: The Ming move the capital to Beijing
anchors.summary: Yongle rules from a rebuilt northern city facing the steppe; the Forbidden City and the Grand Canal now anchor Chinese government.

anchors.title: The Aztec Triple Alliance is formed
anchors.summary: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, and Tlacopan overthrow Azcapotzalco and split the valley's tribute; the Mexica share soon dominates.

anchors.title: Joan of Arc relieves Orleans
anchors.summary: A peasant visionary breaks the siege and marches the Dauphin to Reims; France's cause revives and grinds toward victory.

anchors.title: Ayutthaya sacks Angkor
anchors.summary: The Khmer court quits its hydraulic capital for the river towns near Phnom Penh; the temple city keeps only its monks.

anchors.title: Gil Eannes rounds Cape Bojador
anchors.summary: The current-swept cape that had turned back fifteen expeditions is passed; the West African coast opens to Portuguese sail.

anchors.title: Cosimo de' Medici masters Florence
anchors.summary: A banker rules the republic from behind its committees; his family's patronage sets painters, scholars, and architects to work.

anchors.title: Brunelleschi's dome crowns Florence cathedral
anchors.summary: The widest masonry dome ever built rises without centering; engineering ambition becomes a Renaissance credential.

anchors.title: Ulugh Beg's observatory charts the stars
anchors.summary: Samarkand's prince-astronomer measures a thousand stars afresh, the best positions anyone will hold until Tycho.

anchors.title: Pachacuti begins the Inca expansion
anchors.summary: After repelling the Chanca, the rebuilder of Cusco starts the conquests that stretch Tawantinsuyu across the Andes within two generations.

anchors.title: Ewuare the Great rebuilds Benin
anchors.summary: The oba rings his capital with walls and moats and expands the kingdom; Benin City's guilds cast brass for the court.

anchors.title: Portugal auctions African captives at Lagos
anchors.summary: Two hundred thirty-five captives seized on the Mauritanian coast are sold in the Algarve; the Atlantic trade in enslaved Africans has begun.

anchors.title: Sejong promulgates Hangul
anchors.summary: Korea's king publishes an alphabet built for the language's own sounds so commoners can write; literacy stops requiring Chinese.

anchors.title: The Ming emperor is captured at Tumu
anchors.summary: An Oirat ambush takes the Zhengtong emperor prisoner; the dynasty turns to wall-building and the defensive for good.

anchors.title: The Haudenosaunee league takes shape
anchors.summary: By tradition the Great Law of Peace binds five warring nations under one longhouse; the confederacy will outbargain empires.

anchors.title: Moai carving peaks on Rapa Nui
anchors.summary: Hundreds of ancestral figures stand along the coasts, quarried and moved by a society of a few thousand at the ocean's far edge.

anchors.title: Castillon ends the Hundred Years War
anchors.summary: French cannon destroy the last English field army; of the continental empire only Calais remains, and both crowns centralize.

anchors.title: Constantinople falls to the Ottomans
anchors.summary: Mehmed II's guns end the Eastern Roman Empire; Greek scholars and their libraries scatter west.

anchors.title: Gutenberg completes the 42-line Bible
anchors.summary: Movable type proves itself at Mainz; the price of the written word begins its long collapse.

anchors.title: Sunni Ali begins Songhai's conquests
anchors.summary: Gao's ruler takes Timbuktu and Djenne with river fleet and cavalry; Songhai supplants Mali as the western Sudan's power.

anchors.title: The Onin war ignites Sengoku Japan
anchors.summary: Eleven years of fighting level Kyoto and expose the shogun's weakness; provincial lords begin a century of private war.

anchors.title: Ferdinand and Isabella marry
anchors.summary: The wedding at Valladolid points Castile and Aragon toward one monarchy, the machine that will finish Granada and fund Columbus.

anchors.title: The Inca road system spans the Andes
anchors.summary: Forty thousand kilometers of graded road and rope bridges run an empire without wheels or writing.

anchors.title: Dai Viet conquers Champa's heartland
anchors.summary: Vijaya falls and the Cham kingdom is reduced to a remnant; Vietnamese settlement rolls south along the coast.

anchors.title: Caxton sets up England's first press
anchors.summary: Printing arrives at Westminster in English, not Latin; the London dialect starts hardening into a national standard.

anchors.title: Charles the Bold falls at Nancy
anchors.summary: Burgundy's ambition dies with its duke; France takes the duchy while the Netherlands pass by marriage to the Habsburgs.

anchors.title: The Spanish Inquisition is established
anchors.summary: A royal tribunal takes charge of orthodoxy, aimed first at converts from Judaism; religious policing becomes state machinery.

anchors.title: Printing presses blanket Europe
anchors.summary: Barely a generation after Mainz, presses run in over a hundred towns; books become a tenth of their manuscript price.

anchors.title: The stand on the Ugra ends Horde rule
anchors.summary: Ivan III faces down Akhmat's army without battle; Moscow stops paying tribute and calls itself sovereign.

anchors.title: Portugal builds Elmina on the Gold Coast
anchors.summary: A prefabricated fortress anchors the sea route for Akan gold, then for captives; European empire in Africa begins as a trading post.

anchors.title: Portugal makes contact with Kongo
anchors.summary: Diogo Cao anchors in the Congo estuary; within a decade the mani Kongo is baptized and the kingdoms exchange envoys as equals.

anchors.title: Bosworth crowns the Tudors
anchors.summary: Richard III dies in the melee and the Wars of the Roses effectively end; the new dynasty rebuilds the English crown's authority.

anchors.title: Tenochtitlan dedicates the Great Temple
anchors.summary: The rebuilt pyramid is consecrated with captives killed in the thousands, a toll the sources dispute; imperial ritual and terror fuse.

anchors.title: Dias rounds the Cape of Good Hope
anchors.summary: The African coast turns north under his keel; a sea road to India exists, waiting only for a fleet to sail it through.

anchors.title: Columbus reaches the Caribbean
anchors.summary: Two hemispheres that had traded nothing begin exchanging crops, silver, empires, and diseases.

anchors.title: Granada surrenders; Iberia expels its Jews
anchors.summary: The last emirate in Spain falls, and within months the expulsion edict scatters Sephardic life across the Mediterranean.

anchors.title: Askia Muhammad takes Songhai's throne
anchors.summary: A general's coup replaces Sunni Ali's line; the new dynasty organizes the empire around Islam, learning, and the Niger trade.

anchors.title: Charles VIII invades Italy
anchors.summary: A French army with siege guns crosses the Alps and walks through old walls; sixty years of great-power war in Italy begin.

anchors.title: Pacioli prints double-entry bookkeeping
anchors.summary: The Summa spreads Venice's method of debits and credits; merchants anywhere can now audit their own affairs.

anchors.title: Spain and Portugal divide the globe at Tordesillas
anchors.summary: A meridian drawn by treaty splits future discoveries between two crowns, to the lasting irritation of everyone else.

anchors.title: Cabot makes landfall in Newfoundland
anchors.summary: A Venetian under English colors touches North America; the cod banks he reports will draw fleets before any colony follows.

anchors.title: Leonardo completes the Last Supper
anchors.summary: A mural in a Milan refectory catches the instant of accusation; painting's new command of psychology becomes the standard to beat.

anchors.title: Da Gama reaches India by sea
anchors.summary: Portugal opens a spice route around Africa and prices the old caravans out.

anchors.title: Guru Nanak begins his teaching
anchors.summary: After a revelation at Sultanpur he preaches one God beyond Hindu and Muslim; the Sikh path begins in the Punjab.

anchors.title: Cabral sights Brazil
anchors.summary: Swinging wide toward India, the Portuguese fleet strikes South America and claims it under Tordesillas; a continent's colonization is scheduled by accident.

anchors.title: Tenochtitlan at its height
anchors.summary: Canals, causeways, and chinampas feed a lake capital larger than most European cities.

anchors.title: Ismail I makes Shiism the state faith of Iran
anchors.summary: Crowned at Tabriz, the young shah imposes Twelver Shiism on a largely Sunni population, setting Iran apart from its Ottoman and Uzbek neighbors.

anchors.title: The encomienda binds Indigenous labor on Hispaniola
anchors.summary: Crown grants assign Taino villages to settlers as tribute and forced labor, fixing the legal form Spanish colonists will carry to the mainland.

anchors.title: A Portuguese fleet sacks Kilwa and Mombasa
anchors.summary: Almeida's ships burn two of the Swahili coast's richest ports, announcing that Indian Ocean trade will now be taxed by force from Lisbon.

anchors.title: Waldseemuller's map names America
anchors.summary: A printed world map made in Lorraine labels the new southern landmass after Amerigo Vespucci, and the name spreads faster than any correction.

anchors.title: Portugal destroys a combined fleet at Diu
anchors.summary: Gujarati, Mamluk and Calicut squadrons are broken in a single day, leaving Portuguese warships free to police the sea lanes to the Red Sea.

anchors.title: Albuquerque takes Goa
anchors.summary: Portugal seizes a defensible harbor on the Konkan coast and makes it the capital of a seaborne empire built from fortified ports rather than conquered interiors.

anchors.title: Portugal captures Melaka
anchors.summary: The strait's great entrepot changes hands after a month of fighting, and its Muslim merchant networks disperse to Aceh, Johor and Brunei rather than submit.

anchors.title: Balboa crosses Panama and sights the Pacific
anchors.summary: A Spanish company hacks over the isthmus in twenty-five days and finds another ocean, proving the new lands are a barrier between Europe and Asia.

anchors.title: Ottoman guns break the Safavids at Chaldiran
anchors.summary: Selim I's artillery and janissary muskets shatter Qizilbash cavalry, fixing an Ottoman and Safavid frontier in eastern Anatolia that will hold for centuries.

anchors.title: Erasmus prints the Greek New Testament
anchors.summary: A scholar's parallel Greek and Latin text exposes errors in the Vulgate, handing reformers the philological ground on which they will contest doctrine.

anchors.title: Luther posts the ninety-five theses
anchors.summary: An indulgence dispute in Saxony becomes, via the printing press, the fracture of western Christendom.

anchors.title: The Ottomans destroy the Mamluk sultanate
anchors.summary: Selim I takes Cairo, absorbs Syria and Egypt, and assumes protection of Mecca and Medina, making the sultan the leading power of the Sunni world.

anchors.title: Cortes enters Tenochtitlan
anchors.summary: A small Spanish company and thousands of Tlaxcalan allies walk into the Mexica capital as guests, and within two years the same alliance will besiege it.

anchors.title: Suleiman I inherits the Ottoman throne
anchors.summary: A sultan takes an empire spanning the Balkans, Anatolia, Syria and Egypt, and spends forty-six years extending its borders and codifying its law.

anchors.title: Tenochtitlan falls
anchors.summary: Cortés, smallpox, and indigenous allies bring down the Mexica capital; New Spain rises on its ruins.

anchors.title: The Diet of Worms outlaws Luther
anchors.summary: Refusing to recant before the emperor, Luther is declared a heretic and an outlaw, and the German princes who shelter him turn the schism into a political fact.

anchors.title: The Victoria completes the first circumnavigation
anchors.summary: Eighteen survivors of Magellan's expedition reach Seville after three years, having measured for themselves the ocean that separates America from Asia.

anchors.title: The Ottomans take Rhodes
anchors.summary: After six months of siege the Knights Hospitaller surrender and sail away, removing the last Christian corsair base in the eastern Mediterranean.

anchors.title: Afonso I of Kongo protests the slave trade
anchors.summary: The Christian king writes to Lisbon that Portuguese traders are depopulating his kingdom, and is answered with more ships rather than fewer.

anchors.title: Mohacs destroys the Hungarian kingdom
anchors.summary: Louis II and most of his nobility die in under two hours, and Hungary is partitioned between Ottoman and Habsburg claimants for the next century and a half.

anchors.title: Babur founds the Mughal empire
anchors.summary: Field guns at Panipat win Delhi for a Timurid exile; his house will govern most of India for two centuries.

anchors.title: Unpaid imperial troops sack Rome
anchors.summary: Mutinous soldiers of Charles V loot the papal city for months, killing thousands and scattering the artists and humanists who had made it a capital of learning.

anchors.title: The Ottoman siege of Vienna fails
anchors.summary: Suleiman's army arrives late in a wet season, cannot bring up its heavy guns, and withdraws, marking the practical limit of Ottoman reach into central Europe.

anchors.title: Pizarro seizes Atahualpa at Cajamarca
anchors.summary: Fewer than two hundred Spaniards ambush the Inca ruler in the middle of his own army and hold the empire's chain of command hostage.

anchors.title: The Spanish take Cuzco
anchors.summary: Atahualpa is executed after his ransom is paid, and Pizarro's men enter the Inca capital, ruling at first through a Sapa Inca of their own choosing.

anchors.title: The Act of Supremacy breaks England from Rome
anchors.summary: Parliament declares the king supreme head of the church in England, turning a marriage dispute into a permanent transfer of religious authority to the state.

anchors.title: The Ottomans take Baghdad from the Safavids
anchors.summary: Suleiman's army occupies Iraq and its Shia shrine cities, adding the Tigris valley and a route toward the Gulf to the empire.

anchors.title: Calvin publishes the Institutes
anchors.summary: A French exile in Basel sets out a systematic Reformed theology, and the book he expands for the rest of his life will organize churches from Geneva to Scotland.

anchors.title: Barbarossa defeats the Holy League at Preveza
anchors.summary: An Ottoman fleet scatters a larger Venetian and Habsburg force, leaving the eastern Mediterranean under Ottoman naval control for a generation.

anchors.title: The papacy approves the Society of Jesus
anchors.summary: Loyola's order takes vows of obedience to the pope and becomes the Catholic reform's teaching corps and its missionary arm from Brazil to Japan.

anchors.title: Charles V's fleet is wrecked off Algiers
anchors.summary: An October storm destroys the emperor's armada before it can land in force, confirming that the Barbary ports will remain Ottoman clients.

anchors.title: The New Laws restrict the encomienda
anchors.summary: Prompted by Las Casas, the crown bans Indigenous enslavement and orders encomiendas to lapse on the holder's death; colonists revolt and much of it is repealed.

anchors.title: Copernicus publishes on the heavens
anchors.summary: A canon's deathbed book moves the Earth; the argument will take a century and several trials.

anchors.title: Portuguese matchlocks reach Tanegashima
anchors.summary: Japanese smiths copy the arquebus within a year, and firearms in quantity change how the warring provinces fight and how their castles are built.

anchors.title: Vesalius publishes De humani corporis fabrica
anchors.summary: Dissections done by the professor's own hand correct Galen in print, and anatomy becomes a subject settled by looking rather than by citation.

anchors.title: Ethiopia defeats Adal at Wayna Daga
anchors.summary: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim is killed and his invasion collapses, but fifteen years of war leave the Ethiopian highlands stripped of churches, books and people.

anchors.title: Cocoliztli kills millions in New Spain
anchors.summary: An epidemic the Nahua called cocoliztli sweeps central Mexico for three years, carrying off much of a population already thinned by earlier disease.

anchors.title: Silver is found at Potosí
anchors.summary: An Andean mountain begins bankrolling Spain and inflating prices from Seville to Beijing.

anchors.title: The Council of Trent opens
anchors.summary: Catholic bishops begin eighteen years of sessions that define doctrine against the reformers, tighten seminary training and end the sale of indulgences.

anchors.title: Francis Xavier lands at Kagoshima
anchors.summary: The first Jesuit mission to Japan begins, winning converts among western daimyo who also want the Portuguese trade that arrives with the priests.

anchors.title: The Columbian exchange reworks world diets
anchors.summary: Potatoes and maize move east, wheat and cattle west, silver everywhere, and pathogens deadliest of all.

anchors.title: Ivan IV takes Kazan
