anchors.summary: Russian siege guns and a mine breach the khanate's walls; the middle Volga passes to Moscow, which now governs Muslim subjects as an empire rather than a principality.

anchors.title: Coffeehouses open in Istanbul
anchors.summary: A new drink builds a new room, caffeinated, talkative, and repeatedly banned for it.

anchors.title: Mercury amalgamation multiplies American silver
anchors.summary: Bartolome de Medina's patio process at Pachuca wins silver from low grade ore with mercury, and the method carried south to Potosi floods world markets with bullion.

anchors.title: The Peace of Augsburg divides Germany by faith
anchors.summary: Each prince may set Lutheranism or Catholicism for his own territory and dissenting subjects may emigrate, freezing the schism into a map.

anchors.title: Akbar takes the Mughal throne at Panipat
anchors.summary: A thirteen-year-old emperor's regent wins the second battle of Panipat, restoring Mughal rule in north India and opening a reign of nearly fifty years.

anchors.title: The Shaanxi earthquake kills hundreds of thousands
anchors.summary: Loess cliff dwellings collapse on their occupants across several provinces in the deadliest earthquake on record, emptying whole counties of people.

anchors.title: Portugal settles at Macau
anchors.summary: Ming officials tolerate a Portuguese trading post on the Pearl River delta, giving Europe a licensed door into Chinese silk and a leg of the silver circuit.

anchors.title: The Spanish crown suspends its debts
anchors.summary: Philip II converts short term loans into low yield bonds and ruins his German bankers, the first of several defaults by a treasury outrunning American silver.

anchors.title: The massacre at Vassy opens France's religious wars
anchors.summary: Ducal troops kill Huguenots at worship in a barn, and France enters thirty-six years of civil war fought over faith, succession and noble faction.

anchors.title: Akbar abolishes the tax on non-Muslims
anchors.summary: Ending the jizya lifts a legal mark of subordination from the Hindu majority and buys the Mughal state Rajput service instead of Rajput revolt.

anchors.title: The Ottomans fail to take Malta
anchors.summary: Four months of siege break on the Knights' fortifications and a relief force from Sicily, checking Ottoman expansion in the western Mediterranean.

anchors.title: Urdaneta finds the Pacific return route
anchors.summary: Sailing north to catch the westerlies, a friar navigator makes the run from the Philippines to Acapulco possible and opens an annual traffic in silver and silk.

anchors.title: Talikota breaks Vijayanagara
anchors.summary: A coalition of Deccan sultanates destroys the empire's army and sacks its capital over months; the dominant state of south India never recovers.

anchors.title: The Ming license private overseas trade
anchors.summary: Lifting most of the ban at Yuegang turns smuggling into taxable commerce and pulls American and Japanese silver into a rapidly monetized Chinese economy.

anchors.title: The Dutch provinces revolt against Spain
anchors.summary: Resistance to Alba's tribunals and taxes becomes open war, and eighty years of fighting will end with a Protestant republic on Europe's richest coastline.

anchors.title: Nobunaga enters Kyoto
anchors.summary: Installing a shogun of his own choosing in the capital, a provincial lord begins subordinating the warring domains by siege, firearms and the destruction of armed temples.

anchors.title: Mercator publishes his navigational projection
anchors.summary: Stretching latitude so that a compass bearing draws as a straight line, the new chart trades true area for usable courses and becomes the sailor's standard.

anchors.title: Lepanto
anchors.summary: A Holy League fleet checks Ottoman sea power in the last great galley battle.

anchors.title: Legazpi founds Manila
anchors.summary: Spain plants a walled city on Luzon's bay, giving the Pacific galleons an Asian terminus where Mexican silver buys Chinese silk and porcelain.

anchors.title: The St Bartholomew's Day massacre
anchors.summary: The killing of Huguenot leaders in Paris spreads to the provinces over weeks, leaving thousands dead and ending hope of a negotiated religious settlement.

anchors.title: Toledo imposes the mita draft at Potosi
anchors.summary: The viceroy conscripts a rotating share of adult men from Andean villages to work the silver mountain and its mercury mines, with high death rates and emptied home communities.

anchors.title: Morocco destroys a Portuguese army at Alcacer Quibir
anchors.summary: King Sebastian dies with much of his nobility in a single day's battle, Morocco stays independent under the Saadis, and Portugal's crown is left without an heir.

anchors.title: Philip II takes the Portuguese crown
anchors.summary: Sixty years of shared monarchy bind Portugal's Asian and Atlantic possessions to Spain's wars, and make Portuguese ports and ships targets for Dutch and English fleets.

anchors.title: The single whip reform puts Ming taxes in silver
anchors.summary: Consolidating scattered levies and labor services into one silver payment simplifies collection and ties peasant households to a currency China does not mine.

anchors.title: Yermak's Cossacks cross the Urals
anchors.summary: A band financed by the Stroganov merchants attacks the Siberian khanate, and fur tribute then pulls Russian forts eastward river by river toward the Pacific.

anchors.title: The Gregorian calendar reform
anchors.summary: Ten days vanish by papal bull; Europe spends three centuries disagreeing about what day it is.

anchors.title: Nobunaga is killed at Honnoji
anchors.summary: A trusted general turns on him in a Kyoto temple; Hideyoshi avenges the death within days and inherits the unfinished unification of Japan.

anchors.title: Antwerp falls and the Scheldt is closed
anchors.summary: Parma retakes the city and the rebel provinces blockade its river, driving merchants, printers and capital north to Amsterdam.

anchors.title: England plants a colony at Roanoke
anchors.summary: Raleigh's settlers land on the Carolina banks, quarrel with their Algonquian hosts, and within five years the site is abandoned and its second party lost.

anchors.title: The Spanish Armada fails
anchors.summary: Weather and gunnery break the invasion of England; Atlantic power starts drifting north.

anchors.title: Hideyoshi's sword hunt disarms the villages
anchors.summary: Confiscating peasant weapons begins a legal separation of farmer from warrior that ends the armed village and closes the path from the fields to samurai rank.

anchors.title: Moroccan gunners break Songhai at Tondibi
anchors.summary: A few thousand soldiers with muskets and cannon cross the Sahara and destroy a far larger army, and the Niger empire fragments into successor states.

anchors.title: Japan invades Korea
anchors.summary: Hideyoshi's armies drive north toward the Ming frontier while Korean fleets under Yi Sun-sin cut their supply by sea; six years of war leave Korea devastated.

anchors.title: The first Dutch fleet sails for the Indies
anchors.summary: Four ships reach Banten; three return with pepper enough to show a profit, and within seven years the competing Dutch ventures are merged into one chartered monopoly.

anchors.title: The Edict of Nantes grants Huguenots toleration
anchors.summary: Henry IV, a Protestant who turned Catholic to gain Paris, guarantees his former co-religionists worship, courts and fortified towns, ending the religious wars.

anchors.title: Abbas I moves the Safavid capital to Isfahan
anchors.summary: A rebuilt central city and a standing army of slave soldiers place the shah's power above the Qizilbash tribes whose cavalry had made the dynasty.

anchors.title: Giordano Bruno is burned in Rome
anchors.summary: The Roman Inquisition executes a friar who taught an infinite universe of many worlds, marking the limits Rome now set on speculation after Trent.

anchors.title: The English East India Company is chartered
anchors.summary: A London syndicate wins a royal monopoly on trade east of the Cape, beginning as a pepper venture and ending as the ruler of much of India.

anchors.title: Huaynaputina erupts in the Andes
anchors.summary: South America's largest historical eruption buries villages in ash and cools summers as far away as Russia, where famine follows within two years.

anchors.title: Sekigahara decides Japan
anchors.summary: One morning's battle delivers Japan to the Tokugawa, who close and quiet it for 250 years.

anchors.title: The great Russian famine begins
anchors.summary: Three cold summers after a distant eruption ruin the harvests; perhaps two million die and Boris Godunov's government loses the country's obedience.

anchors.title: The Dutch East India Company is chartered
anchors.summary: Amsterdam invents the joint-stock megacorporation, complete with shares, dividends, and a private navy.

anchors.title: Ieyasu is named shogun at Edo
anchors.summary: The Tokugawa house takes the shogunate and begins two and a half centuries of enforced internal peace, with the daimyo held by hostages and alternate residence.

anchors.title: James VI of Scotland inherits England
anchors.summary: One king now rules Scotland, England, and Ireland from London, a personal union that leaves three parliaments, three churches, and three legal systems in place.

anchors.title: Cervantes publishes Don Quixote
anchors.summary: A parody of chivalric romance turns into the prototype of the European novel, read in translation across the continent within a decade.

anchors.title: Jahangir succeeds Akbar
anchors.summary: Akbar dies after half a century on the throne and his son inherits most of north India, a working revenue system, and a court that spends on painting and gardens.

anchors.title: Jamestown is planted in Virginia
anchors.summary: A company venture on the James river survives starvation and war with the Powhatan, and England gains its first permanent foothold in the Americas.

anchors.title: Champlain founds Quebec
anchors.summary: A fur post on the St Lawrence becomes the capital of New France and the base from which French traders and missionaries work deep into the continent's rivers.

anchors.title: Kepler gives the planets elliptical orbits
anchors.summary: Astronomia Nova replaces circles with ellipses and equal areas swept in equal times, fitting Tycho's observations of Mars at last.

anchors.title: Galileo publishes his telescope observations
anchors.summary: Moons around Jupiter and mountains on ours: the heavens acquire texture and the argument acquires evidence.

anchors.title: The Jesuits found the Guarani reductions
anchors.summary: Mission towns on the Parana gather Guarani families under Jesuit rule, sheltering them from slave raiders while dissolving the ways of living they arrived with.

anchors.title: Abbas begins the Shah Mosque at Isfahan
anchors.summary: Tiled domes rise on the new capital's great square, advertising Safavid wealth and the Shia establishment the dynasty had imposed on Iran.

anchors.title: Michael Romanov is elected tsar
anchors.summary: An assembly of estates ends the Time of Troubles by choosing a teenage boyar; his family will hold the Russian throne for three centuries.

anchors.title: Nurhaci proclaims the Later Jin
anchors.summary: A Jurchen chief who spent thirty years absorbing his rivals declares a state on the Ming's northeastern frontier and organizes its households into banners.

anchors.title: The Thirty Years' War begins
anchors.summary: A defenestration in Prague opens a war that will kill perhaps a third of the German lands.

anchors.title: The first enslaved Africans reach Virginia
anchors.summary: An English privateer sells about twenty captives taken from a Portuguese slave ship at Point Comfort, the beginning of African bondage in England's mainland colonies.

anchors.title: The VOC founds Batavia on Java
anchors.summary: Coen burns Jayakarta and builds a Dutch headquarters in its place, the hub from which the company will police the archipelago's spice trade for two centuries.

anchors.title: Ming armies are destroyed at Sarhu
anchors.summary: Nurhaci defeats four converging Ming columns in five days; the dynasty loses the initiative in the northeast and never recovers it.

anchors.title: The Mayflower lands at Plymouth
anchors.summary: Emigrants, Separatists and others alike, sign a compact for self-government before going ashore in Massachusetts, and half of them are dead by spring.

anchors.title: The Bohemian revolt ends at White Mountain
anchors.summary: An imperial army breaks the Protestant estates outside Prague in under two hours; Bohemia is re-Catholicized by force and its nobility dispossessed.

anchors.title: The VOC seizes the Banda islands
anchors.summary: To hold a monopoly on nutmeg, company forces kill, deport, or enslave nearly the whole Bandanese population and hand the groves to Dutch planters.

anchors.title: Abbas takes Hormuz from Portugal
anchors.summary: Safavid troops carried by English company ships storm the island fortress; Portuguese control of the Gulf ends and the shah's new port at Bandar Abbas replaces it.

anchors.title: Nzinga takes power in Ndongo
anchors.summary: She inherits a kingdom being hollowed out by Portuguese slave raiding and spends four decades fighting, negotiating, and relocating her people against it.

anchors.title: The Dutch plant New Amsterdam
anchors.summary: The West India Company builds its North American capital at the tip of Manhattan, bought from Lenape leaders in a transaction the two sides understood differently.

anchors.title: Harvey describes the circulation of blood
anchors.summary: Measurement rather than authority shows that the heart pumps the same blood around a closed circuit, and Galenic physiology loses its foundation.

anchors.title: The Dutch seize Pernambuco
anchors.summary: West India Company forces take Brazil's richest sugar province and hold it for twenty-four years, learning plantation methods they will carry to the Caribbean.

anchors.title: Magdeburg is sacked and burned
anchors.summary: An imperial army storms the city and fire consumes it; some twenty thousand inhabitants die, and the war's cost to civilians becomes its defining fact.

anchors.title: Work begins on the Taj Mahal
anchors.summary: Shah Jahan commits imperial revenues and twenty years of labor to a tomb for Mumtaz Mahal on the Yamuna at Agra.

anchors.title: Galileo is condemned in Rome
anchors.summary: The Inquisition makes the old astronomer abjure the motion of the earth and confines him for life; the best Italian natural philosophy is published abroad thereafter.

anchors.title: Hong Taiji proclaims the Qing
anchors.summary: Nurhaci's son renames the Jurchen state Qing, claims the imperial title at Shenyang, and forces Korea out of Ming allegiance into tribute to the new house.

anchors.title: Descartes publishes the Discourse
anchors.summary: Method, systematic doubt, and a plane of coordinates arrive in one French volume; algebra and geometry become a single subject.

anchors.title: The Dutch take Elmina castle
anchors.summary: The Gold Coast's main Portuguese fort changes hands, and the Dutch inherit its gold trade and its growing traffic in captives.

anchors.title: Russian cossacks reach the Pacific
anchors.summary: Moskvitin's party comes out on the Sea of Okhotsk sixty years after the crossing of the Urals; a fur frontier has carried Moscow's claim across a continent.

anchors.title: Japan expels the Portuguese
anchors.summary: The bakufu bars Portuguese ships and forbids Japanese departure, leaving Dutch and Chinese traders at Nagasaki as the country's only regulated window abroad.

anchors.title: Zuhab fixes the Ottoman-Persian border
anchors.summary: A century and a half of war ends with Mesopotamia Ottoman and the Caucasus divided, on a line that still roughly marks Iraq from Iran.

anchors.title: Portugal breaks from the Spanish crown
anchors.summary: A coup in Lisbon puts the Duke of Braganza on the throne and opens twenty-eight years of war to make the separation from Madrid stick.

anchors.title: The VOC takes Malacca
anchors.summary: After a five-month siege the strait's chokepoint passes from Portugal to the Dutch company, and Portuguese Asia is reduced to scattered remnants.

anchors.title: England's civil war begins
anchors.summary: King and parliament raise armies over taxes, religion, and who commands the militia; the quarrel will kill a larger share of the English than any later war.

anchors.title: Tasman charts Tasmania and New Zealand
anchors.summary: A Dutch company voyage sights Van Diemen's Land and the New Zealand coast, where four of its crew are killed, and Europe learns the southern land has an edge.

anchors.title: Barbados turns to sugar
anchors.summary: Planters adopt Brazilian methods and Dutch credit, replace indentured servants with enslaved Africans, and make one small island the model for Caribbean society.

anchors.title: Torricelli weighs the atmosphere
anchors.summary: A sealed tube of mercury leaves an empty space at its top, evidence both that air has weight and that a vacuum can be made after all.

anchors.title: The Qing take Beijing
anchors.summary: Manchu banners ride through a rebel-opened gate; China's last dynasty begins.

anchors.title: The Qing order the queue
anchors.summary: Han men are given ten days to shave the forehead and braid the queue or lose their heads; resistance in the Yangtze towns is answered with massacre.

anchors.title: The Peace of Westphalia
anchors.summary: Exhausted powers settle religion and territory in the Empire and confirm the princes' rights; later theorists read the treaties as the charter of the sovereign state system.

anchors.title: Charles I is executed at Whitehall
anchors.summary: A court of parliament's making tries a king for waging war on his own people and beheads him; England is declared a commonwealth without king or lords.

anchors.title: Oyo's cavalry dominate the Yoruba savanna
anchors.summary: Horses bought from the north give the alaafin an army no forest kingdom can match, and tribute and captives flow from the interior toward the coastal trade.

anchors.title: Hobbes publishes Leviathan
anchors.summary: Sovereignty is argued from fear and contract rather than from God or custom, and the state becomes an artificial person its subjects have made.

anchors.title: The Dutch settle the Cape
anchors.summary: A refreshment station for company ships rounding Africa grows into a farming colony, and Khoikhoi herders lose pasture and water to settlers within a generation.

anchors.title: Huygens builds the pendulum clock
anchors.summary: Regulating a clock by a swinging weight cuts daily error from a quarter of an hour to seconds, and exact time becomes an instrument of science.

anchors.title: Aurangzeb takes the Mughal throne
anchors.summary: The third son wins the war of succession, imprisons his father in Agra fort, and turns the empire toward orthodoxy and forty years of campaigning.

anchors.title: The Royal Society is founded
anchors.summary: London gentlemen institutionalize the experiment: nothing by mere authority.

anchors.title: The Stuart monarchy is restored
anchors.summary: Eleven years of republic and army rule end with Charles II invited back on terms, and England settles into a monarchy parliament can bargain with.

anchors.title: Louis XIV rules without a first minister
anchors.summary: On Mazarin's death the young king announces he will govern himself, and France becomes the model absolute monarchy of intendants, standing army, and court.

anchors.title: Koxinga expels the Dutch from Taiwan
anchors.summary: Ming loyalist forces starve Fort Zeelandia into surrender and found a maritime state on Taiwan that outlives its founder by twenty years.

anchors.title: New Amsterdam becomes New York
anchors.summary: An English squadron takes the Dutch colony without a fight, joining New England to the Chesapeake and giving the crown a continuous Atlantic seaboard.

anchors.title: Plague empties London
anchors.summary: Something near a hundred thousand Londoners die within a year, close to a quarter of the city, in the last great bubonic epidemic England will suffer.

anchors.title: Kongo is broken at Mbwila
anchors.summary: A Portuguese-led force kills King Antonio I and much of his court; the kingdom dissolves into rival claimants and its people into the slave trade.

anchors.title: Fire destroys the City of London
anchors.summary: Four days of fire take some thirteen thousand houses and old St Paul's; the city is rebuilt in brick under the first building rules worth the name.

anchors.title: Candia falls and Crete turns Ottoman
anchors.summary: The longest siege of the age ends after twenty-one years with Venice surrendering the island, and the republic's sea empire shrinks to the Ionian islands.

anchors.title: The Royal African Company is chartered
anchors.summary: A crown-backed English monopoly organizes the purchase of captives on the Gold Coast and in Benin, and English ships begin carrying more of them than any rival's.

anchors.title: Leeuwenhoek reports what his lenses show
anchors.summary: A Delft draper who grinds glass better than anyone alive begins writing to the Royal Society, and within three years reports living things too small for any other lens.

anchors.title: Shivaji is crowned chhatrapati
anchors.summary: A Maratha commander who raided Mughal and Bijapuri territory for twenty years has himself enthroned as a sovereign king in the western hills.

anchors.title: Osei Tutu draws the Akan states together
anchors.summary: Kumasi becomes the center of an alliance of Akan chiefdoms whose army and gold will make Asante the dominant power of the forest.

anchors.title: The Pueblo revolt expels Spain
anchors.summary: Coordinated risings across New Mexico kill the missionaries and drive the colonists south to El Paso, and Spanish rule stays out for twelve years.

anchors.title: Louis XIV moves the court to Versailles
anchors.summary: Government settles into a palace built to keep the nobility occupied with ceremony, and absolutism acquires the stage set every rival monarch will copy.

anchors.title: The Ottomans fail before Vienna
anchors.summary: A relief army breaks a two-month siege in a single day, and the Habsburgs turn from defense to a reconquest that takes all Hungary within sixteen years.

anchors.title: France revokes the Edict of Nantes
anchors.summary: Protestant worship is outlawed and its churches pulled down; some two hundred thousand Huguenots leave, taking their trades to England, the Dutch Republic, and Prussia.

anchors.title: Aurangzeb annexes Golconda
anchors.summary: The last Deccan sultanate falls after an eight-month siege; the empire reaches its greatest extent and the limit of what its revenues can garrison.

anchors.title: Newton publishes the Principia
anchors.summary: One set of laws for apples and planets; nature becomes calculable.

anchors.title: The Glorious Revolution
anchors.summary: England imports a king on conditions; parliament and public debt both become permanent.

anchors.title: The English Bill of Rights is enacted
anchors.summary: Parliament makes its own consent the condition of taxes, standing armies, and the suspension of laws, and settles the crown on those terms.

anchors.title: Nerchinsk fixes the Amur frontier
anchors.summary: Russia gives up the Amur valley in exchange for caravan trade with Beijing, in the Qing empire's first treaty negotiated with a European state as an equal.

anchors.title: Famine strikes Louis XIV's France
anchors.summary: Cold, wet weather ruins two harvests running and well over a million people die of hunger and the fevers that follow, the deadliest crisis of the reign.

anchors.title: The Bank of England is founded
anchors.summary: Subscribers lend the state 1.2 million pounds and receive a chartered bank in return; England can now borrow for war at rates its enemies cannot match.

anchors.title: Palmares is destroyed
anchors.summary: Bandeirante troops take the last stronghold of a community of people who had escaped slavery and held the Pernambuco highlands for most of a century.

anchors.title: Sultan Husayn inherits a weakening Iran
anchors.summary: The last effective Safavid shah takes a throne whose army, revenue, and frontier garrisons have decayed, and Afghan invaders will end the dynasty within thirty years.

anchors.title: Oman takes Fort Jesus at Mombasa
anchors.summary: A siege of nearly three years ends Portuguese rule on the northern Swahili coast, and Omani merchants take over its ports and its trade in ivory and captives.

anchors.title: Karlowitz ends the Ottoman advance
anchors.summary: For the first time the sultan negotiates as a defeated power, ceding Hungary and Transylvania to the Habsburgs, the Morea to Venice, and Podolia to Poland.

anchors.title: The Atlantic slave trade nears its peak
anchors.summary: The plantation complex moves millions of Africans in chains; sugar and cotton price in the suffering.

anchors.title: Edo's townsman culture flowers
anchors.summary: A million-person city of clerks and craftsmen invents kabuki seasons, print celebrity, and takeout food.

anchors.title: Asante breaks Denkyira at Feyiase
anchors.summary: Osei Tutu's union of Akan states wins its independence and the roads to the coast, founding an empire that will hold the forest gold trade for two centuries.

anchors.title: The War of the Spanish Succession begins
anchors.summary: Europe spends twelve years fighting over who inherits Spain, and settles that no dynasty may swallow another's empire whole.

anchors.title: Peter founds Saint Petersburg
anchors.summary: A capital is driven into Baltic marshland by conscripted labor, giving Russia a naval base, a window on Europe, and a court that faces west.

anchors.title: England and Scotland unite
anchors.summary: One parliament, one market, one flag for the island that is about to run the seas.

anchors.title: Aurangzeb dies and Mughal authority fragments
anchors.summary: Twenty-six years of campaigning in the Deccan leave the treasury spent and the provinces armed; governors, Marathas, and trading companies divide what the throne can no longer hold.

anchors.title: Darby smelts iron with coke
anchors.summary: Coalbrookdale frees ironmaking from charcoal and the shrinking woods, tying metal output to coal seams that will not run out for centuries.

anchors.title: Poltava breaks the Swedish empire
anchors.summary: Peter's rebuilt army destroys Charles XII's veterans in Ukraine, and within a dozen years the Baltic order passes from Stockholm to Russia.

anchors.title: Newcomen's engine pumps a mine
anchors.summary: Fire lifts water in Staffordshire, inefficiently, profitably, and portentously.

anchors.title: The Peace of Utrecht
anchors.summary: A Bourbon keeps Spain on condition that he never inherit France, Britain takes Gibraltar and the contract to supply slaves to Spanish America, and balance of power enters treaty language.

anchors.title: The Kyoho reforms begin in Japan
anchors.summary: Yoshimune answers shogunal insolvency with austerity, rice price management, and an eased ban on Western books that lets Dutch learning into Edo.

anchors.title: New Orleans is founded
anchors.summary: France plants a port above the Mississippi delta, giving the whole interior of the continent one outlet and every later power a reason to want it.

anchors.title: Baji Rao leads the Marathas north
anchors.summary: A young peshwa turns a Deccan kingdom into a cavalry confederacy that raids to Delhi and collects a share of Mughal revenue across northern India.

anchors.title: Plague strikes Marseille
anchors.summary: A ship from the Levant lands infection past a hurried quarantine, killing perhaps half the city in what proves to be western Europe's last great plague epidemic.

anchors.title: Brazilian gold reorders the Portuguese empire
anchors.summary: Minas Gerais is made a captaincy as the mines pull the colony's weight south, draw in enslaved Africans by the hundred thousand, and pay for a court in Lisbon that need not tax nobles.

anchors.title: The South Sea Bubble bursts
anchors.summary: A scheme to swap national debt for company shares inflates and collapses in a season, ruining thousands and teaching London its first lesson in manias.

anchors.title: Kangxi's sixty-one year reign ends
anchors.summary: The Qing pass from a conquering dynasty to a governing one, with the southern revolts finished, the Mongol frontier held, and the population climbing fast.

anchors.title: Roggeveen reaches Rapa Nui
anchors.summary: A Dutch squadron sights the island on Easter Sunday and reports its standing statues, beginning the outside contact that will later bring disease and slave raiding.

anchors.title: Afghan armies end Safavid Iran
anchors.summary: Isfahan starves through a six-month siege and the shah hands his crown to the besieger, beginning decades of invasion, partition, and civil war in Iran.

anchors.title: Dahomey conquers Whydah
anchors.summary: Agaja's army takes the busiest slaving port on the Bight of Benin, placing the traffic in captives under one kingdom's control and its army's demand for guns.

anchors.title: Muteferrika prints the first Ottoman books
anchors.summary: A licensed press in Istanbul issues a dictionary in Turkish, permitted only on condition that it never print religious texts, nearly three centuries after Gutenberg.

anchors.title: The Norfolk rotation spreads in English farming
anchors.summary: Turnips and clover replace the fallow year, feeding livestock through winter and raising yields enough to release hands from the land.

anchors.title: Kay patents the flying shuttle
anchors.summary: One weaver can now throw a broad cloth alone, doubling weaving speed and leaving spinners unable to keep the looms supplied.

anchors.title: Linnaeus publishes Systema Naturae
anchors.summary: A ranked scheme of kingdom, class, order, and genus gives naturalists in every country one filing system for the specimens ships keep bringing home.

anchors.title: Nader Shah crowns himself in Iran
anchors.summary: A soldier of common birth ends the Safavid line on the Mughan plain and rebuilds Iran as a war machine that empties its own treasury and breaks apart when he is murdered.

anchors.title: Qianlong takes the Qing throne
anchors.summary: Sixty years of expansion, prosperity, and literary censorship follow, and China's population passes three hundred million before the reign is over.

anchors.title: Nader Shah sacks Delhi
anchors.summary: A Persian army destroys the Mughal one at Karnal, occupies the capital, kills tens of thousands of its people, and carries off the treasury and the Peacock Throne.

anchors.title: The Stono rebellion
anchors.summary: Enslaved men in South Carolina march for Spanish Florida and are hunted down within days; the colony answers with a code restricting movement, assembly, and reading.

anchors.title: Frederick II seizes Silesia
anchors.summary: Prussia takes Austria's richest province without pretext, opening eight years of European war and announcing a new great power built on its army.

anchors.title: The pact at Diriyah founds a Saudi state
anchors.summary: A preacher of strict monotheism and an oasis ruler trade doctrine for protection, joining a movement of religious purification to a dynasty in central Arabia.

anchors.title: Excavation begins at Pompeii
anchors.summary: Buried streets are opened under Bourbon patronage, and a Europe that had only read about antiquity begins digging it up and copying its furniture.

anchors.title: Montesquieu publishes The Spirit of the Laws
anchors.summary: Separated powers are presented as the mechanism of liberty rather than a defect of monarchy, and constitution writers quarry the book for the next century.

anchors.title: Madrid redraws the line in South America
anchors.summary: Spain and Portugal replace the Tordesillas meridian with actual occupation, confirming Portuguese Amazonia and condemning the Guarani mission towns caught on the wrong side.

anchors.title: The Encyclopédie begins publication
anchors.summary: Diderot's contributors put trades, machines, and heresies into alphabetical order for subscribers.

anchors.title: Franklin identifies lightning as electricity
anchors.summary: A kite flown into a Philadelphia storm connects the sky to the laboratory, and the lightning rod goes onto roofs and steeples within months.

anchors.title: Alaungpaya founds the Konbaung dynasty
anchors.summary: A village headman drives the Mon armies out of upper Burma and begins the expansion that will reach Siam, Manipur, and eventually the Qing frontier.

anchors.title: The French and Indian War begins in the Ohio
anchors.summary: A Virginia militia skirmish over a contested forest frontier grows into the American theater of a world war, and colonial soldiers learn what British regulars think of them.

anchors.title: Qing armies destroy the Dzungar khanate
anchors.summary: Campaigns of extermination and the smallpox that followed them kill most of the Dzungar people, ending the last independent steppe power and opening Xinjiang to Qing rule.

anchors.title: The Lisbon earthquake
anchors.summary: A capital falls on All Saints' morning; European philosophy takes the aftershock personally.

anchors.title: The Seven Years War begins
anchors.summary: Fighting spreads from Bohemia to Bengal to the Ohio valley; Britain ends it paramount at sea and France loses its North American empire.

anchors.title: European trade is confined to Canton
anchors.summary: Qianlong restricts foreign merchants to one port and a licensed guild of brokers, a bottleneck that holds until British warships force the coast open in the next century.

anchors.title: Plassey delivers Bengal to a company
anchors.summary: The East India Company converts a bribed battle into the revenues of a province, and then of an empire.

anchors.title: Voltaire publishes Candide
anchors.summary: A short brutal comedy of earthquake, war, and slavery makes philosophical optimism look like an excuse, and its author the most read critic in Europe.

anchors.title: Quebec falls on the Plains of Abraham
anchors.summary: Half an hour of musketry outside the walls decides the fate of French North America, and both commanders die of the wounds they take in it.

anchors.title: The Bridgewater Canal opens
anchors.summary: Coal floats from Worsley to Manchester at half the old price, and Britain starts digging the canal network that heavy industry will need.

anchors.title: The third battle of Panipat
anchors.summary: Afghan and Rohilla armies break the Maratha host north of Delhi in a single day, ending the confederacy's bid to inherit the Mughal empire outright.

anchors.title: Rousseau publishes The Social Contract
anchors.summary: Legitimacy is relocated from kings to the general will, an argument that will be quoted in every revolutionary assembly of the next fifty years.

anchors.title: Britain draws the Proclamation Line
anchors.summary: After a season of Indigenous war in the west, London forbids settlement beyond the Appalachian crest, and the colonists who wanted that land read the ban as a grievance.

anchors.title: Buxar makes the Company a revenue power
anchors.summary: Defeating the Mughal emperor and two nawabs wins the Company, within a year, the right to collect Bengal's land tax, and a trading firm becomes the treasury of tens of millions.

anchors.title: Hargreaves builds the spinning jenny
anchors.summary: One worker turns eight spindles at once, ending the yarn shortage that held back the looms and beginning the removal of spinning from the cottage.

anchors.title: Burmese armies destroy Ayutthaya
anchors.summary: Four centuries of Siamese capital are burned and its people carried off, and the surviving state is rebuilt downriver under a new dynasty within a year.

anchors.title: Spain expels the Jesuits from its empire
anchors.summary: Charles III expels the order by sealed decree, closing colleges and mission towns from Paraguay to California and handing the crown their estates and their pupils.

anchors.title: Arkwright patents the water frame
anchors.summary: Rollers driven by a waterwheel spin thread strong enough for warp, making all-cotton cloth possible and putting spinning where the rivers are.

anchors.title: Famine empties much of Bengal
anchors.summary: Two failed monsoons meet undiminished revenue demands and grain hoarding; contemporaries reckon a third of the province dead, and the Company's rule is argued about in London.

anchors.title: Cook charts the Pacific
anchors.summary: Three voyages map the ocean's last blank spaces, and open every island on them to empire.

anchors.title: Cromford mill puts spinning under one roof
anchors.summary: Arkwright hires whole families to keep water-driven machines running in shifts through the night, and the factory becomes a way of organizing work.

anchors.title: The first partition of Poland
anchors.summary: Russia, Prussia, and Austria each take a slice of a working kingdom by agreement, and the powers learn that dismemberment can be negotiated instead of fought over.

anchors.title: Tea is destroyed in Boston harbor
anchors.summary: Colonists tip an East India Company cargo into the water rather than pay its duty, and parliament's punitive answer turns thirteen quarrels into one.

anchors.title: Kaitai Shinsho translates Dutch anatomy
anchors.summary: Edo physicians check a Dutch atlas against a dissection, find the inherited charts wrong, and give Japanese scholars an appetite for Western science.

anchors.title: Kucuk Kaynarca opens the Black Sea
anchors.summary: A beaten Ottoman government detaches Crimea, admits Russian shipping through the straits, and concedes a claim to protect Orthodox subjects that Russia will use for a century.

anchors.title: American independence is declared
anchors.summary: Thirteen colonies secede on Enlightenment credit and win with French help.

anchors.title: Watt's improved engine goes to work
anchors.summary: A separate condenser turns steam from a pump into a prime mover for anything.

anchors.title: Smith publishes The Wealth of Nations
anchors.summary: The division of labor gets its theorist; political economy becomes a discipline.

anchors.title: Saratoga brings France into the war
anchors.summary: A British army surrenders in upstate New York, and the rebellion gains a great power's fleet, money, and troops within four months.

anchors.title: War opens on the Cape's eastern frontier
anchors.summary: Dutch stock farmers and Xhosa chiefdoms fight over grazing along the Fish River, beginning a hundred years of frontier wars for the same pastures.

anchors.title: Tupac Amaru II rises in Peru
anchors.summary: A Cuzco curaca leads Andean villages against tribute and forced mine labor; the rising is crushed with tens of thousands dead and Inca titles and dress banned outright.

anchors.title: Kant publishes the Critique of Pure Reason
anchors.summary: Knowledge is recast as the mind's own shaping of experience, and German philosophy acquires the problem it will work on for a hundred years.

anchors.title: Yorktown ends the fighting in America
anchors.summary: A French fleet closes the bay while two armies close the land side, and Cornwallis surrenders an army Britain cannot replace across an ocean.

anchors.title: The Zong killings
anchors.summary: The crew of a Liverpool slave ship throw more than 130 people into the sea and claim on the insurance, and the resulting suit puts the trade's arithmetic before the British public.

anchors.title: Cort patents puddling and rolling
anchors.summary: Coal-fired stirring converts pig iron into wrought iron in bulk, so bars, boilers, and machine frames can be made without charcoal or hand hammering.

anchors.title: Jones links Sanskrit to Greek and Latin
anchors.summary: A judge in Calcutta argues that three distant languages descend from a common source now lost, and comparative philology begins as a discipline.

anchors.title: London's abolition committee organizes
anchors.summary: Twelve men, nine of them Quakers, begin a campaign of petitions, sworn testimony, and sugar boycott that turns the slave trade into a public question.

anchors.title: The United States Constitution is drafted
anchors.summary: Delegates in Philadelphia replace a failing confederation with a federal government of divided powers, and buy southern agreement with clauses that protect slavery without naming it.

anchors.title: The First Fleet lands at Sydney Cove
anchors.summary: Britain founds a convict colony on the far side of the world, on country taken without treaty or purchase from the people already living on it.

anchors.title: The French Revolution begins
anchors.summary: A bankrupt monarchy summons the estates and receives a nation instead; every European order takes note.

anchors.title: Smallpox devastates the peoples of Port Jackson
anchors.summary: An epidemic kills perhaps half the Eora and their neighbors within a year of the colony's founding, emptying camps around the harbor before the frontier has moved at all.

anchors.title: The Haitian revolution begins
anchors.summary: The enslaved of Saint-Domingue rise and, uniquely, win, founding a state and terrifying every slaveholding power.

anchors.title: Wollstonecraft claims the rights of woman
anchors.summary: The revolution's language is turned on the education of women, arguing that their dependence is trained into them rather than natural.

anchors.title: Whitney's gin makes short-staple cotton pay
anchors.summary: A simple comb cleans seed from upland cotton dozens of times faster, and slavery expands west into land where it had looked unprofitable.

anchors.title: The Terror governs France
anchors.summary: The republic answers invasion and revolt with emergency committees, price controls, and mass executions, killing tens of thousands before it turns on its own organizers.

anchors.title: The Macartney embassy is refused
anchors.summary: Britain asks for resident envoys and open ports; Qianlong answers that the empire lacks nothing and needs no foreign manufactures, and both sides go on misreading each other.

anchors.title: The Permanent Settlement fixes Bengal's revenue
anchors.summary: Cornwallis makes zamindars proprietors at a rent set forever, creating a landlord class with an interest in British rule and a tenantry with no security under it.

anchors.title: Kamehameha wins Oahu at Nuuanu
anchors.summary: Cannon and muskets bought from passing ships help one chief defeat his rivals and bring nearly all the Hawaiian islands under a single kingdom.

anchors.title: The third partition erases Poland
anchors.summary: What remains of the commonwealth is divided among three monarchies, and a large European nation spends the next 123 years without a state of its own.

anchors.title: Jenner demonstrates vaccination
anchors.summary: Cowpox against smallpox: the first standardized defeat of a disease begins.

anchors.title: Park reaches the Niger at Segu
anchors.summary: A Scottish surgeon confirms that the great river runs east, and European geography acquires a target for fifty years of expeditions and the claims that follow them.

anchors.title: The White Lotus rebellion begins
anchors.summary: Tax-pressed migrants in the mountain borderlands rise for nine years, revealing an army gone slack and a treasury far emptier than the reign's reputation suggested.

anchors.title: Bonaparte invades Egypt
anchors.summary: A French army beats the Mamluks and is then stranded when Nelson burns its fleet, but the scholars it brought begin the survey that founds Egyptology.

anchors.title: Malthus publishes his Essay on Population
anchors.summary: Population is argued to press permanently against the food supply, giving political economy its grim arithmetic and its longest running quarrel.

anchors.title: Bonaparte seizes power on 18 Brumaire
anchors.summary: A victorious general and his allies dissolve the Directory at bayonet point, ending ten years of revolution in a consulate he will shortly head alone.

anchors.title: Ranjit Singh takes Lahore
anchors.summary: A young misl chief seizes the Punjab's capital and begins welding the Sikh confederacies into the one Indian state the Company will not absorb for fifty years.

anchors.title: The Dutch East India Company is wound up
anchors.summary: Debt, private trading, and lost wars finish the corporation that invented the joint-stock empire, and its Asian ports and monopolies pass directly to the Dutch state.

anchors.title: Volta builds the electric pile
anchors.summary: Stacked discs of zinc and silver in brine give the first steady current, and electricity stops being a spectacle and becomes an instrument.

anchors.title: Britain and Ireland are joined in one kingdom
anchors.summary: The Dublin parliament votes itself out of existence and Irish members sit at Westminster instead; Catholic emancipation is promised with the union and then withheld for a generation.

anchors.title: The Louisiana Purchase
anchors.summary: France sells half a continent to fund a war; the United States doubles overnight.

anchors.title: Lewis and Clark start up the Missouri
anchors.summary: An army expedition is sent to find a water route to the Pacific; it returns without one, but with maps, specimens, and the report that the West is reachable overland.

anchors.title: Napoleon crowns himself emperor of the French
anchors.summary: The republic becomes a hereditary empire in Notre-Dame; the revolution's institutions survive inside a monarchy that must keep winning wars to justify itself.

anchors.title: The Napoleonic Code is promulgated
anchors.summary: France replaces a patchwork of local customs with one civil code on property, contract, and family, plain enough for a clerk to read and exported wherever French armies go.

anchors.title: Usman dan Fodio's jihad founds the Sokoto caliphate
anchors.summary: A scholar's rising against the Hausa kings builds the largest state in nineteenth-century Africa, ruled from Sokoto through emirs and a written body of Islamic law.

anchors.title: Austerlitz breaks the Third Coalition
anchors.summary: Napoleon destroys a joint Russian and Austrian army in a single December day; Austria signs peace within the month and the old German order loses its protector.

anchors.title: Muhammad Ali takes power in Egypt
anchors.summary: An Albanian officer of the Ottoman army is acclaimed governor by Cairo's notables and begins building a conscript army, state monopolies, and factories on European models.

anchors.title: Trafalgar
anchors.summary: Nelson's fleet settles a century's question: the seas are British.

anchors.title: Britain takes the Cape of Good Hope
anchors.summary: The Dutch colony at the Cape passes permanently to British hands as a naval station on the route to India, and its Dutch-speaking farmers acquire a government they did not choose.

anchors.title: The Continental System closes Europe to British trade
anchors.summary: Decrees from Berlin bar British goods from the continent; smuggling, shortage, and the wars fought to enforce the ban cost Napoleon's allies more than they cost Britain.

anchors.title: The Holy Roman Empire is dissolved
anchors.summary: Francis II lays down a crown a thousand years old rather than see Napoleon wear it; the German lands are consolidated into fewer, larger, and more governable states.

anchors.title: Steamboats begin scheduled service on the Hudson
anchors.summary: Fulton's boat runs New York to Albany against the current on a published schedule; within twenty years steam is working upstream on the Mississippi and turning the interior toward market.

anchors.title: Britain abolishes the slave trade
anchors.summary: The world's largest slaving power outlaws the traffic and sets its navy against it, slowly, and for mixed motives.

anchors.title: The Portuguese court moves to Rio de Janeiro
anchors.summary: Fleeing Napoleon under British escort, the monarchy governs its empire from Brazil and opens Brazilian ports to foreign ships; the colony acquires a capital it will not give back.

anchors.title: Spain rises against French occupation
anchors.summary: A Madrid revolt opens six years of siege, guerrilla, and British intervention; with its king a prisoner, Spain's American colonies lose the government they were obeying.

anchors.title: The United States bans the import of slaves
anchors.summary: The Atlantic traffic to American ports is outlawed at the earliest date the constitution allowed; the enslaved population keeps growing, and a domestic trade carries people south instead.

anchors.title: Spanish America begins its independence wars
anchors.summary: Napoleon's occupation of Spain snaps the imperial chain; juntas from Caracas to Buenos Aires stop waiting.

anchors.title: A rising shakes northern Korea
anchors.summary: Merchants, miners, and farmers of Pyongan province rebel against a court that taxes their region and bars its men from high office; they hold a walled town for months before it is mined and stormed.

anchors.title: The Grande Armee is destroyed in Russia
anchors.summary: Six hundred thousand men cross the Niemen, reach a burning Moscow, and retreat through the winter; a small fraction return, and with them go Napoleon's veterans and his reputation.

anchors.title: The United States declares war on Britain
anchors.summary: Impressment at sea and land hunger in the west bring a second Anglo-American war that moves no border, burns Washington, and ends organized Native resistance east of the Mississippi.

anchors.title: Settlers cross the Blue Mountains
anchors.summary: A route over the ranges west of Sydney opens grass plains to sheep runs; the colony stops being a coastal prison and begins taking the interior from the people living on it.

anchors.title: The Company's Indian trade monopoly ends
anchors.summary: Parliament opens India to private British merchants and to missionaries, and orders the Company to spend a yearly sum on education; commerce and conversion arrive on the same ships.

anchors.title: Leipzig drives the French out of Germany
anchors.summary: The largest battle Europe has yet fought ends with Napoleon's army retreating over the Rhine; his German allies change sides and the coalition does not break again.

anchors.title: The German Confederation replaces the old empire
anchors.summary: Thirty-nine states are bound in a loose league under Austrian presidency, strong enough to suppress agitation and too weak to govern; the German question stays open for fifty years.

anchors.title: Tambora erupts
anchors.summary: The largest eruption in recorded history yellows skies worldwide and cancels the next summer's harvests.

anchors.title: Waterloo and the Vienna settlement
anchors.summary: Napoleon's last army breaks; the powers redraw Europe for a century of managed balance.

anchors.title: Shaka builds the Zulu kingdom
anchors.summary: Regiments organized by age and drilled for close combat turn a small chiefdom into the dominant power between the Tugela and the Pongola in under a decade.

anchors.title: The United Provinces declare independence at Tucuman
anchors.summary: Delegates from the provinces of the Rio de la Plata renounce Spanish rule outright; the state they name will need another half century of civil war to agree on its borders and its capital.

anchors.title: Cholera leaves the Ganges delta
anchors.summary: An outbreak in Bengal follows marching armies and merchant shipping outward and becomes the first of seven global pandemics; it reaches Russia and Britain within fifteen years.

anchors.title: San Martin crosses the Andes into Chile
anchors.summary: An army of five thousand hauls guns over passes above three thousand metres and wins at Chacabuco within weeks; Chile is freed, and the campaign turns north by sea toward Peru.

anchors.title: Egyptian troops destroy the first Saudi state
anchors.summary: Ibrahim Pasha takes Diriyah after a long siege and razes it; Wahhabi rule over the holy cities ends for a generation and the sultan's authority in Arabia is restored on paper.

anchors.title: The Maratha confederacy is broken
anchors.summary: The last Anglo-Maratha war ends with the peshwa pensioned off and his territories annexed; the East India Company is now the paramount power from the southern tip to the Sutlej.

anchors.title: Bolivar wins at Boyaca and founds Gran Colombia
anchors.summary: A march across flooded plains and the Andes surprises the royalists at Boyaca and Bogota falls in three days; a congress then unites Venezuela, New Granada, and Quito in one republic.

anchors.title: The Mfecane uproots southern Africa
anchors.summary: War, drought, and flight scatter peoples across the highveld and far beyond it; new kingdoms including Lesotho and the Ndebele form from the survivors, and emptied land is later read as unclaimed.

anchors.title: Raffles founds a free port at Singapore
anchors.summary: A trading post on a lightly settled island is declared free of duties; within fifty years it commands the traffic of the straits and draws migrants from China, India, and the archipelago.

anchors.title: Long-staple cotton becomes Egypt's crop
anchors.summary: A variety noticed in a Cairo garden is planted across the delta under state monopoly; Egyptian fields are turned to an export the mills of Lancashire will pay for, and to the debt that follows it.

anchors.title: Greece rises against Ottoman rule
anchors.summary: Risings in the Morea begin eight years of massacre and reprisal on both sides, which educated European opinion reads as ancient Hellas returning to life.

anchors.title: Brazil declares independence under its own prince
anchors.summary: Pedro refuses Lisbon's order to come home and is crowned emperor of a Brazil that separates without a general war, keeping its monarchy, its slavery, and its territory whole.

anchors.title: The Monroe Doctrine warns Europe off the Americas
anchors.summary: A presidential message declares the hemisphere closed to new colonization; for decades the Royal Navy does the enforcing, and later Washington reads the doctrine as a licence of its own.

anchors.title: Ayacucho ends Spanish rule in South America
anchors.summary: A royalist army is beaten in the Peruvian highlands and its viceroy taken prisoner; three centuries of Spanish government on the continent end in the surrender terms signed that afternoon.

anchors.title: The Decembrist revolt fails in Petersburg
anchors.summary: Officers who saw constitutional Europe on campaign refuse the new tsar's oath and are dispersed by artillery in an afternoon; Nicholas I governs by political police for thirty years.

anchors.title: The Erie Canal links the Hudson to the Great Lakes
anchors.summary: Three hundred and sixty miles of ditch cut the cost of moving a ton of wheat from Buffalo to New York by roughly nine tenths, and make New York the continent's port.

anchors.title: Japan orders foreign ships driven off
anchors.summary: The shogunate directs coastal domains to fire on any Western vessel that comes near without waiting to ask its business; seclusion becomes a standing military instruction.

anchors.title: The first public railway opens
anchors.summary: Stockton to Darlington by steam: distance begins its long discount.

anchors.title: Mahmud II destroys the Janissary corps
anchors.summary: The sultan's new artillery fires on the mutinous barracks in Istanbul and the corps is abolished by decree; the empire loses its oldest army and gains the freedom to conscript another.

anchors.title: Allied fleets destroy an Ottoman navy at Navarino
anchors.summary: British, French, and Russian squadrons sink an Ottoman and Egyptian fleet in a bay of the Morea, an action their governments had not quite ordered; Greek independence becomes unstoppable.

anchors.title: Catholics may sit in the British parliament
anchors.summary: Facing an Irish county that has elected a man barred from taking his seat, Wellington's government concedes emancipation rather than risk a rising, and splits its own party doing it.

anchors.title: Bengal outlaws the burning of widows
anchors.summary: A regulation makes sati a criminal act, urged by Indian reformers and resented by others as intrusion; colonial government has begun legislating on religious practice.

anchors.title: France takes Algiers
anchors.summary: An expedition sent over an unpaid grain debt and a slighted consul captures the city; what follows is forty years of conquest and a settler colony administered as part of France.

anchors.title: The powers recognize an independent Greece
anchors.summary: A protocol signed in London makes Greece a sovereign kingdom under great-power guarantee; the Ottoman empire has lost a province to nationalism, and every Balkan capital takes the lesson.

anchors.title: Congress authorizes Indian removal
anchors.summary: The act empowers the president to exchange eastern homelands for territory west of the Mississippi; treaties signed under pressure follow, and then forced marches under military escort.

anchors.title: Java is put under the Cultivation System
anchors.summary: Dutch administrators require villages to plant a fifth of their land in coffee, sugar, and indigo for the state; the proceeds balance the budget in the Netherlands and hunger follows the quotas.

anchors.title: The July Revolution unseats the Bourbons
anchors.summary: Three days of Paris barricades replace Charles X with a king who reigns by charter rather than by right; Europe's restored monarchies learn that they are negotiable.

anchors.title: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway opens
anchors.summary: The first line built to carry passengers between two cities entirely by locomotive runs to a printed timetable; within a decade Britain is laying track by the hundred miles.

anchors.title: Faraday discovers electromagnetic induction
anchors.summary: A magnet moved through a coil of wire makes a current; the bench demonstration contains, in principle, every dynamo, transformer, and electric motor that follows.

anchors.title: Mazzini founds Young Italy
anchors.summary: An exile in Marseille organizes a society pledged to win a united Italian republic by insurrection; its conspiracies fail for thirty years and its idea outlives every one of them.

anchors.title: The Reform Act redraws Britain's franchise
anchors.summary: Rotten boroughs are abolished and seats go to the manufacturing towns; the vote still reaches only about one adult man in five, so further reform becomes a question of when.

anchors.title: Britain limits child labour in the textile mills
anchors.summary: Children under nine are barred from the mills, older children's hours are capped, and salaried inspectors are appointed to see the law kept; the state accepts that it may set the terms of employment.

anchors.title: Britain abolishes slavery in its colonies
anchors.summary: Some eight hundred thousand people in the Caribbean and at the Cape are freed into years of unpaid apprenticeship, while the Treasury borrows twenty million pounds to compensate their owners.

anchors.title: The Tenpo famine empties Japanese villages
anchors.summary: Cold summers and failed rice harvests bring years of hunger, rural flight to the cities, and hundreds of riots against grain dealers that leave the shogunate looking incapable.

anchors.title: The Zollverein makes a single German market
anchors.summary: Prussia's customs union drops tolls between most German states; goods move as though the country already existed, and the politics follow the freight.

anchors.title: The Beagle reaches the Galapagos
anchors.summary: A young naturalist on a survey of South American coasts collects finches, mockingbirds, and tortoises that differ island by island; the puzzle he takes home is more than twenty years from publication.

anchors.title: Boer farmers trek out of the Cape Colony
anchors.summary: Thousands of Dutch-speaking families leave with wagons and herds after emancipation and frontier policy turn against them; the republics they plant inland will shape South African politics for a century.

anchors.title: English becomes the language of Indian instruction
anchors.summary: Macaulay's minute persuades the government to fund schooling in English rather than Sanskrit or Persian, in order to produce a class of clerks Indian in descent and English in taste.

anchors.title: Texas breaks away from Mexico
anchors.summary: Anglo settlers and Tejano allies declare a republic and secure it by capturing Santa Anna at San Jacinto; its constitution keeps slavery legal, and annexation nine years later brings war with Mexico.

anchors.title: The electric telegraph is patented in Britain
anchors.summary: Cooke and Wheatstone's needle instrument is strung along a railway line, and the wire's first employment is keeping trains from meeting on the same track.

anchors.title: Voortrekker guns defeat a Zulu army at Blood River
anchors.summary: Firearms fired from behind a ring of wagons break a much larger force at almost no cost to the settlers; the date becomes a founding observance of Afrikaner nationalism.

anchors.title: Chartism demands the vote for working men
anchors.summary: Six points, universal male suffrage and the secret ballot among them, are published as a charter, and petitions carrying millions of signatures follow; every point but annual parliaments is law within eighty years.

anchors.title: The Cherokee are marched west under guard
anchors.summary: Sixteen thousand people are removed from Georgia to Indian Territory in stockades and winter columns; roughly a quarter die of exposure, hunger, and disease along the way.

anchors.title: The daguerreotype makes the first public photographs
anchors.summary: France buys Daguerre's process and releases it to the world; a silvered plate now records a face or a street more exactly than any draughtsman can.

anchors.title: The First Opium War begins
anchors.summary: Commissioner Lin destroys twenty thousand chests of confiscated British opium at Canton; the fleet sent in answer outguns the Qing coast at will.

anchors.title: The Gulhane edict opens the Tanzimat
anchors.summary: The sultan promises security of life and property, regular taxation, and equal standing before the law to all subjects whatever their religion; Ottoman reform becomes a written programme.

anchors.title: The powers force Egypt out of Syria
anchors.summary: Muhammad Ali's army had taken Syria and pushed deep into Anatolia; a European convention and a naval blockade force it back, and he settles for hereditary rule of Egypt alone.

anchors.title: The Treaty of Waitangi is signed
anchors.summary: Maori chiefs and the Crown sign texts that do not say the same thing in both languages; Britain claims sovereignty, the chiefs understood a governorship, and the gap is still being litigated.

anchors.title: Chadwick reports on the sanitary state of the towns
anchors.summary: A survey of drains, cellars, and burial grounds ties early death to filth rather than to vice, and turns sewers into an argument the Treasury can be made to cost.

anchors.title: Japan softens its order to repel foreign ships
anchors.summary: News that British gunboats have humbled the Qing persuades the shogunate to let foreign vessels take on firewood and water instead of shot; seclusion is now a policy that knows its own price.

anchors.title: The Treaty of Nanking opens the treaty ports
anchors.summary: Five ports are opened to British merchants, Hong Kong is ceded, and a fixed tariff and large indemnity are imposed; a century of treaties written on foreign terms begins aboard a warship.

anchors.title: Brunel launches the first great iron steamship
anchors.summary: The Great Britain is hulled in iron and driven by a screw propeller instead of paddles; both choices become standard, and the Atlantic settles into a scheduled two-week passage.

anchors.title: Morse telegraphs Washington to Baltimore
anchors.summary: News detaches from horses; markets and ministries synchronize by wire.

anchors.title: The United States wins the same terms at Wanghia
anchors.summary: Washington's treaty adds explicit extraterritoriality to the privileges taken at Nanking, and Paris follows at Whampoa; foreigners in China now answer to their own consuls, not to Chinese courts.

anchors.title: The Great Famine begins in Ireland
anchors.summary: Blight meets doctrine; a million die and two million leave while grain is exported under guard.

anchors.title: Britain repeals the Corn Laws
anchors.summary: Peel abandons agricultural protection during the Irish famine and shatters his party; cheap imported grain becomes the price Britain pays for being a workshop rather than a farm.

anchors.title: Ether takes the pain out of surgery
anchors.summary: A Boston dentist renders a patient insensible before the knife in a public demonstration; within a year surgeons on both sides of the Atlantic operate without agony on either side of the table.

anchors.title: The United States invades Mexico
anchors.summary: A clash on the disputed Rio Grande opens a war carried to the Mexican capital; Mexico loses about half its territory, and the American union gains a question about slavery it cannot settle by vote.

anchors.title: Liberia declares itself a republic
anchors.summary: Settlers sent from the United States by a colonization society proclaim Africa's first modern republic, and govern indigenous neighbours who never agreed to their arrival.

anchors.title: The 1848 revolutions sweep Europe
anchors.summary: Barricades from Paris to Vienna win constitutions in the spring that armies revoke by winter.

anchors.title: The Communist Manifesto is published
anchors.summary: Marx and Engels hand the year's revolutionaries a pamphlet most of them never read, and the next century a vocabulary of class that it cannot argue without.

anchors.title: Seneca Falls demands the vote for women
anchors.summary: A convention in upstate New York issues a declaration of sentiments modelled on 1776; its suffrage resolution passes narrowly and takes seventy-two years to become constitutional law.

anchors.title: The Punjab is annexed after the Sikh wars
anchors.summary: Two hard-fought wars end the empire Ranjit Singh assembled; the Company takes the last independent power in India, along with the Koh-i-noor diamond and the Sikh regiments it will soon recruit.

anchors.title: The Taiping rebellion begins
anchors.summary: A failed examination candidate's heavenly kingdom drags China into the deadliest civil war ever fought.

anchors.title: The Australian gold rushes begin
anchors.summary: Payable gold near Bathurst and then across Victoria draws migrants from three continents and more than triples the settler population within twenty years.

anchors.title: The Great Exhibition opens in Hyde Park
anchors.summary: A hall of iron and glass holds the manufactures of the world, and six million visitors learn to read industry as public spectacle.

anchors.title: Britain recognizes the Transvaal republic
anchors.summary: The Sand River Convention concedes self-government to Boer settlers north of the Vaal, planting republics that a later war will destroy.

anchors.title: Argentina adopts a federal constitution
anchors.summary: A year after Rosas falls at Caseros the provinces accept a federal charter; Buenos Aires stays outside it for six more years.

anchors.title: India's first railway runs out of Bombay
anchors.summary: Twenty-one miles of track to Thane begin a network laid for cotton, troops, and revenue that will grow into the largest railway system in Asia.

anchors.title: Perry's squadron enters Edo Bay
anchors.summary: Four American ships end Japanese seclusion by arithmetic of gun calibers.

anchors.title: Britain mandates smallpox vaccination
anchors.summary: The state requires a medical procedure of every infant; public health and civil liberty begin their long argument.

anchors.title: Snow traces cholera to a single pump
anchors.summary: A London doctor maps deaths house by house, has the Broad Street handle removed, and gives epidemiology its method before anyone can see the microbe.

anchors.title: Britain and France enter the Crimean war
anchors.summary: Two western powers fight Russia to keep the Ottoman empire standing, and the siege of Sevastopol kills more of their soldiers by disease than by shot.

anchors.title: The Kansas-Nebraska Act reopens the slavery question
anchors.summary: Repealing the Missouri Compromise puts slavery to a settlers' vote, fills Kansas with armed partisans, and calls the Republican party into being.

anchors.title: Nightingale reorganizes the Scutari hospitals
anchors.summary: Trained nurses, sanitary works, and carefully kept mortality statistics turn an army barrack hospital into the argument that nursing is a profession with standards.

anchors.title: Bessemer announces cheap steel
anchors.summary: Air blown through iron makes steel by the ton; rails, ships, and skylines follow.

anchors.title: The Ottoman reform edict promises legal equality
anchors.summary: The Islahat Fermani grants non-Muslim subjects equal standing in law, taxation, and office, and satisfies neither the provinces nor the powers that demanded it.

anchors.title: The second Opium war begins
anchors.summary: Britain and France use the seizure of a ship flying the British flag to force wider trade, legalized opium, and resident ministers on the Qing.

anchors.title: The Indian rebellion of 1857
anchors.summary: Sepoy mutiny becomes general revolt; the Company is abolished and the Raj rules directly.

anchors.title: The Xhosa cattle-killing
anchors.summary: Prophecy urges the slaughter of herds and destruction of grain to bring renewal; tens of thousands starve and the Cape colony annexes the emptied land.

anchors.title: The Crown replaces the East India Company
anchors.summary: The Government of India Act transfers a subcontinent from a chartered trading company to a secretary of state, making the Raj a department of British government.

anchors.title: Drake drills the first commercial oil well
anchors.summary: Sixty-nine feet of pipe at Titusville turns rock oil from a curiosity into an industry, first for lamplight and later for engines.

anchors.title: Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species
anchors.summary: Selection without a selector: biology acquires its unifying, unsettling theory.

anchors.title: Garibaldi's thousand land in Sicily
anchors.summary: A volunteer expedition takes Palermo, crosses to the mainland, and delivers the Bourbon south to Piedmont within six months.

anchors.title: The New Zealand wars resume in Taranaki
anchors.summary: A disputed land purchase brings imperial troops against Maori communities, and the fighting ends in confiscations that strip some tribes of most of their territory.

anchors.title: The Summer Palace is looted and burned
anchors.summary: Anglo-French forces occupy the Qing capital and destroy the emperor's garden palaces; the Convention of Peking then opens more ports and cedes Kowloon.

anchors.title: Italy is proclaimed a kingdom
anchors.summary: Cavour's diplomacy and Garibaldi's volunteers stitch the peninsula together under Piedmont.

anchors.title: The Qing begin the self-strengthening movement
anchors.summary: A new foreign office, arsenals, and shipyards import western guns and schools while insisting the Confucian order beneath them stays unchanged.

anchors.title: Russia abolishes serfdom
anchors.summary: Twenty-three million people are unbound by decree, into redemption payments that last generations.

anchors.title: The American civil war begins
anchors.summary: Eleven states secede to protect slavery, the guns open on Fort Sumter, and four years of industrial war kill roughly seven hundred thousand people.

anchors.title: Bismarck takes charge in Prussia
anchors.summary: Appointed to break a budget deadlock, the new minister-president tells the deputies that great questions are settled by iron and blood, then governs without them.

anchors.title: France takes eastern Cochinchina
anchors.summary: The Treaty of Saigon cedes three provinces and opens ports to French trade, the first instalment of an Indochinese empire.

anchors.title: The Emancipation Proclamation
anchors.summary: The American civil war becomes, officially, a war against slavery.

anchors.title: The first Geneva Convention is signed
anchors.summary: Twelve states agree that the wounded and those who tend them are neutral, giving the laws of war their first standing treaty and a recognizable emblem.

anchors.title: Pasteur patents pasteurization
anchors.summary: Gentle heat keeps wine, then milk, from souring; germ theory reaches the kitchen.

anchors.title: Nanjing falls and the Taiping are destroyed
anchors.summary: Provincial armies under Zeng Guofan retake the heavenly capital after fourteen years of war that left perhaps twenty million dead and the provinces armed.

anchors.title: The War of the Triple Alliance begins
anchors.summary: Paraguay fights Brazil, Argentina, and Uruguay for six years, losing much of its territory and, by most estimates, more than half its population.

anchors.title: The Confederacy surrenders and slavery is abolished
anchors.summary: Lee's surrender at Appomattox ends the fighting, and the Thirteenth Amendment ends legal slavery for four million people before the year is out.

anchors.title: Maxwell unifies electricity, magnetism, and light
anchors.summary: A set of field equations predicts waves travelling at the speed of light, and tells physicists that light is one narrow band of a much larger spectrum.

anchors.title: Mendel publishes the rules of inheritance
anchors.summary: Pea crosses in a monastery garden show traits passing as discrete units in fixed ratios; the paper is read by almost no one for thirty-four years.

anchors.title: Canada is confederated
anchors.summary: The British North America Act joins four provinces into a self-governing dominion that reaches the Pacific within a decade.

anchors.title: Marx publishes the first volume of Capital
anchors.summary: A theory of value, accumulation, and recurring crisis gives the labour movement a doctrine and the next century much of its political vocabulary.

anchors.title: Diamonds are found on the Orange River
anchors.summary: A stone picked up near Hopetown starts the rush to Kimberley, and mineral wealth begins pulling British power and migrant labour into the southern African interior.

anchors.title: Lister publishes antiseptic surgery
anchors.summary: Carbolic acid on wounds, hands, and instruments cuts surgical mortality sharply, carrying germ theory from the laboratory into the operating room.

anchors.title: The Fourteenth Amendment defines citizenship
anchors.summary: Birthright citizenship, due process, and equal protection are written into the constitution, then left largely unenforced against the states for ninety years.

anchors.title: The Meiji Restoration
anchors.summary: Japan's young oligarchs abolish their own class and industrialize the country in a generation.

anchors.title: Mendeleev arranges the elements
anchors.summary: Ordering the known elements by weight and property leaves deliberate gaps, and the gaps are filled by elements found later with the predicted characteristics.

anchors.title: The Suez Canal opens
anchors.summary: Europe and Asia move four thousand miles closer; whoever holds the ditch holds the route.

anchors.title: The US transcontinental railroad is joined
anchors.summary: A golden spike closes the gap at Promontory; the continent becomes a week wide.

anchors.title: England provides elementary schools for all
anchors.summary: Elected school boards fill the gaps the churches left, and within two decades attendance is compulsory and near-universal literacy is in sight.

anchors.title: The Franco-Prussian war and Sedan
anchors.summary: A telegram edited for insult brings war; Napoleon III is captured at Sedan within seven weeks and the Second Empire falls two days later.

anchors.title: Germany is unified at Versailles
anchors.summary: Bismarck's wars end with a Prussian king crowned German emperor in a French palace.

anchors.title: The Iwakura mission sails
anchors.summary: Half the Japanese government spends nearly two years inspecting American and European industry, law, and schools, and returns with a programme rather than an impression.

anchors.title: The Paris Commune
anchors.summary: A defeated city governs itself for seventy-two days and is retaken street by street; the repression kills thousands and shapes European politics for a generation.

anchors.title: The crash of 1873 opens the Long Depression
anchors.summary: Railway speculation collapses first in Vienna and then in New York, and two decades of falling prices push governments back toward tariffs and empire.

anchors.title: Zanzibar closes its slave market
anchors.summary: Under British naval pressure the sultan ends the public sale of slaves, though caravans out of the interior continue for another generation.

anchors.title: Japan opens Korea by treaty
anchors.summary: Gunboats off Ganghwa force open ports, extraterritorial courts, and a denial of Chinese suzerainty, placing Korea between two rising claims.

anchors.title: The Great Famine strikes southern India
anchors.summary: Drought, continued grain exports, and a relief policy designed not to undercut wages combine to kill between five and ten million people over three years.

anchors.title: The Ottoman empire adopts a constitution
anchors.summary: A written charter and an elected chamber last little more than a year before the sultan suspends them, but the text remains the reference point for later reformers.

anchors.title: Bell patents the telephone
anchors.summary: The wire learns to carry voices; conversation stops requiring presence.

anchors.title: Federal troops leave the southern states
anchors.summary: A disputed presidential election is settled by withdrawing the garrisons, and within two decades black voters across the former Confederacy are disfranchised.

anchors.title: The Satsuma rebellion is crushed
anchors.summary: A conscript army with rifles, steamships, and telegraphs defeats the last samurai revolt, and the warrior class ceases to be a political force.

anchors.title: The Congress of Berlin redraws the Balkans
anchors.summary: The powers shrink Russia's gains, recognize new Balkan states, and leave a set of national grievances that will still be armed in 1914.

anchors.title: The Anglo-Zulu war
anchors.summary: A Zulu army destroys a British column at Isandlwana; within the year the kingdom is broken into thirteen chiefdoms and its king deposed.

anchors.title: Practical incandescent light
anchors.summary: Edison's filament and his grid make night optional for the paying public.

anchors.title: The War of the Pacific begins
anchors.summary: Chile takes the nitrate coast from Peru and Bolivia, gaining a fertilizer monopoly and leaving Bolivia without a seaport.

anchors.title: Alexander II is assassinated
anchors.summary: A bomb on a St Petersburg canal kills the tsar who freed the serfs; his successor answers with repression and reform in Russia stops for a generation.

anchors.title: France makes Tunisia a protectorate
anchors.summary: Debt, a frontier raid, and Bismarck's quiet encouragement hand France the regency, and hand Italy a grievance it carries into alliance politics.

anchors.title: Britain occupies Egypt
