anchors.summary: Bombardment at Alexandria and victory at Tel el-Kebir put the canal and Egyptian finances under a British administration that stays for seventy years.

anchors.title: Koch isolates the tuberculosis bacillus
anchors.summary: Disease acquires identifiable causes; public health acquires targets.

anchors.title: Krakatoa erupts
anchors.summary: The explosion and the waves it raised kill more than thirty thousand people around the Sunda Strait, and its dust cools global temperatures for years.

anchors.title: The Berlin conference partitions Africa
anchors.summary: European ministries rule lines across a continent most of them have never seen.

anchors.title: New Guinea is partitioned
anchors.summary: Germany claims the north-east and Britain the south-east within weeks of each other, carrying the European scramble into the Pacific.

anchors.title: Leopold II is granted the Congo Free State
anchors.summary: A territory the size of western Europe is recognized as one monarch's private possession, and rubber and ivory quotas enforced by killing and mutilation follow.

anchors.title: The Mahdists take Khartoum
anchors.summary: A religious movement drives Egyptian and British forces out of the Sudan and rules it from Omdurman for the next thirteen years.

anchors.title: The Indian National Congress is founded
anchors.summary: Seventy-two delegates meet in Bombay to petition for a share in government, and the body they create becomes the vehicle of Indian independence.

anchors.title: Japan creates a cabinet government
anchors.summary: Ito Hirobumi becomes the first prime minister of a ministry organized on European lines, three years before the constitution written to house it.

anchors.title: Benz patents the petrol motor car
anchors.summary: A three-wheeled carriage with a four-stroke engine is patented at Mannheim, and the internal combustion engine finds its most consequential application.

anchors.title: Haymarket and the eight-hour movement
anchors.summary: A bomb thrown at a Chicago rally is followed by trials on doubtful evidence and four hangings, and the eight-hour day acquires its international commemoration.

anchors.title: Gold is found on the Witwatersrand
anchors.summary: The world's richest goldfield turns a farming republic into an industrial magnet, draws migrant labour from across the region, and sets Britain against the Transvaal.

anchors.title: Hertz makes and detects radio waves
anchors.summary: A spark across one gap produces a spark across another metres away, confirming Maxwell's prediction and opening the path to wireless communication.

anchors.title: Brazil abolishes slavery
anchors.summary: The Golden Law frees the last several hundred thousand enslaved people in the Americas, with compensation to no one and land to none of them.

anchors.title: Japan adopts the Meiji constitution
anchors.summary: Asia's first modern constitution, drafted to keep the oligarchs in and the powers impressed.

anchors.title: The Wounded Knee massacre
anchors.summary: Soldiers disarming a Lakota band kill some two hundred and fifty people, most of them not fighting, and armed resistance on the plains ends.

anchors.title: Persia's tobacco protest
anchors.summary: A nationwide boycott backed by a clerical ruling forces the shah to cancel a British tobacco monopoly, showing that organized public pressure can bend a throne.

anchors.title: New Zealand grants women the vote
anchors.summary: The first national women's franchise; the precedent travels slowly but does not reverse.

anchors.title: The Dreyfus affair begins
anchors.summary: A Jewish artillery officer is convicted of treason on forged evidence, and the twelve-year fight to clear him splits France over army, church, and antisemitism.

anchors.title: The first Sino-Japanese war
anchors.summary: Japan destroys the Qing fleet and armies in eight months, takes Taiwan and a crushing indemnity, and inverts the region's order of prestige.

anchors.title: The Lumieres project films to a paying audience
anchors.summary: Ten short films shown in a Paris basement establish cinema as a commercial spectacle rather than a peep-show novelty for one viewer at a time.

anchors.title: Röntgen photographs the invisible
anchors.summary: X-rays open the body to inspection without a knife and physics to a new century of surprises.

anchors.title: Ethiopia defeats Italy at Adwa
anchors.summary: Menelik's army destroys an invading Italian force and wins treaty recognition of Ethiopian independence, the one African state to keep it through the scramble.

anchors.title: The first modern Olympic Games
anchors.summary: Fourteen nations compete at Athens, and an invented tradition becomes the recurring occasion on which states perform rivalry without fighting.

anchors.title: Becquerel finds rays that need no light
anchors.summary: Uranium salts fog a photographic plate shut in a dark drawer, revealing that some atoms give out energy entirely on their own.

anchors.title: The halfpenny press reaches a mass audience
anchors.summary: The Daily Mail sells to a newly literate public at half the usual price and pays for itself with advertising; the newspaper becomes a mass consumer good.

anchors.title: The Philippine revolution begins
anchors.summary: The Katipunan rises against Spanish rule, and the archipelago's fight for independence outlasts the empire it was launched against.

anchors.title: Segregation is upheld as lawful
anchors.summary: Plessy v. Ferguson declares separate accommodation compatible with equal protection, giving the southern states a constitutional footing for Jim Crow.

anchors.title: Plague in Bombay brings emergency powers
anchors.summary: The third plague pandemic arrives by ship, and an epidemic act grants officials powers of search, segregation, and demolition that provoke violent resistance.

anchors.title: The first Zionist Congress meets in Basel
anchors.summary: Two hundred delegates adopt a programme for a Jewish home in Palestine secured in public law, and build the institutions that will pursue it.

anchors.title: The Hundred Days' reform is suppressed
anchors.summary: The Guangxu emperor's decrees on schools, examinations, and ministries are annulled after three months by a palace coup, and six reformers are executed.

anchors.title: The Curies identify polonium and radium
anchors.summary: Two new elements are tracked down by their radiation alone, and radioactivity becomes a property of atoms rather than a peculiarity of uranium.

anchors.title: The Spanish-American war
anchors.summary: Four months of fighting end Spanish rule in Cuba, Puerto Rico, and the Philippines, and leave the United States governing territory across two oceans.

anchors.title: The second Boer war begins
anchors.summary: Britain needs two and a half years, a scorched-earth campaign, and camps in which tens of thousands of Boer and African civilians die, to annex the gold republics.

anchors.title: The Boxer rising and the foreign expedition
anchors.summary: An anti-foreign movement besieges the legations, eight powers march on Peking, and the Qing are left with an indemnity they cannot pay.

anchors.title: Planck quantizes radiated energy
anchors.summary: To fit the spectrum of a hot cavity, energy is assumed to come in discrete packets, and the mathematical trick turns out to describe how nature works.

anchors.title: The Australian colonies federate
anchors.summary: Six self-governing colonies become one commonwealth with a single parliament and tariff, and with immigration law written to exclude non-European settlers.

anchors.title: A wireless signal crosses the Atlantic
anchors.summary: Marconi reports hearing three faint clicks in Newfoundland sent from Cornwall, evidence that radio is not stopped by the curve of the earth.

anchors.title: McKinley is shot and Roosevelt succeeds him
anchors.summary: An anarchist's bullet in Buffalo puts a forty-two-year-old reformer in the presidency, and federal prosecution of industrial trusts begins in earnest.

anchors.title: The Qing court orders the New Policies
anchors.summary: Defeated and heavily indemnified, the dynasty opens a decade of reform that builds new armies, new schools, and eventually provincial assemblies, training the men who desert it.

anchors.title: Spindletop gushes oil in Texas
anchors.summary: A single Gulf coast well outproduces every other American field, and cheap fuel oil begins displacing coal in ships, mills, and locomotives.

anchors.title: Britain and Japan sign an alliance
anchors.summary: The first alliance on equal terms between a European power and an Asian one lets Japan confront Russia without fear that a third power will intervene.

anchors.title: Russian Marxists split into Bolsheviks and Mensheviks
anchors.summary: A quarrel over who counts as a party member divides Russian social democracy into a disciplined professional vanguard and a broad open movement.

anchors.title: The Wright Flyer lifts at Kitty Hawk
anchors.summary: Twelve seconds of powered flight; the third dimension opens for traffic and war alike.

anchors.title: Germany begins the Herero and Nama genocide
anchors.summary: German colonial forces drive Herero families into the Omaheke desert and confine survivors in camps; most Herero and roughly half the Nama population die.

anchors.title: Bengal is partitioned
anchors.summary: An administrative division drawn along communal lines provokes the Swadeshi boycott and turns the Indian National Congress from petitioning to mass agitation.

anchors.title: Bloody Sunday opens the Russian revolution of 1905
anchors.summary: Troops fire on a petition march to the Winter Palace, and a year of strikes, mutinies, and workers' councils forces the tsar to concede an elected Duma.

anchors.title: Einstein publishes four papers in one year
anchors.summary: A patent examiner in Bern sets out special relativity, the light quantum, Brownian motion, and mass-energy equivalence within six months.

anchors.title: The Maji Maji rising spreads in German East Africa
anchors.summary: A revolt against forced cotton cultivation crosses southern Tanganyika, and the German scorched-earth reply produces a famine that kills on the order of 200,000 people.

anchors.title: The Qing abolish the imperial examinations
anchors.summary: Thirteen centuries of recruiting officials by classical examination end, cutting the educated gentry loose from the dynasty that had employed them.

anchors.title: Japan defeats Russia
anchors.summary: An Asian constitutional power sinks a European empire's fleet; every colonized capital notices.

anchors.title: HMS Dreadnought is launched
anchors.summary: An all-big-gun turbine battleship makes every existing capital ship obsolete and restarts the Anglo-German naval race from an even count.

anchors.title: The All-India Muslim League is founded
anchors.summary: Muslim notables meeting at Dhaka organize to seek separate representation, beginning the constitutional argument that ends in partition.

anchors.title: Persia wins a constitution and a majlis
anchors.summary: Merchants, clerics, and reformers force the shah to grant a written constitution and an elected assembly, and the bazaar becomes a standing political power.

anchors.title: The Anglo-Russian convention completes the Entente
anchors.summary: Britain and Russia divide their claims in Persia, Afghanistan, and Tibet, leaving Europe sorted into two armed alliance blocs.

anchors.title: Austria-Hungary annexes Bosnia and Herzegovina
anchors.summary: A unilateral annexation humiliates Serbia and Russia, hardens Balkan grievance, and rehearses the crisis sequence that runs again in 1914.

anchors.title: Budi Utomo is founded in Java
anchors.summary: Students at a Dutch colonial medical school form the first modern Indonesian association, and colonial subjects begin organizing as a nation.

anchors.title: The Model T goes on sale
anchors.summary: A car built for rutted farm roads and priced lower each year turns the automobile from a rich man's amusement into ordinary transport.

anchors.title: Oil is struck at Masjid-i-Suleiman
anchors.summary: The first commercial oil field in the Middle East comes in at a Persian site, and the region's politics acquire a permanent stake in fuel supply.

anchors.title: The Young Turks restore the Ottoman constitution
anchors.summary: Army officers in Macedonia force Abdulhamid II to recall parliament, and a committee of officers takes control of the empire's direction.

anchors.title: Bleriot flies across the English Channel
anchors.summary: A monoplane crosses from near Calais to Dover in about thirty-seven minutes, and British security stops being a question of navies alone.

anchors.title: Haber fixes nitrogen from air
anchors.summary: Synthetic ammonia unlocks fertilizer and explosives in the same reaction; the world's food ceiling lifts.

anchors.title: Japan annexes Korea
anchors.summary: A treaty signed under military pressure ends the Korean state, and thirty-five years of Japanese rule begin with land surveys and censorship.

anchors.title: The Mexican revolution begins
anchors.summary: Madero's call to arms against Porfirio Diaz opens a decade of civil war over land and labor that costs on the order of a million lives.

anchors.title: The Union of South Africa is created
anchors.summary: Four colonies merge into a self-governing dominion whose parliamentary franchise is reserved almost entirely for white voters.

anchors.title: The Qing dynasty falls
anchors.summary: A railway dispute becomes a revolution; two millennia of imperial rule end with a child's abdication.

anchors.title: The Raj moves its capital to Delhi
anchors.summary: George V announces at the Delhi durbar that government will leave Calcutta and that the partition of Bengal is reversed, conceding to six years of protest.

anchors.title: Italy takes Libya from the Ottomans
anchors.summary: An Italian invasion of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica strips the Ottomans of their last African province and advertises the empire's weakness to its Balkan neighbours.

anchors.title: The First Balkan War expels Ottoman rule from Europe
anchors.summary: Serbia, Bulgaria, Greece, and Montenegro overrun the Ottoman provinces in weeks, leaving the empire holding little more than the ground around Constantinople.

anchors.title: Argentina adopts the secret ballot
anchors.summary: The Saenz Pena law makes the vote universal, secret, and compulsory for adult male citizens, and the oligarchy loses its first honest election four years later.

anchors.title: The South African Native National Congress is founded
anchors.summary: African teachers, ministers, and chiefs meet at Bloemfontein to contest a dominion built on their exclusion, forming the body later renamed the African National Congress.

anchors.title: The Amazon rubber boom collapses
anchors.summary: Plantation rubber from Southeast Asia undercuts wild Amazonian latex, and the boom towns of Manaus and Iquitos lose the single trade that had built them.

anchors.title: Ford runs a moving assembly line
anchors.summary: Bringing the work to the worker at Highland Park cuts chassis assembly from twelve hours to about ninety minutes and sets the pace of industrial labour.

anchors.title: Bohr quantizes the atom
anchors.summary: Electrons are allowed only fixed orbits and jump between them in discrete steps, which explains the hydrogen spectrum and forces physics toward quantum theory.

anchors.title: The Federal Reserve Act creates a central bank
anchors.summary: After a generation of bank panics the United States accepts a lender of last resort, twelve regional banks issuing a single elastic currency.

anchors.title: The Rite of Spring premieres in Paris
anchors.summary: Stravinsky's hammered rhythms and Nijinsky's turned-in dancers set off an uproar in the theatre and mark the arrival of musical modernism.

anchors.title: The Second Balkan War redraws the spoils
anchors.summary: Bulgaria attacks its former allies over Macedonia and loses; the Treaty of Bucharest leaves every Balkan capital with a grievance and a mobilisation plan.

anchors.title: The Marne halts the German advance
anchors.summary: French and British counterattacks northeast of Paris stop the invasion short of the capital, and both sides dig the trench line that holds for four years.

anchors.title: The Ottoman empire enters the Great War
anchors.summary: Ottoman warships shell Russian Black Sea ports, and a European war becomes a war for the Middle East, with the Turkish straits closed to Russian trade.

anchors.title: The Panama Canal opens
anchors.summary: The isthmus is cut after forty years and twenty-five thousand deaths; two oceans share a lock.

anchors.title: The July Crisis becomes the Great War
anchors.summary: A murder in Sarajevo works through the alliance machinery; four empires enter the grinder.

anchors.title: The Ottoman state destroys its Armenian population
anchors.summary: Beginning with the arrest of Armenian community leaders in Constantinople, deportations and killings across Anatolia and the Syrian desert kill a million people or more.

anchors.title: Chlorine gas is released at Ypres
anchors.summary: German troops open cylinders of chlorine against French colonial units, and industrial chemistry becomes a standing weapon of the war.

anchors.title: The Allies land at Gallipoli
anchors.summary: An attempt to force the Dardanelles and reach Constantinople stalls on the beaches for eight months and is evacuated, with heavy losses on both sides.

anchors.title: Italy enters the war against Austria-Hungary
anchors.summary: Promised Austrian territory by the secret Treaty of London, Italy opens an alpine front where eleven battles are fought along one river, the Isonzo.

anchors.title: Japan presents the Twenty-One Demands to China
anchors.summary: Tokyo demands rights over Shandong, Manchuria, and Chinese administration itself; the partial acceptance becomes a date of national humiliation for Chinese students.

anchors.title: The Arab revolt begins in the Hejaz
anchors.summary: Sharif Husayn of Mecca rises against Ottoman rule with British money and arms, on the understanding of an Arab kingdom that the wartime treaties do not grant.

anchors.title: The Easter Rising is put down in Dublin
anchors.summary: A week-long republican seizure of central Dublin fails, but the execution of its leaders turns a minority cause into a majority one within two years.

anchors.title: Washington promises the Philippines independence
anchors.summary: The Jones Act declares eventual independence as American policy and hands Filipinos an elected senate, the first such pledge by a colonial power in Asia.

anchors.title: The Somme offensive opens
anchors.summary: The British army takes about 57,000 casualties on the first day and about 420,000 by November, and Britain's volunteer generation is spent on a few miles of chalk.

anchors.title: Britain and France divide the Ottoman east in secret
anchors.summary: The Sykes-Picot understanding assigns spheres across Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, and Palestine before the territory is taken, and later fixes the mandate borders.

anchors.title: The battle of Verdun grinds on for ten months
anchors.summary: A German offensive meant to bleed the French army white produces some 700,000 casualties on both sides and moves the front only a few kilometres.

anchors.title: Yuan Shikai dies and the warlord era begins
anchors.summary: The republic's strongman dies months after a failed attempt to make himself emperor, and provincial commanders divide China for the next decade.

anchors.title: The Balfour declaration is issued
anchors.summary: Britain declares favour for a Jewish national home in Palestine while promising not to prejudice the rights of the existing communities, and commits to both.

anchors.title: Brazil declares war on Germany
anchors.summary: Submarine attacks on its shipping bring the only South American belligerent into the war, and wartime demand accelerates Brazilian industry behind blocked imports.

anchors.title: The February revolution ends the Romanov monarchy
anchors.summary: Bread queues and a garrison mutiny in Petrograd topple Nicholas II in a week, leaving a provisional government and the soviets sharing authority.

anchors.title: Mexico adopts the constitution of 1917
anchors.summary: Land reform, an eight-hour day, and national ownership of the subsoil are written into fundamental law, a template other Latin American movements borrow.

anchors.title: The Bolsheviks take Petrograd
anchors.summary: War-broken Russia falls to the one party promising bread, land, and exit; the century acquires its schism.

anchors.title: The United States enters the Great War
anchors.summary: Unrestricted German submarine warfare and the Zimmermann telegram bring America in, adding fresh manpower and credit to an exhausted Allied coalition.

anchors.title: The armistice silences the western front
anchors.summary: Fighting stops at eleven in the morning on the eleventh of November after four years that killed some nine million soldiers and unseated four empires.

anchors.title: Soviet Russia signs the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
anchors.summary: To end the war in the east the Bolsheviks surrender Poland, the Baltic lands, Finland, and Ukraine, giving up a third of the empire's population and most of its coal.

anchors.title: The German revolution ends the Hohenzollern monarchy
anchors.summary: A naval mutiny at Kiel spreads to workers' and soldiers' councils across Germany, Wilhelm II abdicates, and a republic is proclaimed in Berlin.

anchors.title: The Habsburg monarchy dissolves
anchors.summary: Czechoslovakia, Hungary, and a south Slav kingdom declare themselves out of a collapsing empire, replacing one customs union with a lattice of new tariff borders.

anchors.title: The influenza pandemic
anchors.summary: The flu kills more than the war just ending, and is remembered less.

anchors.title: The Russian civil war spreads across the empire
anchors.summary: Red, White, and nationalist armies fight from the Baltic to the Pacific for three years, and famine and typhus kill far more people than the fighting does.

anchors.title: Britain extends the vote to women over thirty
anchors.summary: The Representation of the People Act enfranchises about eight million women with a property qualification and nearly all adult men, tripling the electorate.

anchors.title: Troops fire on a crowd at Amritsar
anchors.summary: British Indian soldiers shoot into an enclosed gathering at Jallianwala Bagh, killing several hundred people, and moderate Indian faith in British justice does not recover.

anchors.title: The Irish war of independence begins
anchors.summary: Sinn Fein members meet as an Irish parliament in Dublin and a guerrilla campaign opens against the police, fought in ambushes and reprisals for two and a half years.

anchors.title: The March First movement rises across Korea
anchors.summary: A declaration of independence read in Seoul sets off months of demonstrations by perhaps two million people, which Japanese police and troops suppress with heavy loss of life.

anchors.title: The May Fourth movement begins in Beijing
anchors.summary: Students protest the transfer of German rights in Shandong to Japan, and the demonstrations grow into a wider campaign for science, plain language, and national renewal.

anchors.title: The Treaty of Versailles
anchors.summary: The victors redraw Europe and price the war onto Germany; the settlement satisfies no one who signs it.

anchors.title: Germany adopts the Weimar constitution
anchors.summary: A republic is built on proportional representation, universal suffrage, and an emergency article allowing rule by presidential decree.

anchors.title: The League of Nations opens its first assembly
anchors.summary: Forty-one states meet at Geneva in the first standing organisation for collective security, without the United States, which declines to join.

anchors.title: American women win the vote
anchors.summary: The Nineteenth Amendment is ratified after seventy years of campaigning, though local law continues to bar most Black women in the southern states.

anchors.title: Gandhi launches non-cooperation in India
anchors.summary: Congress adopts the boycott of British courts, schools, titles, and cloth, turning a lawyers' association into a mass organisation with village committees.

anchors.title: Germany's Pacific colonies become League mandates
anchors.summary: Japan takes the islands north of the equator, Australia takes New Guinea and New Zealand takes Samoa, spreading naval rivalry across the western Pacific.

anchors.title: Prohibition takes effect in the United States
anchors.summary: The manufacture and sale of alcohol becomes illegal nationwide, closing a large industry and handing its trade to organised smuggling for thirteen years.

anchors.title: Regular radio broadcasting begins
anchors.summary: A voice speaks to everyone in range at once; the mass audience becomes simultaneous.

anchors.title: San Remo assigns the Ottoman provinces as mandates
anchors.summary: Britain takes Palestine and Mesopotamia and France takes Syria and Lebanon under League mandate, converting wartime promises into administered borders.

anchors.title: The Anglo-Irish Treaty partitions Ireland
anchors.summary: Twenty-six counties become a dominion with an oath to the crown while six northern counties stay in the United Kingdom, and the compromise starts a civil war.

anchors.title: The Chinese Communist Party is founded in Shanghai
anchors.summary: A dozen delegates meeting in the French concession found a party of some fifty members, organised on Bolshevik lines with Comintern advice.

anchors.title: The Bolsheviks retreat to the New Economic Policy
anchors.summary: After the Kronstadt mutiny and peasant revolts, grain requisitioning gives way to a tax in kind and legal private trade, and the countryside starts feeding the cities again.

anchors.title: Gandhi calls off non-cooperation after Chauri Chaura
anchors.summary: A crowd burns a police post and kills its constables, and Gandhi suspends the whole campaign, insisting that a mass movement stay non-violent or stop.

anchors.title: Britain declares Egypt independent with reservations
anchors.summary: Cairo gains a king and formal sovereignty while Britain reserves the canal, defence, the Sudan, and the protection of foreigners, so the occupation continues in substance.

anchors.title: Insulin saves its first patients
anchors.summary: A death sentence becomes a manageable condition within a single year of clinical work.

anchors.title: Mussolini is made prime minister after the march on Rome
anchors.summary: The king refuses to declare martial law against the fascist columns and appoints their leader instead, and Europe acquires its first fascist government.

anchors.title: The Greek army is driven out of Anatolia
anchors.summary: Turkish forces retake Smyrna after a three-year war and fire destroys much of the city, ending the Greek project of a state spanning the Aegean.

anchors.title: The tomb of Tutankhamun is opened
anchors.summary: Carter's team finds a nearly intact royal burial in the Valley of the Kings, and Egyptian antiquity becomes a mass enthusiasm and a question of Egyptian ownership.

anchors.title: The Soviet Union is founded
anchors.summary: A treaty of union binds the Russian, Ukrainian, Belorussian, and Transcaucasian republics into one federal state under a single party.

anchors.title: The Washington treaty limits battleship fleets
anchors.summary: Britain, the United States, Japan, France, and Italy accept fixed capital ship ratios and scrap ships already building, the first arms limitation actually carried out.

anchors.title: The German mark collapses into hyperinflation
anchors.summary: Prices rise until a loaf of bread costs billions of marks, wiping out savings and salaries before a new currency stops it in November.

anchors.title: An earthquake and firestorm destroy Tokyo and Yokohama
anchors.summary: About 105,000 people die, mostly in fires, and in the days after rumour-driven mobs and officials kill thousands of Koreans and other minorities.

anchors.title: Greece and Turkey exchange populations by treaty
anchors.summary: About 1.2 million Orthodox Christians and 400,000 Muslims are moved by agreement on religious criteria, and compulsory transfer enters the toolkit of states.

anchors.title: France and Belgium occupy the Ruhr
anchors.summary: Troops seize Germany's coal and steel district over unpaid reparations, and the government answers with passive resistance paid for by printing money.

anchors.title: The Turkish republic is proclaimed
anchors.summary: From the Ottoman collapse, Mustafa Kemal builds a secular nation-state by decree.

anchors.title: Chilean officers end the parliamentary republic
anchors.summary: A military intervention forces through stalled labour and social laws and opens a decade in which the army decides who governs Chile.

anchors.title: Aircraft circle the globe for the first time
anchors.summary: Two American biplanes finish a 175-day flight around the world in stages, proving that air routes can be strung across oceans with prepared depots.

anchors.title: America closes its doors with national origin quotas
anchors.summary: Quotas keyed to an earlier census cut immigration from southern and eastern Europe to a trickle and bar most Asian entry, ending a century of open arrivals.

anchors.title: Lenin dies and the succession struggle opens
anchors.summary: The Soviet state loses its founder without an agreed rule for replacing him, and a contest between Stalin and Trotsky decides the shape of the party.

anchors.title: The Great Syrian Revolt challenges the French mandate
anchors.summary: A Druze rising spreads to Damascus, where French artillery and aircraft shell the old city twice before two years of fighting end the revolt.

anchors.title: The Locarno treaties settle Germany's western border
anchors.summary: Germany accepts its frontiers with France and Belgium voluntarily and leaves the eastern ones open to revision, buying five years of European calm.

anchors.title: The May Thirtieth movement sweeps Chinese cities
anchors.summary: Police under foreign command shoot demonstrators in Shanghai, and the strikes and boycotts that follow turn nationalism into a mass urban force.

anchors.title: Quantum mechanics is put on a formal footing
anchors.summary: Heisenberg's matrix scheme replaces electron orbits with tables of observable quantities, and within a year physics has a working theory of the atom.

anchors.title: The Northern Expedition marches north
anchors.summary: Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalist armies leave Guangdong to break the warlords, and China acquires a single claimant government again.

anchors.title: Reza Shah is crowned in Tehran
anchors.summary: A Cossack brigade officer takes the throne and begins imposing conscription, railways and a centralized bureaucracy on Iran.

anchors.title: Lindbergh flies the Atlantic alone
anchors.summary: Thirty-three hours from New York to Paris turn the aeroplane from a stunt into a plausible instrument of commerce and war.

anchors.title: The Nationalists purge the communists in Shanghai
anchors.summary: Chiang's troops and allied gangs kill union organizers and party members in April, opening a civil war that runs for twenty-two years.

anchors.title: Fleming notices penicillin
anchors.summary: A contaminated dish in a London lab holds the first antibiotic, unexploited for a decade.

anchors.title: The Soviet Union adopts its first five-year plan
anchors.summary: Output targets set in Moscow, not prices, now decide what factories build, and heavy industry is ordered to double within five years.

anchors.title: The Wall Street crash
anchors.summary: Leverage unwinds; the Depression it triggers unseats governments and gold standards everywhere.

anchors.title: Collectivization begins in the Soviet countryside
anchors.summary: Peasant holdings are merged into state and collective farms by force, and those who resist are dispossessed and deported as kulaks.

anchors.title: The Nazis become Germany's second party
anchors.summary: Depression voters lift a fringe movement from twelve Reichstag seats to a hundred and seven, and the republic loses any governing majority.

anchors.title: Gandhi walks to the sea to make salt
anchors.summary: Two hundred and forty miles of deliberate lawbreaking turn a tax on a household necessity into a mass campaign against British rule.

anchors.title: The United States raises tariffs to record levels
anchors.summary: Duties on twenty thousand goods invite retaliation, and world trade contracts by roughly two thirds over the next three years.

anchors.title: Vargas takes power in Brazil
anchors.summary: A disputed election ends in a military-backed coup, and fifteen years of centralizing, industrializing rule replace the coffee oligarchy.

anchors.title: Bank failures spread the depression worldwide
anchors.summary: Vienna's Creditanstalt collapses in May, Germany's banks close in July and Britain leaves gold in September; by 1932 some thirty million are out of work.

anchors.title: Japan seizes Manchuria
anchors.summary: Officers of the Kwantung Army stage an explosion on their own railway and take a province, and the League of Nations answers with nothing binding.

anchors.title: Bolivia and Paraguay go to war over the Chaco
anchors.summary: Two landlocked states fight three years for scrubland thought to hold oil, and about ninety thousand men die, many of them of thirst and disease.

anchors.title: Japan proclaims the state of Manchukuo
anchors.summary: The last Qing emperor is installed as figurehead over a Japanese-run territory, and the League's censure prompts Japan to walk out of it.

anchors.title: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is proclaimed
anchors.summary: Ibn Saud joins Nejd and the Hejaz into one realm, placing the holy cities and, within a decade, enormous oil reserves under a single dynasty.

anchors.title: The first concentration camp opens at Dachau
anchors.summary: Political prisoners are held outside the courts under SS guard, and the camp becomes the training ground and model for the system that follows.

anchors.title: The Reichstag fire brings the Enabling Act
anchors.summary: Emergency decrees suspend civil liberties in February, and in March a cowed parliament votes its own legislative power away to the cabinet.

anchors.title: Hitler is appointed chancellor
anchors.summary: Germany's conservatives hand power to a movement they believe they can manage.

anchors.title: Famine kills millions in Soviet Ukraine
anchors.summary: Grain requisitions continue through the collapse of the harvest and villages are barred from leaving to find food; roughly four million die.

anchors.title: The New Deal's first hundred days
anchors.summary: Fifteen major acts in three months close and reopen the banks, pay farmers to cut output, and put federal money directly into relief work.

anchors.title: Dust storms strip the southern plains
anchors.summary: A May storm carries plains topsoil as far as New York, and drought on deep-ploughed grassland drives hundreds of thousands of farm families west.

anchors.title: The Long March
anchors.summary: The Chinese communists retreat six thousand miles and emerge with a leader: Mao.

anchors.title: The Night of the Long Knives
anchors.summary: Hitler has the SA leadership and other rivals shot without trial, and the army accepts him as the single source of authority in Germany.

anchors.title: Italy invades Ethiopia
anchors.summary: Italian forces cross from Eritrea and Somaliland using aircraft and poison gas, and the League votes sanctions that exclude oil and fail.

anchors.title: The Nuremberg laws strip German Jews of citizenship
anchors.summary: Marriage and civil status are redefined by ancestry, and exclusion from German public life becomes a matter of statute rather than street violence.

anchors.title: The United States enacts social security
anchors.summary: Old-age pensions and unemployment insurance funded by payroll taxes make the federal government a permanent party to the household budget.

anchors.title: The Arab revolt begins in Palestine
anchors.summary: A general strike against Jewish immigration and land sales becomes three years of armed rebellion, British repression and rival partition schemes.

anchors.title: German troops reoccupy the Rhineland
anchors.summary: A small force marches into the demilitarized zone with orders to withdraw if opposed, and neither France nor Britain moves against it.

anchors.title: The Spanish civil war begins
anchors.summary: A generals' rising against the republic becomes a three-year war in which Germany and Italy supply Franco while the Soviet Union supplies Madrid.

anchors.title: Chiang is seized at Xi'an
anchors.summary: His own commanders arrest him and release him only on terms: Nationalists and communists suspend their civil war to fight Japan together.

anchors.title: The Great Purge
anchors.summary: Arrest and execution quotas are sent to every region; some seven hundred thousand people are shot in two years, including most senior army officers.

anchors.title: Japan and China go to full-scale war
anchors.summary: A night clash outside Beijing escalates into an undeclared war that occupies the Chinese coast and kills millions before it ends in 1945.

anchors.title: Japanese troops massacre civilians at Nanjing
anchors.summary: After the capital falls in December, six weeks of mass killing and rape leave a toll of civilians and disarmed prisoners estimated in the tens of thousands and above.

anchors.title: Germany annexes Austria
anchors.summary: German troops enter unopposed and a plebiscite held under occupation ratifies the union, leaving the settlement of 1919 openly void.

anchors.title: Oil is struck in commercial quantity at Dammam
anchors.summary: The seventh well on the Saudi coast flows steadily, and the kingdom's finances and foreign relations reorganize around export.

anchors.title: Synagogues burn across Germany in November
anchors.summary: State-organized attacks destroy hundreds of synagogues and thousands of businesses, kill scores of Jews, and send thirty thousand men to camps.

anchors.title: Munich hands the Sudetenland to Germany
anchors.summary: Britain and France award Czechoslovakia's border districts to Hitler without Czech consent, and the country loses its frontier defences.

anchors.title: Fission is identified in uranium
anchors.summary: Hahn and Strassmann find barium after bombarding uranium, and Meitner and Frisch read the result as a nucleus splitting and releasing energy.

anchors.title: Einstein and Szilard warn Roosevelt
anchors.summary: A letter drafted by refugee physicists tells the president that uranium may yield extremely powerful bombs, and a federal committee is formed.

anchors.title: Germany and the Soviet Union sign a pact
anchors.summary: A public non-aggression treaty carries secret protocols dividing Poland, the Baltic states and Bessarabia between the two signatories.

anchors.title: Germany invades Poland
anchors.summary: The European war resumes twenty years after its armistice, this time totally.

anchors.title: The Battle of Britain
anchors.summary: Radar-directed fighters deny the Luftwaffe daylight air superiority over the Channel, and the invasion of England is postponed indefinitely.

anchors.title: The Dunkirk evacuation
anchors.summary: Warships, ferries and small craft lift about three hundred and thirty-eight thousand Allied soldiers off the beaches, leaving the equipment behind.

anchors.title: France signs an armistice with Germany
anchors.summary: Six weeks after the attack through the Ardennes the Third Republic ends, Germany occupies the north and the coast, and Vichy governs the rest.

anchors.title: Italy invades Greece from Albania
anchors.summary: The October attack stalls and is driven back, and Germany is pulled into the Balkans the following spring to rescue its ally.

anchors.title: The Muslim League demands separate states
anchors.summary: Meeting at Lahore, the League resolves that India's Muslim-majority regions should form independent states, and partition becomes a stated aim.

anchors.title: The Blitz begins over British cities
anchors.summary: Eight months of night bombing kill some forty-three thousand civilians and damage or destroy more than a million homes without breaking war production.

anchors.title: Britain and the Soviet Union occupy Iran
anchors.summary: The two powers take the railway to move supplies to the Soviet front, force Reza Shah to abdicate, and install his young son in his place.

anchors.title: Mass shootings at Babi Yar
anchors.summary: German units and local auxiliaries kill 33,771 Jews in a ravine outside Kyiv over two days, part of the shooting campaign that follows the invasion.

anchors.title: Germany invades the Soviet Union
anchors.summary: Three million troops attack on a front from the Baltic to the Black Sea in a war of annihilation planned around starvation and mass shooting.

anchors.title: Italian East Africa falls and the emperor returns
anchors.summary: Imperial and Ethiopian forces retake Addis Ababa within a year, and Haile Selassie re-enters his capital five years to the day after the Italians took it.

anchors.title: Lend-Lease opens American supply to the Allies
anchors.summary: Congress lets the president lend war material without payment, and tens of billions of dollars in goods flow to Britain, the Soviet Union and China.

anchors.title: Pearl Harbor
anchors.summary: Japan staggers the US Pacific fleet and, in doing so, ends American neutrality everywhere.

anchors.title: The siege of Leningrad begins
anchors.summary: The city is encircled for eight hundred and seventy-two days, and about a million civilians die, most of them of hunger.

anchors.title: The first controlled chain reaction
anchors.summary: Under a stadium in Chicago a graphite and uranium pile sustains fission on command, and the Manhattan Project turns physics into an industrial problem.

anchors.title: The Axis advance stops at El Alamein
anchors.summary: A prepared British attack in October breaks the German and Italian line sixty miles from Alexandria and begins their long retreat out of Egypt.

anchors.title: Singapore surrenders to Japan
anchors.summary: The garrison capitulates after a week of fighting on the island, about eighty thousand troops become prisoners, and British authority in Asia loses its assumed permanence.

anchors.title: The Wannsee conference coordinates the Holocaust
anchors.summary: Bureaucrats schedule genocide; six million Jews are murdered in the machinery that follows.

anchors.title: Four Japanese carriers are sunk at Midway
anchors.summary: Broken codes put American aircraft over the Japanese fleet while its decks are full, and the initiative in the Pacific changes hands for good.

anchors.title: American and British forces land in North Africa
anchors.summary: Landings in Morocco and Algeria put Allied armies on the continent, draw German troops into Tunisia, and end Vichy's hold on its colonies.

anchors.title: The Quit India movement
anchors.summary: Congress demands immediate British withdrawal, its leadership is jailed for most of the rest of the war, and mass protest is put down by force.

anchors.title: Famine in Bengal
anchors.summary: Wartime requisitioning, a cyclone, the loss of Burmese rice and a refusal to divert shipping combine to kill some two to three million people.

anchors.title: Italy surrenders and Germany occupies the north
anchors.summary: Mussolini falls in July and the armistice is announced in September, whereupon German forces disarm the Italian army and hold the peninsula for twenty months.

anchors.title: The German offensive fails at Kursk
anchors.summary: An attack on a heavily fortified salient is called off within a fortnight, and from then on the eastern front moves only westward.

anchors.title: Penicillin is mass-produced
anchors.summary: Deep-tank fermentation turns a lab curiosity into a war supply; bacterial infection loses its death grip.

anchors.title: Stalingrad falls to the Soviets
anchors.summary: An army freezes and surrenders on the Volga; the eastern war reverses direction.

anchors.title: The Allied leaders meet at Tehran
anchors.summary: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin agree on a landing in France for 1944 and sketch the extent of Soviet gains in eastern Europe.

anchors.title: The Axis armies surrender in Tunisia
anchors.summary: About two hundred and thirty thousand German and Italian troops give up, clearing North Africa and reopening the Mediterranean to Allied shipping.

anchors.title: The Warsaw ghetto rises against deportation
anchors.summary: A few hundred fighters with smuggled weapons hold out for four weeks, and the ghetto is burned block by block with its remaining inhabitants inside.

anchors.title: Germany's last western offensive fails in the Ardennes
anchors.summary: A December surprise attack through fog gains fifty miles, then stalls for want of fuel and dies under clear skies and Allied reinforcement.

anchors.title: Bretton Woods designs the postwar economy
anchors.summary: Delegates in a New Hampshire hotel peg currencies to the dollar and invent the IMF and World Bank.

anchors.title: The Allies land in Normandy
anchors.summary: Some hundred and fifty thousand troops come ashore behind airborne landings and artificial harbours, and a second front opens in the west.

anchors.title: The Japanese fleet is broken at Leyte Gulf
anchors.summary: The largest naval battle ever fought ends Japan's capacity for fleet action and brings the first organized suicide attacks on Allied ships.

anchors.title: Paris is liberated
anchors.summary: The garrison surrenders after a police and resistance rising, the city is not demolished as ordered, and a French provisional government takes office.

anchors.title: The Red Army destroys Army Group Centre
anchors.summary: A summer offensive in Belarus breaks twenty-eight German divisions in five weeks and carries Soviet armies to the Vistula.

anchors.title: Soviet troops reach Auschwitz
anchors.summary: About seven thousand prisoners are found alive in the abandoned camp complex where roughly a million people, most of them Jews, were murdered.

anchors.title: Dresden is destroyed by firebombing
anchors.summary: British and American raids over three days burn out the city centre and kill some twenty-five thousand people in a war already decided.

anchors.title: Berlin falls and Germany surrenders
anchors.summary: Soviet armies take the city street by street over two weeks, Hitler kills himself, and the unconditional surrender takes effect on 8 May.

anchors.title: Atomic bombs destroy Hiroshima and Nagasaki
anchors.summary: Two cities end in two flashes; war acquires a ceiling and politics a new arithmetic.

anchors.title: Indonesia declares independence
anchors.summary: Two days after Japan's surrender, Sukarno and Hatta proclaim a republic, and four years of war against the returning Dutch begin.

anchors.title: Japan surrenders
anchors.summary: The emperor broadcasts acceptance of Allied terms in August, the instrument of surrender is signed in Tokyo Bay in September, and the occupation begins.

anchors.title: Firebombing destroys central Tokyo
anchors.summary: One night raid with incendiaries burns sixteen square miles and kills about a hundred thousand people, the deadliest air attack of the war.

anchors.title: The first nuclear explosion at Trinity
anchors.summary: A plutonium device tested in the New Mexico desert releases about twenty kilotons, confirming three years of secret industrial work.

anchors.title: The United Nations is chartered
anchors.summary: The victors institutionalize their alliance with a veto for each of them.

anchors.title: The Allies divide postwar Europe at Yalta
anchors.summary: The three leaders agree occupation zones for Germany, a Soviet entry into the Pacific war, and Polish elections that are never held as promised.

anchors.title: Nuclear tests begin at Bikini Atoll
anchors.summary: The islanders are moved off for what they are told is a temporary trial, and two test shots make the Pacific a proving ground for the arms race.

anchors.title: ENIAC is unveiled
anchors.summary: A room of eighteen thousand vacuum tubes computes artillery tables in seconds, and general-purpose electronic computing leaves the laboratory.

anchors.title: Churchill names the iron curtain
anchors.summary: Speaking in Missouri, he describes a line drawn across Europe from Stettin to Trieste, and the wartime alliance is publicly declared finished.

anchors.title: The Nuremberg tribunal delivers its verdicts
anchors.summary: Twenty-two surviving leaders are tried before an international court, twelve are sentenced to death, and aggressive war is named a punishable crime.

anchors.title: Perón wins the Argentine presidency
anchors.summary: A former labour secretary builds a coalition of unions and the army, and wages, welfare and nationalized industry redefine Argentine politics for decades.

anchors.title: The Tokyo tribunal opens
anchors.summary: Twenty-eight Japanese leaders are charged with waging aggressive war, the emperor is not among them, and seven are eventually hanged.

anchors.title: India and Pakistan become independent
anchors.summary: The Raj ends at midnight, partitioned; freedom and displacement arrive on the same trains.

anchors.title: Japan's postwar constitution takes effect
anchors.summary: Sovereignty passes to the people, the emperor becomes a symbol, and article nine renounces war as a sovereign right of the state.

anchors.title: The Marshall plan is proposed
anchors.summary: The United States offers to fund European recovery as one coordinated programme, the Soviet bloc refuses to join, and the division of Europe hardens.

anchors.title: The transistor is demonstrated
anchors.summary: Three men at Bell Labs replace the vacuum tube with a sliver of germanium; electronics begins shrinking.

anchors.title: The United Nations votes to partition Palestine
anchors.summary: The assembly recommends separate Jewish and Arab states with Jerusalem internationalized, the Arab states reject the plan, and fighting begins at once.

anchors.title: The Berlin blockade and the airlift
anchors.summary: The Soviets cut the land routes to the western sectors, aircraft land every few minutes with coal and food for eleven months, and the blockade is lifted.

anchors.title: Gandhi is assassinated
anchors.summary: A Hindu nationalist shoots him in Delhi five months after partition, and the new Indian state moves against the organizations behind the killing.

anchors.title: Israel declares independence
anchors.summary: A state is proclaimed and immediately at war; the region's defining conflict takes shape.

anchors.title: South Africa's National Party wins on apartheid
anchors.summary: A minority of the total electorate returns a government pledged to systematic racial separation, and existing segregation begins to be codified.

anchors.title: Palestinians are displaced in the first Arab-Israeli war
anchors.summary: The fighting ends with Israel holding more territory than the partition plan allotted and about seven hundred thousand Palestinians made refugees.

anchors.title: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
anchors.summary: The General Assembly adopts a list of rights owed to every person; it binds no state legally, but it becomes the reference text for those who claim them.

anchors.title: The Netherlands transfers sovereignty to Indonesia
anchors.summary: After four years of war and heavy international pressure the Dutch concede, and the largest colony in Southeast Asia becomes a republic.

anchors.title: The Nationalist government withdraws to Taiwan
anchors.summary: Chiang moves the republic's institutions, its gold reserve and its remaining forces across the strait, and two governments claim to be China.

anchors.title: NATO binds North America to western Europe
anchors.summary: Twelve states agree that an attack on one is an attack on all, and American forces stay in Europe in peacetime for the first time.

anchors.title: The People's Republic of China is proclaimed
anchors.summary: Mao announces the new state from Tiananmen; the world's largest population changes systems.

anchors.title: Apartheid is written into South African law
anchors.summary: The Population Registration Act classifies every person by race and the Group Areas Act dictates where they may live and trade.

anchors.title: India adopts a republican constitution
anchors.summary: The longest written constitution in the world takes effect, granting universal adult suffrage at once and abolishing untouchability by law.

anchors.title: North Korean forces cross the thirty-eighth parallel
anchors.summary: The June invasion draws in United Nations and then Chinese armies, and three years of war leave the peninsula divided close to where it started.

anchors.title: France and Germany pool coal and steel
anchors.summary: Six states put their war industries under one authority; European integration begins as an arms-control scheme with a market attached.

anchors.title: Japan signs the San Francisco peace treaty
anchors.summary: Forty-eight states end the occupation on American terms; Japan regains sovereignty, renounces its empire, and keeps the bases.

anchors.title: Libya becomes independent
anchors.summary: The United Nations midwifes its first new state out of an Italian colony, and oil is struck under it within a decade.

anchors.title: Egypt's Free Officers depose the king
anchors.summary: Colonels take Cairo and end the monarchy; Nasser's republic will nationalize the canal and export Arab nationalism.

anchors.title: Kenya's Mau Mau emergency begins
anchors.summary: Britain answers a Kikuyu revolt with mass detention, screening, and over a thousand hangings; Kenya becomes independent in 1963.

anchors.title: The first thermonuclear device is detonated
anchors.summary: Ivy Mike vaporizes an islet at Enewetak; megatons replace kilotons and the arms race loses its upper bound.

anchors.title: The structure of DNA is published
anchors.summary: A double helix explains heredity's copying trick; biology becomes an information science.

anchors.title: A coup restores the shah in Iran
anchors.summary: British and American services unseat Mossadegh after he nationalizes the oil; the grievance outlives every government it touches.

anchors.title: The Korean war ends in armistice
anchors.summary: Three years of fighting stop near the line where they started; the peninsula keeps two states, no treaty, and a fortified scar.

anchors.title: Stalin dies
anchors.summary: The Soviet dictator dies of a stroke; his successors halt the terror, empty much of the camp system, and begin denouncing him.

anchors.title: Algeria's war of independence begins
anchors.summary: Nationalists attack on All Saints' night; eight years of massacre and torture end France's largest settler colony and its Fourth Republic.

anchors.title: Brown v. Board outlaws school segregation
anchors.summary: The US Supreme Court finds separate schooling inherently unequal; the ruling arms a decade of marches and provokes a decade of defiance.

anchors.title: Castle Bravo contaminates the Marshall Islands
anchors.summary: A fifteen-megaton test at Bikini more than doubles its predicted yield; fallout poisons islanders and a Japanese crew, and testing becomes public business.

anchors.title: France loses Dien Bien Phu
anchors.summary: A besieged garrison surrenders in the hills of Tonkin; Geneva partitions Vietnam and hands the next war to Washington.

anchors.title: The Bandung conference
anchors.summary: Twenty-nine African and Asian states meet without their former rulers and name themselves a third force.

anchors.title: The polio vaccine is declared effective
anchors.summary: Salk's trial results are announced to ringing church bells; mass immunization drives childhood paralysis out of the industrial world.

anchors.title: The Warsaw Pact is signed
anchors.summary: Days after West Germany joins NATO, Moscow formalizes its bloc; Europe's division acquires two commands and a legal excuse for intervention.

anchors.title: The first container ship sails
anchors.summary: A trucker's steel box collapses loading costs and, with them, the distance between factory and market.

anchors.title: Soviet tanks crush the Hungarian revolution
anchors.summary: Budapest's councils declare neutrality and are broken in November; two hundred thousand flee and Western communist parties bleed members.

anchors.title: The United States funds its interstate highways
anchors.summary: Forty-one thousand miles of federal road are authorized; suburbs, trucking, and the drive-in economy follow the pavement.

anchors.title: The Suez crisis
anchors.summary: Britain and France seize the canal and are ordered out by Washington; the imperial era's end is invoiced.

anchors.title: Malaya becomes independent
anchors.summary: Britain leaves after a decade of jungle counterinsurgency; a multiethnic federation starts the rubber and tin route to industry.

anchors.title: Ghana leads sub-Saharan independence
anchors.summary: Nkrumah's Ghana leaves the empire first and hosts every liberation movement that follows.

anchors.title: Sputnik orbits
anchors.summary: A beeping sphere makes the sky political; the space race is on.

anchors.title: The Treaty of Rome creates a common market
anchors.summary: Six states abolish tariffs among themselves and pool farm policy; the European Economic Community begins its ratchet toward union.

anchors.title: Guinea votes no to the French community
anchors.summary: Sékou Touré chooses immediate independence; France withdraws its administrators and equipment overnight, and the rest of French Africa follows in 1960.

anchors.title: The integrated circuit is demonstrated
anchors.summary: Kilby fits a whole circuit onto one slab of semiconductor; component counts, and eventually everything downstream, begin doubling.

anchors.title: Castro's rebels take Havana
anchors.summary: Batista flies out on New Year's Day; within three years Cuba is socialist, embargoed, and hosting Soviet missiles.

anchors.title: Famine spreads under the Great Leap Forward
anchors.summary: Requisitions, falsified harvest reports, and backyard furnaces starve the countryside; tens of millions die before the campaign is abandoned.

anchors.title: The year of Africa
anchors.summary: Seventeen colonies become states in twelve months; the UN's roster and the map both redraw.

anchors.title: The Congo crisis follows independence
anchors.summary: Belgium leaves in June; the army mutinies within days, Katanga secedes, and Lumumba is deposed and murdered inside a year with foreign help.

anchors.title: OPEC is founded in Baghdad
anchors.summary: Five oil states organize against the majors that set their prices; within thirteen years the cartel can move the world economy.

anchors.title: The contraceptive pill is approved
anchors.summary: Fertility becomes a daily private decision; family size and workforces shift within a generation.

anchors.title: Police kill protesters at Sharpeville
anchors.summary: Sixty-nine people are shot at an anti-pass demonstration; South Africa bans the liberation movements, which turn to armed struggle.

anchors.title: The Sino-Soviet alliance breaks
anchors.summary: Moscow withdraws its advisers and blueprints from China; the communist world has two centers, and eventually a shooting border.

anchors.title: East Germany walls off West Berlin
anchors.summary: Overnight barbed wire becomes concrete, stopping the exodus that was draining the state; the crisis over Berlin freezes for a generation.

anchors.title: Gagarin orbits the Earth
anchors.summary: A single orbit in 108 minutes makes a Soviet pilot the first human in space and sets Washington a deadline it chooses itself.

anchors.title: The Green Revolution takes hold
anchors.summary: Dwarf wheats and new rices double harvests across Asia; famine retreats where fertilizer reaches.

anchors.title: Algeria wins independence
anchors.summary: The Evian accords end 132 years of French rule; nearly a million settlers leave within months and de Gaulle's republic keeps the oil contracts.

anchors.title: The Cuban missile crisis
anchors.summary: Thirteen days at the edge; both superpowers glimpse the end and install a hotline.

anchors.title: The Second Vatican Council opens
anchors.summary: Rome reworks the liturgy into local languages and reopens relations with other faiths; the largest church on earth modernizes by committee.

anchors.title: Carson publishes Silent Spring
anchors.summary: A study of pesticide damage becomes a bestseller; environmental regulation acquires a public constituency and the chemical industry an enemy.

anchors.title: The partial test ban treaty is signed
anchors.summary: Moscow, London, and Washington drive their tests underground; fallout in milk falls, and arms control becomes a permanent negotiation.

anchors.title: Brazil's military seizes power
anchors.summary: Generals depose Goulart with American blessing and rule for twenty-one years; the model spreads to most of South America.

anchors.title: China tests an atomic bomb
anchors.summary: A device fires at Lop Nur two days after Khrushchev's removal; the nuclear club admits an Asian member nobody can sanction into compliance.

anchors.title: The US Civil Rights Act
anchors.summary: A decade of marches and murders forces segregation out of American law, if not life.

anchors.title: Mass killings follow Indonesia's failed coup
anchors.summary: The army and allied militias kill at least half a million suspected communists; Suharto takes power and holds it for three decades.

anchors.title: Moore states his law
anchors.summary: An engineer notices transistor counts doubling on a schedule and predicts it will hold; the industry then organizes itself to make the prediction true.

anchors.title: American ground troops land in Vietnam
anchors.summary: Marines come ashore at Da Nang and the bombing of the north becomes routine; half a million Americans are committed within three years.

anchors.title: The Cultural Revolution begins
anchors.summary: Mao turns China's youth against the party; a decade of struggle sessions and purges closes the schools, smashes the temples, kills half a million or more, and persecutes tens of millions.

anchors.title: Nigeria's civil war begins over Biafra
anchors.summary: The eastern region secedes and is blockaded into starvation; a million or more die, mostly of hunger, and the federation holds.

anchors.title: Colonels seize power in Greece
anchors.summary: A junta suspends the constitution, exiles the king, and jails its critics; it falls seven years later over Cyprus.

anchors.title: Israel wins the Six-Day War
anchors.summary: Six days of fighting deliver Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank, and the Golan; the occupation that follows defines the conflict thereafter.

anchors.title: King is assassinated in Memphis
anchors.summary: A rifle shot on a motel balcony kills the civil rights movement's central figure; a hundred cities burn and fair housing passes within a week.

anchors.title: France's students and workers strike together
anchors.summary: Barricades in Paris trigger a general strike of ten million; de Gaulle survives, the cultural authority of the old order does not.

anchors.title: The Warsaw Pact invades Czechoslovakia
anchors.summary: Half a million troops end the experiment in socialism with a human face; the bloc's reformers give up on reform from within.

anchors.title: ARPANET's first message
anchors.summary: Two university computers exchange half a word; the network of networks begins.

anchors.title: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon
anchors.summary: Six hundred million watch a footprint; the program that made it is cancelled within three years.

anchors.title: The Stonewall raid provokes days of resistance
anchors.summary: Patrons of a New York bar fight back against a police raid; gay liberation acquires a movement, a date, and eventually a legal agenda.

anchors.title: The non-proliferation treaty takes effect
anchors.summary: Most states trade the bomb for reactor fuel and inspections; the five who already had it promise disarmament later.

anchors.title: Bangladesh wins independence
anchors.summary: Pakistan's army tries to crush Bengali autonomy with mass killing and rape; ten million flee to India, whose intervention makes Bangladesh a state.

anchors.title: The dollar leaves gold
anchors.summary: Nixon closes the gold window; money becomes, openly, a matter of policy.

anchors.title: Nixon goes to Beijing
anchors.summary: An anticommunist president shakes Mao's hand; the Cold War becomes triangular and China's door opens a crack before its economy does.

anchors.title: SALT I and the ABM treaty are signed
anchors.summary: The superpowers cap launchers and renounce most missile defense; mutual vulnerability is written down as policy and detente gets a text.

anchors.title: The first UN environment conference meets
anchors.summary: Stockholm puts pollution on the diplomatic agenda and creates a UN environment programme; poorer states insist development stay on it too.

anchors.title: Pinochet overthrows Allende in Chile
anchors.summary: The presidential palace is bombed on 11 September; thousands are killed or disappeared and Chile becomes the laboratory of free-market dictatorship.

anchors.title: Egypt and Syria attack across the ceasefire lines
anchors.summary: The October war shocks Israel, restores Egyptian standing, and produces both the oil embargo and the opening for a separate peace.

anchors.title: The first oil shock
anchors.summary: An embargo quadruples oil prices; the postwar boom's cheap-energy floor gives way.

anchors.title: Genes are spliced between organisms
anchors.summary: Cohen and Boyer move DNA into bacteria that then copy it; biotechnology becomes an industry and its practitioners write their own safety rules.

anchors.title: Australia drops its racial immigration bar
anchors.summary: The last of the White Australia rules are struck out; within a generation a quarter of the population is born overseas, much of it in Asia.

anchors.title: Portugal's dictatorship falls to its own army
anchors.summary: Captains sick of colonial war take Lisbon almost bloodlessly; Europe's oldest empire is liquidated within eighteen months.

anchors.title: Cyprus is partitioned after invasion
anchors.summary: A coup by the Athens junta brings Turkish troops ashore; the island splits, two hundred thousand are displaced, and the colonels fall.

anchors.title: India tests a nuclear device
anchors.summary: Delhi calls the Pokhran blast peaceful; suppliers tighten export rules and Pakistan starts building in earnest.

anchors.title: The Helsinki accords trade borders for rights
anchors.summary: The West recognizes postwar frontiers and the East signs a human rights clause; dissidents quote it back at their governments for fifteen years.

anchors.title: The Khmer Rouge empty Phnom Penh
anchors.summary: Cambodia's cities are marched into the fields; execution, starvation, and forced labor kill roughly a quarter of the population before Vietnam invades in 1979.

anchors.title: Angola and Mozambique become independent
anchors.summary: Portugal's African colonies free themselves and fall straight into Cold War civil wars that outlast the Cold War itself.

anchors.title: Papua New Guinea becomes independent
anchors.summary: Australia hands over its territory on a compressed timetable; the Pacific decolonizes by treaty and small delegations rather than by war.

anchors.title: Franco dies and Spain begins its transition
anchors.summary: The dictator dies in bed and his chosen king dismantles the regime instead of defending it; free elections follow in two years.

anchors.title: Saigon falls
anchors.summary: Helicopters lift from a rooftop; the superpower loses the war and keeps the argument.

anchors.title: Argentina's junta begins the disappearances
anchors.summary: Generals seize power and abduct, torture, and kill some thirty thousand people; the mothers of the missing outlast the regime and put it on trial.

anchors.title: Mao dies and the Gang of Four fall
anchors.summary: The chairman's death is followed within a month by arrests that end the Cultural Revolution; the succession opens the road to reform.

anchors.title: Soweto's schoolchildren rise against Afrikaans
anchors.summary: Police fire on a student march and hundreds are killed; apartheid loses its last claim to quiet and its young leave to train abroad.

anchors.title: The Apple II puts a computer in the house
anchors.summary: A finished machine with a keyboard, colour, and a spreadsheet two years later turns computing from a hobby into a household purchase.

anchors.title: The last natural smallpox case
anchors.summary: A disease that killed three hundred million in its final century is hunted to zero.

anchors.title: Deng opens China's economy
anchors.summary: Household plots and special zones begin the fastest mass enrichment in history.

anchors.title: The first child conceived in vitro is born
anchors.summary: Louise Brown's birth in Oldham separates conception from intercourse; millions of births and a permanent ethical argument follow.

anchors.title: Egypt and Israel sign a peace treaty
anchors.summary: Sinai is traded for recognition after Camp David; the Arab League expels Egypt and Sadat is murdered for it two years later.

anchors.title: The Iranian revolution
anchors.summary: The shah flies out and the ayatollah flies in; political Islam takes state power.

anchors.title: Soviet troops enter Afghanistan
anchors.summary: Moscow props up a failing client and inherits a decade-long insurgency armed by Washington, Riyadh, and Islamabad.

anchors.title: The Federal Reserve breaks inflation with rates
anchors.summary: Volcker pushes interest rates past twenty percent; prices come down, industry sheds workers, and indebted countries face default.

anchors.title: Iraq invades Iran
anchors.summary: Eight years of trench fighting, chemical weapons, and tanker attacks kill roughly a million people and change no borders at all.

anchors.title: The WHO certifies smallpox eradicated
anchors.summary: An assembly vote declares the first disease deliberately driven from the wild; routine vaccination stops and the virus stays in two freezers.

anchors.title: Solidarity wins recognition in Gdansk
anchors.summary: Shipyard strikers force a communist state to legalize an independent union; martial law follows in sixteen months, the precedent does not go away.

anchors.title: Zimbabwe becomes independent
anchors.summary: Fifteen years of white minority rule and guerrilla war end at Lancaster House; land reform is deferred and returns violently two decades later.

anchors.title: AIDS is first described
anchors.summary: Five case reports in Los Angeles announce a pandemic that will kill tens of millions before treatment arrives.

anchors.title: IBM ships the PC
anchors.summary: Big Blue standardizes the desktop computer and, inadvertently, hands the profits to its suppliers.

anchors.title: Argentina and Britain fight over the Falklands
anchors.summary: A junta invades to distract from its economy and loses in ten weeks; the generals fall and Argentine democracy returns the next year.

anchors.title: Mexico's default opens the debt crisis
anchors.summary: Dollar rates make Latin American borrowing unpayable; a decade of austerity, IMF programmes, and shrinking wages follows across the region.

anchors.title: Israel invades Lebanon and besieges Beirut
anchors.summary: The PLO is expelled to Tunis, allied militias massacre hundreds in Sabra and Shatila, and an eighteen-year occupation breeds Hezbollah.

anchors.title: The virus behind AIDS is isolated
anchors.summary: Paris and then Bethesda identify a retrovirus; a blood test arrives in two years, effective treatment only after a decade of mass death.

anchors.title: Gas escapes from the Bhopal plant
anchors.summary: Forty tons of methyl isocyanate leak over a sleeping city, killing thousands within days and maiming tens of thousands; liability is still argued.

anchors.title: Famine in Ethiopia reaches the television news
anchors.summary: Drought, civil war, and forced resettlement kill hundreds of thousands; a filmed report launches the modern celebrity relief campaign.

anchors.title: Brazil returns to civilian government
anchors.summary: Twenty-one years of military rule end without a shot; the region's largest state joins a democratic wave that runs from Buenos Aires to Santiago.

anchors.title: Gorbachev takes over and starts reforming
anchors.summary: A younger general secretary tries openness and restructuring to save the Soviet system; within six years both the reforms and the system are gone.

anchors.title: The Antarctic ozone hole is reported
anchors.summary: British researchers publish a seasonal collapse in stratospheric ozone; the culprit is a class of useful industrial chemicals.

anchors.title: PCR makes DNA copy itself on demand
anchors.summary: Thermal cycling multiplies any chosen fragment a billionfold; forensics, diagnostics, and sequencing all become routine laboratory work.

anchors.title: Chernobyl
anchors.summary: Reactor four burns openly for days; the fallout reaches Sweden before the admission does.

anchors.title: People Power removes Marcos
anchors.summary: Crowds and defecting soldiers fill Manila's avenues and a twenty-year dictatorship flies to Hawaii; the template travels to Seoul and Rangoon.

anchors.title: The first intifada begins
anchors.summary: Stones, strikes, and boycotts across the occupied territories put Palestinians back at the centre of their own question and force talks by 1991.

anchors.title: The INF treaty abolishes a class of missiles
anchors.summary: Reagan and Gorbachev agree to destroy their intermediate-range weapons with on-site inspection; Europe's hair-trigger is dismantled for thirty years.

anchors.title: South Korea wins direct presidential elections
anchors.summary: June protests by students and office workers force the generals to concede a vote; an industrial success story becomes a democracy.

anchors.title: The Montreal protocol phases out CFCs
anchors.summary: Every state eventually signs, industry substitutes, and the ozone layer begins recovering; environmental diplomacy gets its one clean success.

anchors.title: Chile votes Pinochet out
anchors.summary: A referendum the dictatorship expected to win goes against it by twelve points; the general leaves the presidency and keeps the army.

anchors.title: Global warming reaches legislatures
anchors.summary: A NASA scientist tells the US Senate the warming signal is detectable, and governments found the IPCC to assess it; the negotiating era begins.

anchors.title: The Berlin Wall opens
anchors.summary: A botched press conference ends the German partition; the bloc dissolves within two years.

anchors.title: Romania's revolution ends with executions
anchors.summary: The one bloody exit from the Eastern bloc kills over a thousand people and puts Ceausescu in front of a firing squad on Christmas Day.

anchors.title: The Soviet army leaves Afghanistan
anchors.summary: The last column crosses the Amu Darya after nine years and fifteen thousand Soviet dead; the client state falls in 1992 and the militias turn on each other.

anchors.title: The army clears Tiananmen Square
anchors.summary: Weeks of protest end with troops and tanks killing hundreds or more in Beijing; the party keeps power and buys consent with growth.

anchors.title: Germany reunifies
anchors.summary: East Germany accedes to the west's constitution and currency eleven months after the wall opened; the price is paid in transfers for a generation.

anchors.title: Mandela walks out of prison
anchors.summary: Twenty-seven years inside end on television; the bans are lifted and four years of negotiation replace the prospect of civil war.

anchors.title: Namibia becomes independent
anchors.summary: The last colonial territory in Africa leaves South African control under UN supervision, closing the continent's formal decolonization.

anchors.title: A coalition drives Iraq out of Kuwait
anchors.summary: Six weeks of bombing and a hundred hours of ground war restore the emirate; American forces stay in the Gulf and become a grievance.

anchors.title: India opens its economy
anchors.summary: A payments crisis forces devaluation, licence reform, and foreign investment; growth accelerates and a middle class of hundreds of millions forms.

anchors.title: The Soviet Union dissolves
anchors.summary: The flag comes down on Christmas night; fifteen states inherit the rubble and the warheads.

anchors.title: The World Wide Web goes public
anchors.summary: A CERN side project gives the internet an address book and a face; publishing becomes a verb anyone can do.

anchors.title: Yugoslavia breaks apart in war
anchors.summary: Slovenia and Croatia secede and the federation dissolves into a decade of sieges, expulsions, and roughly a hundred and forty thousand deaths.

anchors.title: The Maastricht treaty founds the EU
anchors.summary: A common market votes itself a union, a citizenship, and, on a schedule, a currency.

anchors.title: Australia's high court recognizes native title
anchors.summary: The Mabo judgment finds the continent was never legally empty; indigenous land claims enter the property system by statute the next year.

anchors.title: The Rio summit signs the climate convention
anchors.summary: Over a hundred and fifty states agree to stabilize greenhouse gases and protect biodiversity, without numbers or deadlines attached.

anchors.title: Israel and the PLO recognize each other
anchors.summary: A handshake on the White House lawn sets up limited Palestinian self-rule and defers every hard question; Rabin is murdered for it in 1995.

anchors.title: South Africa votes across race lines
anchors.summary: Apartheid ends at the ballot box; Mandela is inaugurated by the state that jailed him.

anchors.title: NAFTA joins three North American economies
anchors.summary: Tariffs fall between Canada, the United States, and Mexico; factories move south, and Zapatista rebels rise in Chiapas on the day it starts.

anchors.title: The genocide in Rwanda
anchors.summary: In a hundred days organized militias and neighbours murder some eight hundred thousand Tutsi and moderate Hutu while UN troops are withdrawn.

anchors.title: Srebrenica's men and boys are murdered
anchors.summary: Bosnian Serb forces overrun a UN safe area and kill more than eight thousand; NATO finally bombs and Dayton ends the war in December.

anchors.title: The World Trade Organization opens
anchors.summary: GATT becomes an institution with binding dispute settlement; tariffs keep falling and supply chains lengthen accordingly.

anchors.title: A sheep is cloned from an adult cell
anchors.summary: Dolly proves a differentiated nucleus can be reset; cloning bans, stem cell research, and a long bioethics argument follow within a year.

anchors.title: The Asian financial crisis breaks
anchors.summary: Thailand's baht falls and capital flees the region; IMF programmes deepen the slump, and Asian states start hoarding dollar reserves.

anchors.title: A computer beats the world chess champion
