anchors.summary: Deep Blue defeats Kasparov over six games by brute-force search; machine superiority arrives first in the game chosen to represent intellect.

anchors.title: Hong Kong returns to China
anchors.summary: Britain leaves at midnight and Beijing promises fifty years of separate systems; the promise is renegotiated by force within twenty-three.

anchors.title: Kyoto sets binding emission targets
anchors.summary: Industrial countries accept numbered cuts and invent carbon trading; the United States never ratifies and the developing world takes no targets.

anchors.title: The Good Friday Agreement settles Northern Ireland
anchors.summary: Thirty years of killing end in power sharing, prisoner releases, and an open border that Brexit will later put back in question.

anchors.title: Google indexes the web by ranking links
anchors.summary: Treating citations as votes makes search useful at web scale; attention becomes an auctioned commodity and the advertising business relocates.

anchors.title: India and Pakistan test warheads openly
anchors.summary: Five Indian tests in May are answered by six Pakistani ones within a fortnight; South Asia's rivalry becomes nuclear and its crises shorter.

anchors.title: Mobile phones reach the mass market
anchors.summary: The phone leaves the wall and the desk; presence and reachability quietly renegotiate.

anchors.title: The Second Congo War draws in nine states
anchors.summary: Armies and militias fight over the Congo's minerals and its refugees; millions die, mostly of hunger and disease, in Africa's deadliest war.

anchors.title: Suharto resigns as Indonesia's economy collapses
anchors.summary: Riots and a currency in freefall end thirty-two years of rule; the fourth most populous country builds a democracy and decentralizes it.

anchors.title: East Timor votes to leave Indonesia
anchors.summary: Seventy-eight percent choose independence; militias burn the territory in reprisal until an Australian-led force lands, and statehood follows in 2002.

anchors.title: The euro is launched
anchors.summary: Eleven states surrender their currencies to one central bank while keeping their own budgets; the design flaw surfaces ten years later.

anchors.title: The human genome is drafted
anchors.summary: Three billion letters read once, expensively, then ever more cheaply, forever.

anchors.title: The United States invades Afghanistan
anchors.summary: Air power and local militias remove the Taliban in weeks; twenty years of occupation and state-building end with their return.

anchors.title: China joins the World Trade Organization
anchors.summary: Tariff certainty pulls the world's factories to the coast; hundreds of millions leave farming and Western manufacturing towns hollow out.

anchors.title: Hijacked airliners destroy the World Trade Center
anchors.summary: Nearly three thousand people are killed in one morning; two wars, a surveillance apparatus, and permanent airport ritual follow.

anchors.title: The African Union replaces the OAU
anchors.summary: The continent's states swap non-interference for a charter allowing intervention against coups and atrocities, and a peacekeeping habit.

anchors.title: Mass killing begins in Darfur
anchors.summary: Government forces and militia burn villages across western Sudan, killing some two hundred thousand people and displacing millions.

anchors.title: The United States and Britain invade Iraq
anchors.summary: Baghdad falls in three weeks, the weapons cited are never found, and disbanding the state produces years of insurgency and sectarian killing.

anchors.title: Latin America's left wins the commodity boom
anchors.summary: Lula's inauguration marks a run of left governments funding cash transfers with Chinese demand for ore, oil, and soy.

anchors.title: SARS escapes southern China
anchors.summary: A new coronavirus reaches thirty countries and kills nearly eight hundred people; quarantine, reporting rules, and pandemic plans are rebuilt.

anchors.title: Ten states join the European Union
anchors.summary: Most of the former Eastern bloc enters the single market at once; workers move west and the union's decisions get harder to reach.

anchors.title: The Indian Ocean tsunami
anchors.summary: A magnitude nine rupture off Sumatra kills about two hundred and thirty thousand people in fourteen countries; a warning system is built afterwards.

anchors.title: Two rovers land on Mars
anchors.summary: Spirit and Opportunity find rock chemistry left by ancient water; one drives for fourteen years on a ninety-day warranty.

anchors.title: Social networks reach general use
anchors.summary: Facebook opens to campuses and then to everyone; personal life becomes a published feed and politics acquires a new distribution system.

anchors.title: Katrina floods New Orleans
anchors.summary: Failed levees drown most of a city and kill some eighteen hundred people; American capacity and its racial geography are both exposed.

anchors.title: The iPhone merges phone and computer
anchors.summary: A pocket touchscreen with an application store puts the internet in every hand; attention, cameras, and maps are permanently rearranged.

anchors.title: Genome sequencing costs collapse
anchors.summary: Massively parallel machines cut the price of a human genome from millions to thousands within a few years; population-scale genetics becomes routine.

anchors.title: The global financial crisis
anchors.summary: Lehman's failure freezes credit worldwide; states rescue banks, output falls, and a decade of austerity and populist politics follows.

anchors.title: The Arab uprisings topple four governments
anchors.summary: A Tunisian vendor's suicide sets off protests that unseat rulers in Tunis, Cairo, Tripoli, and Sanaa; only Tunisia comes out with an elected government.

anchors.title: A tsunami wrecks the Fukushima reactors
anchors.summary: Flooded generators cause three meltdowns and a mass evacuation; Japan idles its reactors and Germany votes to abandon nuclear power.

anchors.title: South Sudan becomes independent
anchors.summary: Africa's newest state secedes with the oil after decades of civil war, and collapses into its own civil war within thirty months.

anchors.title: Syria's uprising becomes a long war
anchors.summary: The government answers protest with artillery and the country fractures; over half a million die and half the population is driven from home.

anchors.title: CRISPR is turned into a gene-editing tool
anchors.summary: A bacterial immune system is reprogrammed to cut any chosen DNA sequence; editing becomes cheap enough for any laboratory, and for crops and patients.

anchors.title: Neural networks win the image contest
anchors.summary: A deep network trained on graphics cards nearly halves the error rate in image recognition; the field abandons hand-built features within two years.

anchors.title: China launches the Belt and Road
anchors.summary: State banks lend for ports, rail, and power across Asia, Africa, and Europe; infrastructure arrives with debt and Chinese standards attached.

anchors.title: Migrant drownings make the Mediterranean a border
anchors.summary: A shipwreck off Lampedusa kills three hundred and sixty-eight people; naval rescue, then deterrence, becomes standing European policy.

anchors.title: Snowden discloses mass surveillance
anchors.summary: Leaked documents show intelligence agencies collecting global communications wholesale; encryption spreads by default across the consumer internet.

anchors.title: Russia annexes Crimea
anchors.summary: Unmarked troops take the peninsula after Ukraine's revolution; borders in Europe are changed by force for the first time since 1945 and sanctions begin.

anchors.title: Ebola spreads across West Africa
anchors.summary: The first urban epidemic of the virus kills over eleven thousand people in three countries; the WHO is reformed and a vaccine is finally licensed.

anchors.title: Islamic State declares a caliphate
anchors.summary: Insurgents take Mosul and much of eastern Syria, enslave and massacre Yazidis, and are ground down by 2019 after a coalition air campaign.

anchors.title: A million asylum seekers reach Europe
anchors.summary: Syrians, Afghans, and Iraqis walk the Balkan route as Germany suspends the rules; border fences return and nationalist parties gain everywhere.

anchors.title: The Paris agreement replaces targets with pledges
anchors.summary: Every state promises its own emission plan against a shared limit near two degrees; ratcheting reviews substitute for enforcement.

anchors.title: An orbital rocket's booster lands intact
anchors.summary: A first stage returns upright after delivering satellites; reflown boosters cut launch prices within a few years and traffic to orbit multiplies.

anchors.title: A program beats a champion at Go
anchors.summary: AlphaGo wins four of five games in Seoul using learned intuition rather than exhaustive search; reinforcement learning acquires a public reputation.

anchors.title: Britain votes to leave the European Union
anchors.summary: A narrow referendum reverses forty years of integration; the union loses a member and gains proof that membership is revocable.

anchors.title: Myanmar's army expels the Rohingya
anchors.summary: Villages are burned and thousands killed in Rakhine; some seven hundred thousand Rohingya flee to Bangladesh and a genocide case reaches the world court.

anchors.title: The transformer architecture is published
anchors.summary: Attention replaces recurrence and language models begin scaling with data and compute; the whole later wave of general-purpose models descends from this design.

anchors.title: Venezuela's economy collapses
anchors.summary: Hyperinflation, food shortages, and rule by decree drive millions abroad in South America's largest displacement, while the oil state keeps power.

anchors.title: COVID-19 becomes a pandemic
anchors.summary: A new coronavirus spreads worldwide; reported deaths pass seven million, excess deaths far more, and states shut borders, schools, and workplaces.

anchors.title: mRNA vaccines are authorized within the year
anchors.summary: Vaccines designed from a published sequence in days are cleared by December; billions of doses follow and a new platform is proven in public.

anchors.title: Solar becomes the cheapest new electricity
anchors.summary: Auction prices make new solar the cheapest source of power in most markets; deployment then outruns every forecast the agencies had published.

anchors.title: Protein structures are predicted from sequence
anchors.summary: A learned model reaches experimental accuracy on protein folding and releases structures for nearly every known protein, changing where structural biology begins.

anchors.title: The Taliban retake Kabul
anchors.summary: The Afghan republic collapses in ten days as foreign troops withdraw; twenty years of state-building end with the government it began by removing.

anchors.title: The James Webb telescope launches
anchors.summary: A folded infrared observatory unfolds a million miles out and starts returning images of the earliest galaxies within seven months.

anchors.title: A chatbot puts language models in public hands
anchors.summary: A conversational interface reaches a hundred million users in two months; text generation becomes an everyday tool and an industrial arms race.

anchors.title: Russia invades Ukraine
anchors.summary: The largest European war since 1945 begins; Ukraine holds, Europe rearms and reroutes its gas, and NATO gains two Nordic members.

anchors.title: Lula returns and Brasilia is stormed
anchors.summary: A week after the handover, supporters of the defeated president ransack the capital's institutions; the courts hold and Amazon clearing falls by half.

anchors.title: War in Gaza follows the October attacks
anchors.summary: Hamas-led fighters kill about twelve hundred people in Israel and seize hostages; Israel's campaign kills tens of thousands in Gaza and displaces most of it.

anchors.title: India passes China in population
anchors.summary: UN estimates put India first at about 1.43 billion; China's population begins shrinking and the demographic advantage moves south and west.

anchors.title: Coups detach the Sahel from France
anchors.summary: Soldiers take power in Niger after Mali and Burkina Faso; French garrisons leave, the juntas form their own alliance, and Russian contractors arrive.

anchors.title: Australia offers Tuvaluans refuge from the sea
anchors.summary: A treaty grants residency to Tuvaluans as their atolls flood, the first migration pact written for a state expecting to become uninhabitable.

anchors.title: Half the world's voters go to the polls
anchors.summary: Elections in more than seventy countries cost incumbents ground almost everywhere, from India's ruling party to South Africa's, without settling much.

anchors.title: 2024 is the warmest year on record
anchors.summary: The first calendar year averaging more than 1.5 degrees above preindustrial levels; the long-term limit is not breached yet, but the margin is gone.
